AcceptFrom.description: Which kinds of approval count toward a rule.

AcceptLegalDocumentRequest.description: Accept the legal document and version the address names — the version you were shown.

moment.description: Where you were asked: when you first used Gitmoap, or at any later ask.

AccessAuditChange.description: One change to who can do what, as the audit record keeps it.

oneOf.description: The role after the change. Absent for a revoked grant.
The role before the change. Absent for a new grant.

sensitive.description: Whether either role carries a sensitive or reserved permission.

AccessAuditDetail.description:
The access changes one request made — carried on its audit record, because the operation and
route alone say *that* access changed and not *what* it changed from and to.

oneOf.description: An account closed: every grant it held ended, and what went and what stayed, by path.
A scope's inheritance switched.
A limit set or removed.

A custom role's permissions changing — which changes access wherever the role is granted,
without any grant changing.

AccessBasisView.description: Where an explained principal's access comes from.

AccessCatalogue.description: The permission catalogue and the built-in roles made of it.

roles.description: The five built-in roles, lowest first.

AccessDelta.description: One person's access changing at one group or repository.

gains.description: Permissions they would hold that they do not hold now, by key.

losses.description: Permissions they hold now that they would no longer hold, by key.

AccessEntry.description: One grant that reaches the group or repository the access page is about.

last_exercised_at.description: When the grant last let somebody do something, to the day. Absent until it has.

limited_to.description:
The limits that take away part of what this grant gives here: set on this group or
repository or one above it, naming the grant's holder, a team the person is on, or everyone
— or every service account, for one. An organization owner is never limited, so their
entries carry none.

AccessExplanation.description: Why a principal has the access they have on a group or repository.

oneOf.description:
Present when the scope is a fork of private code and the principal cannot read the code of
every repository it is bound to: the binding left them only `scope.view` and `scope.delete`
here, whatever their grants say.
The nearest group or repository that stops access granted above it, if one does.

grants.description: Every grant that bears on them here, and what became of it.

limits.description: Every limit that capped them here.

oneOf.description: Present when the request named one permission.

Who made the grant. Absent for access the platform created — the creator of a group or
repository, or a copied membership.

last_exercised_at.description: When the grant last let somebody do something, to the day. Absent until it has.

AccessGrantChange.description: What changing a grant did — or, with `dry_run=true`, what it would do.

oneOf.description: The grant as it stands after the change. For a preview, as it would stand.

AccessInheritanceChange.description: The switch flipped — or, with `dry_run`, what flipping it would do.

at.description:
Where the limit is set. It caps its subject there and everywhere beneath, including beneath a
group or repository that does not inherit access.

oneOf.description: The most the subject may hold. Absent when the limit allows nothing at all.

AccessLimitChange.description: A limit set — or, with `dry_run`, what setting it would do.

AccessPageScope.description: A group or repository as its access page describes it.

inherits_access.description:
Whether access granted on the groups above reaches it. When it is `false`, only access
granted here — and the organization's owners — reach it.

AccessPreview.description: What a change to access would do, computed without writing anything.

changes.description: Each person whose access would change at the group or repository the change is made on.

truncated.description: Whether `changes` stops short of everyone affected. The summary still counts them all.

scopes_affected.description:
The group or repository the change is made on, plus every one beneath it that inherits
access and so changes with it.

AccessReviewItem.description: One grant in the access review, and why it is there.

covered_by.description:
For a redundant grant: the grants that already give everything it does, so the reviewer can
see why revoking it takes nothing away.

AccessReviewPage.description:
The access review: every grant in the organization with a reason to look at it, oldest first.

A page can hold fewer items than asked for while more remain — the review reads a bounded
stretch of the organization's grants per request — so keep reading while `next_token` is
present.

AccessReviewReason.description: Why a grant is in the access review.

AccessScope.description: A group or repository, as the access API names one.

AccessSource.description: Where an entry on the access page was granted.

AccessSourceFilter.description: Which grants the access page lists by where they were made.

AccessSourceKind.description: Where an entry on the access page comes from.

AccessSubjectClass.description: A class of principals a limit can cap at once.

AccessTokenOAuth.description: The connected app behind a token.

AccessTokenView.description:
An access token, without its secret: who it belongs to, its scopes, what it is limited to, and
when it expires and was last used.

oneOf.description:
Present when an app connected through sign-in minted this token. Revoking it disconnects
the app.

AccountClosure.description: What closing your account does — or, after the closure, did.

blockers.description: What must happen before the account can be closed. Closing is refused while any is listed.

delete.description:
Your personal namespace, when nobody else is in it: deleted, with everything in it. No other
group is ever deleted by closing an account — one only you are in blocks the closure.

dry_run.description: Whether this only says what closing would do (`dry_run=true`) and changed nothing.

fresh_sign_in.description: Whether you signed in recently enough to close the account now.

keep.description:
Top-level groups other people are in: they stay, without you, and what you wrote there stays
under `username_after`.

oneOf.description:
After the closure: whether the account's record was deleted, or kept under
`username_after` because something you wrote stays. Absent on a dry run.

username_after.description:
The username your account takes where something you wrote stays — merge requests, issues
and comments in places other people work. Your address is replaced with one that reaches
nobody.

warnings.description: What closing loses that is worth knowing first. None of them stops it.

oneOf.description: Who did it. Absent when the platform did — a pipeline nobody triggered, a scheduled action.

metadata.description: Bounded free-form detail; the shape varies by `kind` and is documented per event.

occurred_at.description: When it happened. A feed is ordered by this.

ActivityScope.description: The group or repository something happened in, with its current full path.

ActivitySubject.description: What the event was about, where it has one. A push, a release and a pipeline run do not.

iid.description: The subject's number, as it is now — a work item that has moved since shows its new number.

title.description:
The subject's title: its current title while it exists, the title it had at the time once it
has been deleted. Absent when neither is known.

oneOf.description: The subject's permanent identifier, for a work item.

ActorEgressUsageView.description: Your own budget for data downloaded from gitmoap, for the current hour and day.

actor_key.description:
Which budget this is: `USER#{id}` for a user, `SA#{id}` for a service account, `PRT#{id}`
for a pipeline run. Lets a caller holding several credentials tell them apart.

day.description: The current day's budget, which limits sustained downloading.

hour.description: The current hour's budget, which limits bursts.

ActorSummary.description:
Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each.

avatar_url.description:
The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.

email.description:
The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.

id.description:
The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.

oneOf.description:
What the actor is — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — and so
which page it links to. Absent on a placeholder (a redacted or deleted actor) and on an
actor that is not a principal, such as the platform's own `system` actor; a client draws
such an actor unlinked.

username.description:
The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.

AddAssigneeRequest.description:
Assigns a user or a service account to the work item, so a pipeline or an agent can own it
too.

target.description: The work item at the other end. It may live in another group or repository.

AddReviewerRequest.description:
Who to ask for a review. Only the id: the platform resolves the person's name and email itself,
and refuses one who cannot read the merge request.

AgentCodeTrust.description:
Whether a pipeline run of code an agent wrote gets the repository's connections, secrets,
cloud roles and build cache. `trusted`, the default, runs it like a person's code; `untrusted`
runs it without them until a person approves its commit.

AgentConfig.description:
One agent the revision names. Its key, handle, position and squad are **structural**; its
profile is **pinned**; its work-in-progress limit is **ordered** (lower is stricter).

oneOf.description: Overrides the position's tier for this agent.
How the agent speaks and what it cares about, in at most 4,000 characters.
When the agent works; absent, it works at any hour.

AiAgent.description: An agent: its account, position, squad and state, and what the live revision says about it.

avatar_url.description:
Its picture, `{avatar base}/agents/{agent_id}`, where the deployment stores pictures.
Nothing is served there until someone uploads one, and a client then draws the agent glyph.

created_by.description: The person on whose behalf the platform hired it.

oneOf.description: The session it is running now, if any.

email.description: The no-reply address its commits are authored as.

oneOf.description: Its position, from the live revision; absent once retired.

root_group_id.description: The top-level group whose organization it works in.

oneOf.description: Its squad, from the live revision; absent once retired.

AiAgentOrganization.description: The organization an agent works in: its top-level group, by id, path and name.

full_path.description: Its path, which addresses its pages.

name.description: The name it shows: its display name, else its path name.

AiAgentProfile.description:
An agent's public identity — who it is and where it works — the way a person has a public
profile. Anyone who can see its organization reads it, so it carries nothing of the agent's
sessions, spend, suspension, creator or configuration: those stay in the organization's own
view of its agents.

agent_id.description: The agent's id, which addresses its page.

avatar_url.description:
Its picture, `{avatar base}/agents/{agent_id}`, where the deployment stores pictures.
Nothing is served there until someone uploads one, and a client then draws the agent glyph.

handle.description:
Its handle, which always ends in `-ai` — unique within its organization, so it names the
agent only beside the organization.

oneOf.description: Its position, from the organization's live revision; absent once retired.

state.description: Whether it is working, finishing what it holds before stopping, or retired.

AiBlockedOn.description: What stops an agent that asked a person.

AiCarriedWorkspace.description:
Which of an ended session's workspace objects the platform copied into the session continuing
it, for its workspace to start from: the newer of its last checkpoint and its last out-bundle.

AiDigest.description: A digest a ritual wrote: what happened in a period, from the facts the platform gathered.

cost_micros.description: What writing it cost, in millionths of a dollar with the fee included.

oneOf.description: What it was written from, each record by address.
The squad it is about; absent for the whole organization.

AiFactActor.description:
Who did what a ritual's facts name — a person, a service account or an agent — so that a
stand-up never reads a person's work as an agent's.

kind.description: What they are: `user` for a person, `service_account` or `agent`.

name.description: Their `@username`, or an agent's `@handle`.

AiFactAgent.description: One agent's own record over a ritual's period: what it did and what is on its plate. The platform states it in the run's thread for the agent, so a stand-up's account of the past is never a model's to write.

assigned.title: Refunds: alert on the third retry

assigned.description: The work items assigned to it and not done when the period ended, at most 10.

closed.description: The work items it closed, at most 10.

merged.description: The merge requests it wrote that were merged, at most 10.

opened.description: The merge requests it opened that are not merged, at most 10.

reviewed.description: The merge requests it reviewed, at most 10.

sessions.description: Its sessions that ended in the period, at most 10.

waiting.description: Its gates still waiting for a person, at most 5.

AiFactGate.description: A gate still waiting when a ritual's facts were gathered.

action.description: The action waiting, in one line.

AiFactPreviousRun.description: How the same ritual's previous run for the same squad ended.

digest.description: The digest it wrote, cut at 500 characters.

AiFactRecord.description: A merge request or a work item a ritual's facts name, by address.

oneOf.description: Who wrote it: a merge request's author. Absent on a work item.
Who merged it, or who closed it.

title.description: Its title when the facts were gathered, cut at 200 characters.

AiFactReview.description: A merge request an agent reviewed in a ritual's period, and what it decided.

verdict.description: What the review decided: `approved` or `rejected` — changes requested.

AiFactSession.description: A session a ritual's facts name.

about.description: The address of what it worked on.

summary.description: The agent's own account, cut at 300 characters.

AiGate.description: An action an agent waits on a person to decide — or one already decided.

oneOf.description: The agent whose action it is.

approvers.description:
The people who may decide it besides the board. Empty means the organization's board, as it
is when the gate is decided. A `ritual_outcome` gate whose ritual names no approvers lists
the board as it was when the gate was raised. A member of the board may decide any gate.

body.description:
The exact text the decision is about, for the gates that carry one: what an
`external_message` write would publish, the title and description a `create_work_item` gate
would create, and the digest of a `ritual_outcome` gate's outcome.

consumed_at.description: When the approved action was taken.

decide_by.description: When it expires if nobody decides it.

oneOf.description: Who decided it.

decision_note.description: What the person who decided it wrote for the agent.

kind.description: Which gate of the catalogue it is.

oneOf.description: The ritual run whose outcome waits on it.

root_group_id.description: The organization's top-level group, which the app's links name.

oneOf.description: The session waiting on it; absent for a ritual's outcome.

subject.description: The exact action waiting — what a decision applies to and nothing else.

AiGateDecision.description: A person's decision on a gate.

AiGateId.description: A gate's id: an agent's action — or a ritual's outcome — waiting for a person's decision.

AiGateKind.description: A kind of action an organization's autonomy decides whether an agent may take without asking.

AiGateState.description:
Where a gate stands: waiting for a decision, approved or denied, spent by the action it
approved, lapsed undecided, withdrawn with its session, or — for a gate set to notify — a record
that the agent went ahead and people were told.

AiGateSubject.description:
The exact action a gate waits on, as it is stored and served. `action` says which, and decides
the other fields. Every action also carries `summary`, one line for the person deciding, and
`address`, what it is about, when it has one. A list longer than 50 is cut to 50 and ends with a
line saying how many more there were.

oneOf.description: Merging a merge request at its source head into its target at the target's head.

merge_request_iid.description: The merge request's number in the repository.

source_sha.description: The source head the approval is for.

summary.description: One line for the person deciding.

target_sha.description: The target's head the approval is for.

oneOf.description: Opening a merge request from a branch at its head.

summary.description: One line for the person deciding.

oneOf.description: Creating a work item with this content in this scope; the content is the gate's `body`.

body_digest.description: The SHA-256 of the title and description, which the approval binds.

scope_id.description: The repository or group it would be filed in.

summary.description: One line for the person deciding.

oneOf.description: Marking a work item done.

summary.description: One line for the person deciding.

summary.description: One line for the person deciding.

oneOf.description: Starting a pipeline that deploys to these environments.

summary.description: One line for the person deciding.

oneOf.description: Moving a branch to a change touching privileged paths.

paths.description: The privileged paths the change touches.

summary.description: One line for the person deciding.

to.description: What it moves to: a pushed tip, or a web commit's tree.

oneOf.description: Moving a branch to a change adding third-party dependencies.

summary.description: One line for the person deciding.

to.description: What it moves to: a pushed tip, or a web commit's tree.

oneOf.description: A write people outside the organization read; the text it publishes is the gate's `body`.

body_digest.description: The SHA-256 of what it would publish, which the approval binds.

path.description: The request's path.

summary.description: One line for the person deciding.

oneOf.description: A session spending past its alert into the next multiple of it.

step.description: Which multiple of the alert it reached.

summary.description: One line for the person deciding.

oneOf.description: Applying a ritual run's outcome.

outcome_digest.description: The SHA-256 of the outcome, which the approval binds.

AiMemoryPage.description: One memory page, as it reads now or at a revision.

- Run `make test` before pushing.
- The payments service owns `src/billing/`.

agent_handle.description: The agent's handle, for an agent's page.

body.description: The page, in Markdown; empty for a page nobody has written.

history.description:
The page's kept versions, newest first — each one readable with `?revision=`. Older ones
are no longer kept.

revision.description: Its version, counted from 1; 0 for a page nobody has written.

squad_key.description: The squad's key, for a squad's page.

oneOf.description: Who wrote this version — a person or the agent.

AiMemoryPageKind.description: Which page: an agent's own, a squad's, or the organization's conventions.

AiMemoryPins.description:
The versions of the memory pages a session pinned when it started — what its agent was told,
whatever the pages say now. A page absent here was empty, or not the agent's to read.

AiMemoryRevision.description: One kept version of a memory page, without its text.

oneOf.description: Who wrote it — a person or the agent — while they still exist.

AiModel.description: A model an organization can use, with the prices that apply to it.

announced_prices.description: Prices published to take effect later.

oneOf.description: The price in effect now.

tier_default.description:
Whether this is the model its tier routes to in its region. Every other model is used only
when a revision or a persona draft names it.

AiModelConnection.description: An organization's own account with a model provider, as an Owner reads it. Never the key.

condition_until.description: Until when a `limited` connection waits, or when a refused one is next tried.

connected_at.description: When the current key was activated.

consent_lapses_at.description:
When the connection stops being usable because the person who consented is no longer an
Owner; absent while they are one.

consented_by.description: The Owner whose connecting was the consent.

key_label.description: The label the provider holds the key under, so an Owner can find it there.

routing_region.description: Where the provider routes the organization's calls.

state.description: Whether the provider accepts its calls.

unservable_models.description: Catalogue models the routing could not serve, held back until they are tried again.

zero_data_retention.description: Whether only endpoints that keep nothing may serve the organization's calls.

AiModelConnectionId.description: A model connection's id: an organization's own account with a model provider, which its agents' calls run on once connected.

AiModelPrice.description: A model's list price in one region, per million tokens, in millionths of a dollar.

AiModelTier.description:
A model tier: the most capable, the standard, or the economical model in the organization's
region.

AiOrg.description: An AI organization: its state, live revision, pause epoch, consent and today's spend.

oneOf.description:
Who accepted that the organization's content goes to the model provider, and when. No
model call is made without it.

group_id.description: The root group the organization is attached to.

live_revision.description: The number of the revision in force, absent until the first publish.

readable_squads.description:
The squads whose private sections you can read — their memory, channels and ritual
outcomes — by key. A squad not named here answers those reads `404`.

reads_board.description:
Whether you read what the board keeps: the organization's own channel and its rituals'
outcomes.

spend_today_micros.description: Usage and fees charged so far today (UTC), in micro-dollars.

AiOrgOrigin.description: How an organization came to be: the setup wizard, or joining what already exists.

AiOrgRevision.description: One version of an organization's configuration. A published version never changes.

body_digest.description: Hex SHA-256 of the canonical body; two revisions with one digest are one configuration.

note.description: What a proposed revision changes and why, as the agent that proposed it wrote.

parent_number.description: The revision this one was edited from.

AiOrgRevisionSummary.description:
One revision of an organization's configuration, without the configuration itself — what the
organization's history lists. Read a revision by its number for the whole configuration, or
export it as YAML.

author_kind.description: Who wrote it: a person, an agent proposing it, or the platform.

body_digest.description:
Hex SHA-256 of the canonical configuration; two revisions with one digest are one
configuration.

created_by.description: Who wrote it; for the draft, who saved it last.

note.description:
What a proposed revision changes and why, as the agent that proposed it wrote, in at most
2,000 characters.

number.description:
Its number in the organization, which reads it whole. The draft keeps its number when it
is published.

org_id.description: The organization it is a revision of.

parent_number.description:
The revision it was edited from: the one live when it was last written. Absent when none
was.

published_at.description: When it was published, once it is.

oneOf.description: Who published it, once it is published.

state.description:
Where it stands: the one `draft`, a revision an agent `proposed`, `published` — the live
one — `superseded` by a later publish, or a `declined` proposal.

updated_at.description: When it last changed: each save of the draft, and its publishing, superseding or declining.

AiOrgUsage.description: What an AI organization spent in a period and where.

cache_hit_rate.description: The share of input tokens read from the prompt cache, 0 to 1.

cost_per_merged_change_micros.description: The period's spend over its merged changes.

merged_changes.description: The agents' merge requests merged in the period.

month_forecast_micros.description: This month's spend at the rate so far, projected to the month's end.

month_spent_micros.description: What the organization has spent this calendar month.

monthly_cap_micros.description: The organization's monthly budget, from its live revision.

provider_paid_micros.description:
Of what was charged in the period, the usage the organization's own provider account paid
for — calls on its model connection, whose fee alone the balance paid.

sessions.description: How many sessions started in the period.

total_micros.description: What the sessions started in the period cost, in millionths of a dollar with the fee.

AiOutcomeAssignment.description: A work item a ritual's outcome assigns to an agent.

AiOutcomeCycleChange.description: A work item a ritual's outcome puts into, or takes out of, the next cycle.

AiOutcomeDecision.description: A decision a ritual's outcome records on the organization's conventions page.

AiOutcomeProposal.description: A revision a ritual's outcome proposes, for the board to publish or decline.

body.description: The whole configuration proposed, as a revision's body.

AiOutcomeQuestion.description: A question a ritual's outcome asks people, in the run's thread.

to.description: The people asked, by username; none means the board.

AiProfileDraft.description:

person who asked.

sources.description: The files the persona drew on.

oneOf.description: What the drafted agent does, in one line, once it is written.
The position the persona is written for, once it is written.

AiProfileDraftFailure.description: Why a draft was not written.

AiProfileDraftId.description: A persona draft: a persona a small model wrote from a person's brief

AiQuestion.description: A question an agent asked, as the session's page shows it.

examples.question: Should the retry back off exponentially or at a fixed interval?

oneOf.description: Who answered it.

asked.description: The people asked; empty means the board.

escalate_at.description:
When it goes to the board if nobody asked has answered — while it is open and has not gone
yet.

give_up_at.description: When the session waiting on it ends, unanswered.

posted_at.description: Where the agent posted the question.

AiQuestionState.description: Whether an agent's question is still open.

AiRegion.description:
Where an organization's model calls are served, and so where its content is processed. Fixed
when the organization is created.

AiReviewQueue.description:
The agents' open merge requests, the oldest first — each shown only to a caller who can read
its repository.

items.description: The merge requests.

agent.description: The agent that opened it, by handle.

cost_micros.description: What its work has cost so far.

AiRevisionDiff.description:
What publishing a revision would change: each change with its class and when it takes effect,
and a sentence a person reads first.

live_revision.description: The live revision compared against; absent before the first publish.

AiRitualCalendar.description:
The organization's rituals as a calendar: every occurrence the live revision schedules from now
to `through`, earliest first, one per squad for a ritual of every squad. Nothing is written by
reading it.

oneOf.description: The iteration cadence the cycle rituals follow, when the revision names one.

time_zone.description: The time zone the rituals' times are kept in.

truncated.description: Whether more occurrences fell in the window than one answer holds.

AiRitualFacts.description:
What a ritual read before it wrote: what happened in its squad — or the organization — over its
period, each record by address, so every line of a digest or an outcome opens its evidence.
Gathered from rows when the ritual ran, and kept as they were then.

agents.description: Each agent of the run's scope, with its own record over the period.

closed.description: The work items closed, at most 30, each with who closed it.

merged.description: The merge requests merged, at most 30, each with its author and who merged it.

opened.description: The merge requests opened and not merged, at most 30, each with its author.

period_from.description:
When the period the facts cover began: the same ritual's last completed run for the same
squad, or a day before this one was due.

period_to.description: When it ended: when this run was due.

oneOf.description: How the same ritual's previous run for the same squad ended.

sessions.description:
The agents' sessions that ended, at most 30 — never a ritual's own, so a run is not
something that happened for the next one.

spend_micros.description: What those sessions spent, in millionths of a dollar with the fee included.

waiting.description: The gates still waiting, at most 20.

AiRitualOccurrence.description: One coming occurrence of a ritual, for one squad or for the organization.

kind.description: What kind of ritual it is.

anchor_count.description:
How many anchors the rows add up to: every anchor in the repository whose work item you can
see.

rows.description: One entry per file, the files with the most open work pinned to them first.

AnchorDebtRow.description:
One file in a repository's technical-debt map: how much open work is pinned to it, and who owns
it.

owners.description:
Who the repository's CODEOWNERS file says owns this file. Absent when there is no
CODEOWNERS file, or it names nobody for this path.

AnchorDriftAction.description: What happens when an anchored region of code changes beyond recognition.

scope_id.description: The id of the group or repository the work item lives in.

scope_type.description:
Whether the work item lives in a group or a repository. With `scope_id` and `iid` it is the
item's current address — which need not be the repository the anchor is in: an item that
moves keeps its anchors where the code is.

AnchorKind.description:
What kind of thing the anchor is pinned to. The kind decides what deleting the code means: a
person judges what deleting code pinned to a bug means, but deleting the `// TODO(#412)` that is
the work item's reason to exist can close it.

oneOf.description: A line range a human pinned. The default.

allOf.description: A named symbol, pinned as a region, with the symbol's name recorded.

oneOf.description: A named symbol, pinned as a region, with the symbol's name recorded.

allOf.description:
A `TODO`/`FIXME` comment carrying a work item reference. Created by the platform when it
finds one in the code, never by a person.

oneOf.description:
A `TODO`/`FIXME` comment carrying a work item reference. Created by the platform when it
finds one in the code, never by a person.
The whole file. It follows only renames and deletions of the file; it never drifts.

AnchorState.description: Where the anchored region stands now, as the platform last worked it out.

oneOf.description:
The work item's number, type, title and status. Absent briefly after the work item is
deleted, until its anchors are removed.

AnchorView.description:
An anchor with enough of its work item attached to show it beside the code, such as
`#412 Bug: retry loop double-charges` beside lines 88–104.

ApiSpecKind.description: Which interface-description format a spec is written in.

ApiSpecRef.description: Where this service's interface description lives.

ApplyBlueprintRequest.description: Apply a blueprint to an existing work item — an additive set-difference by `facet_key`.

blueprint.description: The custom type to apply: one defined on the work item's repository or on a group above it.

ApprovalExclusion.description: Why a recorded approval does not count toward a rule.

ApprovalPolicy.description: A group's or repository's approval policy.

ApprovalPolicyView.description: The approval policy and rules in force at a group or repository.

effective.description: The switches that apply here: the nearest policy, tightened by every enforced one above it.

oneOf.description: This group's or repository's own policy, when it sets one.

rules.description:
The rules that apply to merge requests here: every enforced rule above, as strengthened
beneath, then the nearest group's or repository's own rules.

rules_here.description: The rules this group or repository defines itself.

oneOf.description: The branches whose merge requests this rule applies to; absent means every branch.

defined_at.description: The group or repository that defines it.

oneOf.description:
The enforced rule above this one that it strengthens, in whose place it applies here and
beneath.

ApprovalRuleStanding.description: One approval rule, as the merge check found it.

approvals.description: Every recorded approval, with whether it counts toward this rule.

ApprovalStanding.description: One recorded approval, and whether it counts toward a rule.

oneOf.description: Why it does not count, when it does not.

ApprovalSwitches.description: Who may not approve, whatever the rules say — and whether approvals survive a push.

author_can_approve.description: Whether a merge request's author may approve it.

committers_can_approve.description: Whether someone who authored or committed a commit in it may approve it.

last_pusher_can_approve.description: Whether whoever pushed its current head may approve it.

reset_on_push.description: Whether an approval stops counting when new commits are pushed.

approved_value.description: Value to apply; defaults to the request's `requested_value`. Clamped to the ceiling.

ApproveNodeDecision.description:
Your decision on a step waiting for approval: `grant` counts towards letting it run, `deny`
stops it.

ApproveNodeRequest.description: Records your decision on a step that is waiting for approval.

comment.description:
An optional note from the approver. Shown with the decision, and on a denial it is also shown
on the step, so why a deploy did not happen is visible where the run is.

ApproveNodeResponse.description: Confirms the approval decision was accepted. It is applied a moment later, not during this request — poll the run to see the step move.

approvals_received.description: Distinct approvals given so far, this one included.

approvals_required.description: Distinct approvals the gate needs before the step starts.

oneOf.description: Limits the access to one group or repository.

scopes.description: The scopes or bundles to grant: some or all of those the app asked for.

ApprovePipelineRunRequest.description:
Approves the commit an untrusted run built, starting a trusted run of it that has access to the
pipeline's secrets.

commit_sha.description:
The commit you reviewed and are approving. It must be the commit the run built; if the
run built a different one, nothing runs and you are told which.

ApproverRef.description:
Who may satisfy an approval rule or open a deployment gate.

Every reference is resolved when the approval is evaluated. A team or person that no longer
exists resolves to nobody.

oneOf.description: Anyone who may approve merge requests in the repository.

anyone.description: Anyone who may approve merge requests in the repository.

oneOf.description: One person or service account.
The team's members at the time of the check.

team.description: The team's members at the time of the check.

oneOf.description: Anyone whose role at a group or repository is at least `min`.

role.description: Anyone whose role at a group or repository is at least `min`.

direct_only.description:
Count only access given on `at` itself — directly or through a team — and not access
that reaches it from a group above.

oneOf.description: The owners of the files the merge request changes.

code_owners.description: The owners of the files the merge request changes.

AssetDownloadResponse.description: A short-lived download URL, returned instead of a redirect when the request asks for it. Navigate to the URL directly.

url.description: A presigned URL to download the file from. It expires shortly.

AssetState.description:
Whether a release file has been uploaded: `uploading` (an upload URL was issued, but the upload
has not been confirmed yet) or `available`.

AssetUploadResponse.description: A registered release file, and the URL to upload it to.

upload_url.description:
A presigned URL to upload the file to with an HTTP `PUT`. It accepts only a file of the
declared size, and expires shortly.

content_type.description:
The type it is served as: its own for an image that renders in place,
`application/octet-stream` for anything else.

filename.description: Its name as it was uploaded.

inline.description: Whether it renders in place — an image — rather than downloading.

markdown.description: The markdown that embeds it: an image for one that renders in place, a link otherwise.

AttachmentFilename.description: An attachment's file name: 1 to 255 characters, with no path separator or control character, and not only dots.

AttachmentId.description: The identifier of an attachment: a file uploaded into a repository or group, linked from markdown as `/-/attachments/{id}`.

AttachmentLimits.description: The limits an upload is held to.

inline_types.description: The types that render in place.

max_bytes.description: The most one attachment may be, in bytes.

AttachmentUpload.description:
An attachment started: the row, where to send its bytes, and the limits they are held to.
Finish it once the upload succeeds.

limits.description: The limits the upload is held to.

upload.description: Where and how to send its bytes.

AttachmentUploadTarget.description: Where and how to send the bytes.

headers.description: The headers the request must carry, exactly.

url.description: The signed URL to send the bytes to, once.

AttentionCounts.description: The badge — how many items are pending, and how they break down.

by_reason.description: Reasons with at least one pending item, keyed by the wire name.

pending.description: A **capped** count. When `truncated`, this is the cap and the client renders "99+".

AttentionItem.description: One inbox item, as the API returns it.

oneOf.description: Who caused the item, as they are now. Absent when nobody did, such as for a bookmark.

note.description: Your own note, on a bookmark only.
