On a notification's item: what the notification is about — its kind and the ids it names
(a ritual run, a gate, a session, a channel message, the organization), never its title.
It says which run an item whose `target` is the organization's group means.

AttentionReason.description: Why an item is in front of you.

AttentionState.description: Where an item is in its life.

AttentionTargetKind.description: What kind of thing an attention item points at.

AttentionTargetRef.description: The thing an attention item points at. `kind` says which, and decides the other fields.

oneOf.description:
A group — what an item about access on a group points at, and an item about an AI
organization as a whole: its organization's top-level group.
A gate an AI organization raised, waiting for a person's decision.
An AI agent's session.

A message in an organization's channel. The channel is named because it decides who may
read the message.

channel_id.description: The channel the message is in.

AttestCheckRequest.description: A human's answer for a check no machine can see.

evidence_url.description:
Where the evidence is — the runbook, the drill's write-up, the ticket — an `https` link of
at most 2048 characters, served as the result's `detail.evidence_url`.

state.description: `passing` or `failing` — the only two states a person can attest.

AttestResult.description:
The result of checking a community or private provider's images, by capability. The images stay
in your registry; nothing is copied or signed.

AttestedCapability.description:
One capability's image of a community or private provider, as confirmed: its reference in your
registry, used as it is, and its content digest, which must match the digest you attested.

AttestedState.description: The states an attestation may assert.

AuditActor.description: Who performed the action. `username` and `avatar_url` are recorded as they were at the time.

email.description:
Always empty on a record written now: an actor's address is not recorded, so a record kept
for good keeps no person's address past their account's closure. A record written before
keeps the address it was sealed with.

id.description:
The id of the user, service account, agent or pipeline run that acted, the SCIM token's id,
or `anonymous` — whichever `actor_type` says.

AuditActorType.description:
What kind of caller acted — and so what `AuditActor.id` names and where a client links it.

Each spelling is exactly the string every earlier record stored, which is what keeps a record's
hash the same whichever type decoded it: the chain hashes the record as serialized.

AuditCategory.description: What kind of operation the record captures.

AuditOutcome.description: The result of the audited operation.

AuditRecord.description:
One audit record. Records are hash-chained and append-only: never updated or deleted, so any
tampering shows when the chain is verified.

oneOf.description:
For an operation that changed who can do what: each grant it made, changed or revoked, with
the role before and after. Absent everywhere else — and absent fields do not enter the hash,
so every record written before this field existed verifies unchanged.

For a request an AI agent made through the MCP server: the tool and the client. Absent
everywhere else, and so outside the hash of every record that does not carry it.

month.description:
The month the record belongs to, `YYYY-MM`. Each month's records form one segment of the
chain.

prev_hash.description:
Hash of the previous record in the chain (genesis = 64 zeros; first of a
month links to the prior month's tip).

recorded_at.description: When the record was written to the log, RFC 3339 with microseconds.

scope.description: Which audit chain the record belongs to — an organisation, a user, or the platform.

AuthorizationServerMetadata.description: How a client finds this authorization server and what it supports.

AutoSyncPause.description: `diverged`: the fork branch has commits the upstream lacks. `refused`: the fork's push rules refused the move. `actor_lost_access`: the person auto-sync runs as can no longer read the upstream, or is gone. `upstream_narrower`: the upstream became less visible than the fork. `privileged_paths`: the upstream's new commits change a pipeline file, the catalog declaration or a CODEOWNERS file, which only a person's sync may bring in.

AutoTransition.description:
Where an automation moves a work item when its event happens: nowhere (`disabled`), back to
where it was (`restore`), or into a status category (`{"to": "in_progress"}`).

oneOf.description:
The event moves nothing. Unlike leaving the setting unset, this overrides a parent group that
turns the automation on.

Put the work item back in the category it held before the merge request opened. Only
`on_mr_closed` acts on it; for the other automations it means the same as `disabled`.

AutonomyConfig.description:
`autonomy` — the level chosen at setup and each gate's setting. Settings and the large-change
threshold are **ordered**: *ask* is stricter than *notify*, which is stricter than *allow*.
Approvers and the expiry are **pinned**.

approvers.description: Who decides each gate; a gate not named here is decided by the board.

gate_expiry_hours.description: How long a gate waits for a person before it expires and the agent is told.

large_change.description: The size above which a change raises `large_change`.

AutonomyLevel.description:
How much an organization may do without asking: a named preset for every gate, each of which
can still be set on its own.

content_length.description:
Exact byte size of the upload. Bound into the presigned PUT, so the upload
must send exactly this many bytes; rejected up front if over the avatar cap.

BalanceTransaction.description: A change to a prepaid balance: a top-up, refund, chargeback, commitment or adjustment.

balance_micros.description: The balance after this change, in micro-dollars.

BarrierMode.description: When a stage is allowed to start. `strict` waits for every step in every earlier stage to finish, so a failure anywhere stops what follows. `lenient` waits only for the steps a given step actually depends on, so an unrelated branch failing does not block it. `strict` is the default.

BlastRadiusFailure.description: One sampled pipeline that would stop validating.

BlobContent.description:
One file at one commit.

`blob_sha`, `commit_sha` and `mode` are what an editor needs to write the file back: the blob it
started from (a later commit names it to say *change this, if it is still this*), the commit the
read resolved to, and the mode to keep.

blob_sha.description:
The file's git object id — what a commit that edits this file sends back as
`expected_blob_sha`.

commit_sha.description: The commit the requested ref resolved to.

lossy.description:
`true` when the file is text but not valid UTF-8, and `content` shows replacement characters
where its bytes could not be decoded. Writing such content back would change the file.

mode.description: The file's mode at that commit. A symbolic link's content is its target, not a file's text.

Blueprint.description:
A reusable custom work-item type, defined on a group or a repository. Deleting that group or
repository deletes its blueprints.

examples.description: A change to the public API, shipped with its documentation and its dashboards.

facets.hint: Link the updated API reference page.
facets.label: Documentation

examples.name: API Feature

archived.description: Hidden from the type picker; items already filed keep their `type_profile`.

base_type.description:
The built-in type the custom type is based on, which decides where its items may live, their
children and their fields. "API Feature" might be a `story` with a blueprint on top.

blueprint_id.description: The blueprint's slug, unique within its group or repository. It never changes.

created_by.description: Who created the blueprint, as they were when they created it.

name.description: The custom type's display name, such as "API Feature".

version.description:
The blueprint's revision, incremented on every change. An update must send the version it
read, and is refused with a `409` if the blueprint changed since.

BlueprintRef.description:
The custom type a work item was filed as: the blueprint, and the group or repository where it is
defined — not necessarily the item's own. Moving the item does not change it, and an edit to the
blueprint shows on the item the next time it is read.

inherited.description: `true` when the blueprint is defined on an ancestor group rather than on the queried scope.

BlueprintView.description:
A blueprint in a scope's available-types set, tagged with whether it was **inherited** from an
ancestor group or defined on the scope itself. The type picker renders this.

BoundForkRef.description: A fork of private code, bound to this repository: only people who can read this repository can read it, so it is deleted with this repository and stays in its organization.

depth.description:
How far it is from the repository its network started from: `1` for a fork of that
repository, `2` for a fork of a fork.

full_path.description: The fork's path, which names the group that holds it.

BranchMergeRequestRef.description: An open merge request a branch is the source of.

iid.description: The merge request's number in its repository.

target_branch.description: Where it proposes to merge the branch.

Breakdown.description: Whether a namespace rollup also splits per repository.

BrowseProvidersResponse.description: A page of marketplace providers. Pass `next_token` back to get the next page.

Budgets.description:
What the organization may spend, in millionths of a dollar with the fee included. A budget
left out is not capped; the monthly budget is required.

agent_daily_cap_micros.description: What one agent may spend in a UTC day.

org_monthly_cap_micros.description: All model usage and fees of the organization per calendar month in UTC. Required.

session_alert_micros.description: What a session may spend before continuing needs the `session_spend` gate; $25 when absent.

BuiltinRoleInfo.description: One built-in role and everything it holds.

name.description: The role's display name, such as `Developer`.

permissions.description: Every permission the role holds, by key.

BurndownDay.description: One day of an iteration's burndown, as things stood at the end of it (UTC).

added_points.description:
The points of the work items that joined the iteration that day. On its first day, only
those that joined that day, not the work it started with.

completed_items.description: How many of them were done.

removed_points.description: The points of the work items that left it that day — moved, taken out or rolled over.

scope_items.description: How many work items were in the iteration and not cancelled.

CadenceId.description: The identifier of an iteration cadence — the schedule that generates a group's iterations.

CadenceTitle.description: A cadence's title, such as Sprint: 1 to 120 characters, with no control characters. Each iteration it generates is titled with it and the iteration's number.

CadenceVelocity.description:
A cadence's velocity: what each of its most recent closed iterations took on, finished and
carried over, read from each iteration's rollup as it is now.

average_completed_points.description: The mean of their completed points, rounded down. 0 when none has closed.

iterations.description: Its closed iterations, earliest first — at most `count` of them, the most recent.

CalendarConfig.description:
`calendar` — the organization's time zone, in which rituals run and working hours are read, and
the iteration cadence whose schedule gives its cycles. **Pinned.**

oneOf.description:
The iteration cadence, in the organization's top-level group, whose schedule gives its
cycles: each cycle is one of its iterations and the cool-down after it. A ritual held at a
point of a cycle, or one that selects a cycle's work, needs one. Publishing refuses a cadence
that is not the top-level group's, and the cadence cannot be deleted while a live revision
follows it.

CalendarDate.description: A calendar day, `YYYY-MM-DD`, with no time and no zone — a due date, or the day an iteration starts or ends.

oneOf.description: An optional reason for cancelling, shown on the run and kept in its audit trail.

CancelPipelineRunResponse.description:
Confirms the cancellation was accepted. Steps stop a moment later; poll the run to see them
end.

event_id.description: An identifier for this request, useful for correlating it with the run's later activity.

CapabilityDescriptor.description:
One capability a provider version offers: what it does, the container image that runs it, its
inputs and outputs, and the configuration it accepts.

bindable.description:
Config keys that can take their value from an earlier step. Each has an optional `value`
input port of the same name: connect it and read it with `{"$from": "<key>"}`, or leave it
unconnected and write the value yourself.

config_schema.description: The JSON Schema a step's `config` must satisfy to use this capability.

image_digest.description:
The exact build of the capability's container image, when the catalog records one. Pinned so
a run cannot pick up a different build behind the same tag.

image_uri.description: The container image that runs the capability, with an immutable version tag.

input_groups.description: Rules about which inputs are alternatives to each other. Empty for most capabilities.

source_image_ref.description:
For a verified provider, the image's location in its publisher's registry before gitmoap
copied it. Absent for providers gitmoap builds itself.

CapabilityDetailResponse.description: One capability, with the provider version it was read from.

CapabilityMirror.description:
Where one capability's image of a verified provider was copied to: its location in gitmoap's
registry, its content digest, and a reference to its signature.

CardLabel.description: A label on a card: its key and the colour its group or repository defines for it.

CardMilestone.description: A milestone, as a card renders it.

CardReviewer.description: A reviewer chip on a card: the avatar cluster + per-reviewer approval state.

kind.description: Whether the reviewer is a person, a service account or an agent.

stale.description:
Whether this reviewer's approval predates the current source-branch tip
(approved an older revision). Computed at read time; always present.

Category.description:
A marketplace discovery category a provider is listed under. A provider declares one to three,
and they describe where it appears when browsing, not what its capabilities do — a provider in
`infrastructure` may still offer build and deploy capabilities.

CategoryCount.description: One marketplace category, and how many providers are listed under it.

CeilingRef.description:
The most a limit lets its subject hold: `{ "builtin": "reporter" }`, `{ "custom": "<id>" }`, or
`{ "none": {} }` for nothing at all.

ChainVerification.description: The outcome of verifying a chain over a month range.

ChallengeResponse.description: `200` body for a requested challenge — the token + where to place it.

ChangeClass.description: When a change to one field of a revision reaches the organization.

Channel.description: A channel, as the caller sees it.

archived_at.description: When it was archived. An archived channel keeps every message readable and takes no new one.

can_wake.description:
On one of an AI organization's channels or a direct conversation with one of its agents:
whether a message you write there wakes its agents — `true` when you manage the
organization or are on its allow-list — or waits until they next read the channel. Absent
on a channel no agent is woken from.

oneOf.description: Who created it; absent on a channel the platform derived from an AI organization.
A direct conversation's agent.
A direct conversation's person.

disclosure.description: On a direct conversation: who else reads it, as opening it said.

group_path.description: That group's path. With the name it makes the channel's address, `acme/platform/~platform-team`.

kind.description: A named channel, or a direct conversation.

last_seq.description: The number of its newest root message; 0 before the first.

name.description: Its name, unique among the group's channels. A direct conversation is named after its agent.

oneOf.description: The AI organization a derived channel or a direct conversation belongs to.

squad_key.description: The squad a squad's channel belongs to.

topic.description: What it is for, in its members' words.

unread_count.description: How many root messages you have not marked read.

updated_at.description: When its name, topic or state last changed.

ChannelKind.description: Whether a channel is a named channel or a direct conversation.

oneOf.description: Who added them; absent for the two ends of a direct conversation.

member.description: The member: a person, a service account or one of the organization's AI agents.

examples.body: acme/api!87 is green and waiting for review.

oneOf.description: The AI label, on an agent's message.
Who wrote it, when a principal did; `author.kind` is `agent` for an AI agent.

author_kind.description: Whether a principal or the platform wrote it.

chain_depth.description: How many agents' messages led to it.

deleted_at.description: When it was deleted. A deleted message keeps its place, its author and its time.

oneOf.description: Who deleted it.

last_reply_at.description: On a root message: when the last reply arrived.

reply_count.description: On a root message: how many replies its thread holds.

revision.description: 1 when posted, one more for each edit.

seq.description: A root message's number in its channel; absent on a reply.

oneOf.description: A reply's thread: the root message's id.

trust.description: Whether what it says may wake an agent.

ChannelMessageBody.description: A message's text, 1 to 8,000 characters (4,000 for an AI agent). Mention a person or an agent with `@username` or `@handle`.

ChannelMessageRevision.description: One text a message had before it was edited.

oneOf.description: Who replaced it with the next text.

revision.description: Which text it was: 1 for the one the message was posted with.

ChannelName.description: A channel's name: 1 to 80 lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter or digit, and not shaped like an id. Unique among a group's channels.

ChannelReadMark.description: How far you have read a channel.

last_read_seq.description: The number of the newest root message you have seen.

unread_count.description: How many root messages are newer.

ChannelTopic.description: What a channel is for, at most 500 characters. An empty topic clears it.

CheckKindCatalog.description: The platform's built-in checks, for a client offering a choice of checks.

CheckKindDescriptor.description:
One of the platform's built-in checks, described for a client offering a choice of checks: its
key, what it means, which facts it needs and the parameters it takes.

config_schema.description: A JSON Schema over the fields — render a form from this.

description.description: What the check means, and the one thing to do about a failure.

invalidated_by.description: The kinds of activity that can change this check's answer, causing it to be re-evaluated.

requires.description: The facts this check needs. A service with none of them is `not_applicable`.

sweeps.description:
Whether this check is re-evaluated periodically as well as on activity — true for checks
whose answer can change with time alone.

CheckPipelineFileRequest.description:
Pipeline text to check, without committing it: one file that is a namespace of its own, or every
file of a namespace.

files.description:
Every file of one namespace — one directory under `.gitmoap/pipelines/` — each at most
256 KiB. Send this or `text`. Files under `.gitmoap/components/` may be sent beside either:
the components they hold are read in place of the default branch's.

oneOf.description: Which form `text` is; the pipeline language when absent.

text.description:
One file's contents, at most 256 KiB: a namespace of its own declaring the pipeline. Send
this or `files`.

CheckPipelineFileResponse.description: What checking a pipeline file's text found.

diagnostics.message: `memroy` is not an attribute of a step — did you mean `memory`?

oneOf.description: The pipeline the text defines, its names bound. Absent when it does not read or bind.

diagnostics.description: Every problem the text has and everything worth saying about it, in file order.

valid.description: Whether the text has no error: committed, it would apply.

CheckRule.description: How a check decides its answer.

oneOf.description:
Computed by the platform from what it already knows — deployments, releases, repository
settings. The check's `key` names one of the platform's built-in checks.

Proved by the evidence your pipeline runs report, using the same `@`-expression binding a
work item's acceptance criteria use. Its `key` is your own name for the check and may not
reuse a built-in check's key.

Declared by a person, for statements no system can measure, such as "we rehearsed the
failover". An attestation expires after `renew_after_days` and must then be renewed.

CheckState.description:
What a check currently says about a service, listed worst first. `failing`: the check does not
hold. `stale`: the evidence that used to prove it no longer does. `expired`: an attestation whose
renewal window has passed. `unknown`: never evaluated. `passing`: the check holds.
`not_applicable`: the check does not apply to this service, so it does not count against it.

CheckStateCounts.description: How many checks are in each state. All six states are always present.

seats.description:
Seat count for a per-seat tier (e.g. Team). When set, Checkout starts at
this quantity and lets the customer adjust it; omit (or `1`) for a flat
per-namespace tier. Entitlement keys on the product, never the quantity.

ClaimSsoDomainRequest.description: An email domain to claim for the organization's SSO.

ClientConfigDocument.description:
The settings the Gitmoap command-line tools read to reach Gitmoap.

Served unauthenticated at `/.well-known/gitmoap-client-config`. Every field
is public by construction: these are the values a client needs *before* it
can authenticate, so none of them can be a secret.

The `gitmoap` CLI and `git-remote-gitmoap` carry only the host this document
is served from and read everything else here, so the API URL, the git
endpoint and the sign-in settings can change without a new client release.

api_url.description: Base URL of the REST API, no trailing slash.

cli_client_id.description: The OAuth client id the CLI signs in as.

cognito_domain.description: The domain of the hosted sign-in page the login flow authorizes against, without a scheme.

cognito_region.description: The AWS region of the sign-in service.

download_base.description:
Where the client binaries are published, no trailing slash.

Absent when none are.

git_endpoint.description:
WebSocket endpoint for git transport (`wss://…`), used by
`git-remote-gitmoap`.

ClockTime.description: A time of day on a 24-hour clock, `HH:MM`, read in the organization's time zone.

oneOf.description:
A `Done`- or `Cancelled`-category status. Defaults to the set's default done
status.

ClosedRecord.description: What happened to the account's record.

ClosureAuditChange.description:
What closing an account did, as its audit record keeps it: whether the account's record went, and
which top-level groups were deleted and which were kept.

deleted.description: The top-level groups deleted with it, by address.

kept.description: The top-level groups it left, which stay, by address.

record_deleted.description: Whether its record was deleted, or kept under a generated username.

ClosureBlocker.description: Something that must happen before your account can be closed.

examples.action: Make someone else an Owner of Acme, or delete it
examples.name: Acme

action.description: What clears it, in a sentence.

name.description: The group's display name, else its name.

ClosureDeletedNamespace.description: A top-level group closing your account deletes.

name.description: The group's display name, else its name.

name_held.description: Its name, held back from everybody after it is deleted, and until when.

personal.description: Whether it is your personal namespace.

repositories.description: The repositories it holds, every one deleted with it.

ClosureKeptNamespace.description: A top-level group that stays when your account closes, without you.

name.description: The group's display name, else its name.

personal.description:
Whether it is your personal namespace — kept because somebody else works in it. Its address
keeps your username unless you rename it first.

ClosureWarning.description: Something closing your account loses that is worth knowing first.

balance_micros.description: The prepaid balance lost, in millionths of the currency unit.

CodeSearchAlert.description: One alert, with a sentence a person can read.

examples.message: 2 repositories you can read are not indexed yet.

message.description: The same, in a sentence. It never quotes the query.

CodeSearchAlertCode.description: Something the search did not do completely.

CodeSearchChunk.description: A window of context around one or more matches.

cut_lines.description: The lines cut to a window.

lines.description: The lines, without their line endings.

start_line.description: The first line shown, numbered from 1.

CodeSearchCutLine.description: A line longer than 500 characters, cut to a window around its matches.

line.description: The line, numbered from 1 in the file.

offset.description:
Where the window starts in the full line, in UTF-16 code units; a range's offsets are
relative to the window.

CodeSearchErrorCode.description: Why a build failed — a typed reason, never git's own text.

CodeSearchExcludedRepository.description: A repository left out of the index.

full_path.description: Its path, read at the time of the request.

CodeSearchFacets.description: Matched files counted by repository and by language.

languages.description: At most 30 languages, most files first.

other_languages.description: Files matched in the languages past those listed.

other_repositories.description: Files matched in the repositories past those listed.

repositories.description: At most 50 repositories, most files first.

blob_oid.description: The file's blob, when its content is indexed.

chunks.description: Context windows around the matches, at most `chunks_per_file`.

commit_sha.description: The commit the file was indexed at: with `path`, an immutable link to these lines.

language.description: The file's language, when it has one.

match_count.description: Matches in the file, as far as the search verified it.

more_chunks.description: The file holds more matches than its chunks show.

path.description: The file's path in the repository.

path_ranges.description: Where the query matched the path.

repository_id.description: The repository, a key of the response's `repositories`.

CodeSearchFilesSkipped.description: Files a build left out, by why.

binary.description: Files with a NUL byte in their first 8 KiB.

vendored.description: Vendored files: their paths are searchable, their content is not.
Vendored, by `.gitattributes` or its path; only its path is searchable.

CodeSearchLastError.description: The last error a build hit.

code.description: A typed reason, never git's text.

CodeSearchLineRange.description: One match within one line of a chunk.

line.description: The line, numbered from 1 in the file.

start.description: Where the match starts in the line, in UTF-16 code units.

CodeSearchOrganizationUsage.description: The organization's indexed bytes against its plan's cap.

cap_bytes.description: The plan's cap, with any increase granted.

indexed_bytes.description: Indexed source bytes across the organization.

CodeSearchQueryEcho.description: The query, as the server understood it.

normalized.description: The query in its canonical form: two spellings of one query normalize to one string.

repository_id.description: The repository, a key of the response's `repositories`.

CodeSearchRepositoryRef.description:
What a client needs to name and link a repository a result or a facet names, read from the
database at response time.

indexed_sha.description: The commit its results come from.

stale.description: The default branch has moved past `indexed_sha` and a build is due.

CodeSearchResponse.description:
A page of a code search: the matching files in rank order, the repositories they come from,
and what the search counted.

alerts.description: What the search did not do completely.

oneOf.description: Matched files by repository and by language, when asked for.

next_token.description: The next page, when there is one.

query.description: The query, as the server understood it.

repositories.description: Every repository a result or a facet names, by id, in ascending order.

results.description: The files that matched, in rank order.

changed_at.description: When the switch last moved; absent while it never has.

enabled.description: Whether the organization's code is indexed and searchable.

CodeSearchSpan.description: A span of a path or a line, in UTF-16 code units.

CodeSearchStateCounts.description: Repositories of a subtree, counted by where their index stands.

stale.description: Indexed, with a newer commit waiting.

files_matched.description: Files that matched, as far as the evaluation reached.

files_matched_exact.description:
`files_matched` is exact; when false, a work budget stopped the evaluation and the count is
a lower bound.

repositories_not_indexed.description: Readable repositories the index does not hold — pending, failed or over the cap.

repositories_searched.description: Readable repositories the index holds, all of them searched.

repositories_stale.description: Readable repositories whose default branch has moved past their index.

CodeSearchStatusState.description:
A repository's state as its status read reports it: the index row's, or `disabled` and
`not_indexed`, which have no row.

CodeSearchToken.description:
One token of the query as the server understood it: where it is and what kind it is, never its
text.

field.description:
A filter's field, its alias resolved: `repo`, `group`, `path`, `lang`, `case`, `type`,
`test`, `generated` or `vendored`.

kind.description: What kind of token it is.

negated.description: The token is negated with a leading `-`.

span.description: `[start, end)`, in UTF-16 code units of the query as sent.

CodeSearchTokenKind.description: What kind of token of the query a span covers, for a search box to highlight.

CodeTodo.description:
A `TODO` or `FIXME` comment found in a repository's code, and whether it has been turned into a
work item.

author.description: The author of the commit that added the TODO — the work item's creator if it is promoted.

content_digest.description:
The TODO's identifier: a SHA-256 digest of its keyword and text, without the `(@owner)` or
`(#id)` part or the comment syntax. It holds no path or line number, so moving the comment
keeps the same TODO.

first_seen_sha.description: The commit (push head) that first added this marker.

oneOf.description:
The number of the work item this TODO was promoted into, in the same repository. Absent
until it is promoted. `gitmoap todo sync` writes it back into the comment as `(#id)`.

owner.description:
The `@username` an author wrote in the marker (without the `@`), a suggested assignee on
promotion. Absent when the marker named no owner.

path.description: Where the TODO was last seen. It changes as the comment moves; `content_digest` does not.

region_digest.description:
A digest of the TODO's source line as a code region — what the anchor created on promotion
starts with as its `content_digest`. Unlike `content_digest`, it includes any `(#id)`.

text.description: The TODO's text, normalised, at most 255 characters.

CodeTodoState.description:
Which TODOs to list. A promoted TODO stays listed until its comment carries the work item's
`(#id)`, so `promoted` and `promoted_unstamped` return the same TODOs.

allOf.description:
What is being discussed: a merge request (`repository_id` and `merge_request_id`) or a work
item (`scope` and `issue_uid`).

author_can_push.description:
Whether the author can push to where the discussed merge request or work item lives —
false for a drive-by contributor's text. Absent where it was not computed.

reactions.description: The reactions on the comment, one entry per emoji. `me` says whether you placed it.

examples.body: This retries on every 5xx, not only on gateway timeouts. Should a 502 from the fraud check be retried too?
Reproduced with a 12,500 EUR refund in staging: the fraud check answers after 41 seconds.

CommentLineSide.description: Which side of a diff a line is on: the old file, or the new one.

CommentReactionSummary.description: The reactions on one comment, one entry per emoji.

root.description: The comment that starts the thread, general or inline.

examples.message:
Retry card authorizations on gateway timeouts

A timed-out authorization is retried once, with the same idempotency key.
examples.title: Retry card authorizations on gateway timeouts

CommitAuthor.description: Who a commit written in the browser names as its author and committer: the caller.

CommitAuthors.description: One commit's author and committer, each the principal its address belongs to.

oneOf.description:
The principal the commit's author address belongs to — a person anywhere, or a service
account or agent of the repository's organization. Absent when the address is nobody's, or
more than one principal's. Git does not authenticate an author: this says whose address the
commit names, not who made it.
The principal the commit's committer address belongs to, on the same terms as `author`.

CommitAuthorsResponse.description:
Who wrote each of a page of commits: its author and committer resolved to the platform's
people, service accounts and AI organization's agents. Kept apart from the commit itself, which
is addressed by its sha and cached for a year: who an address belongs to can change, so it is
read fresh, one request for a whole page.

items.description:
One entry per requested commit the repository holds, in the order asked. A sha it holds no
commit for — a force-push may have dropped it — is left out.

CommitLinkAction.description: What a commit did to the work item it referenced.

CommitPreview.description: What a commit would do, without doing it — `?dry_run=true`.

allowed.description: Whether the commit, sent as it is, would land.

branch_exists.description: Whether `branch` exists. With `start_branch`, `false` means it will be created.

oneOf.description: The head the commit would land on; absent for a repository's first commit.

pipelines.description: The pipelines this commit would start, as the branch's push triggers stand now.

refusals.description: Every reason the commit would be refused, each on the field it is about.

stale.description: The files that changed since the caller read them.

CommitSummary.description: A commit in brief, as a file browser shows it: who, what and when.

author_avatar_url.description: The author's avatar, when this instance serves avatars.

oneOf.description:
The author's email as recorded in the commit. Absent when the commit records something that
is not an email address; the commit still has its name and message, only no avatar.

author_name.description: The author's name as recorded in the commit — a git identity, not a gitmoap account.

authored_at.description: When the change was written, ISO 8601.

committed_at.description:
When the commit was created, ISO 8601. Later than `authored_at` after a rebase or a
cherry-pick; this is the time a "last updated" column should show.

short_sha.description: The abbreviated SHA, as git chose to abbreviate it in this repository.

CommunicationConfig.description:
`communication` — how agents talk: how long a question waits, and how much an agent may say. Its
limits are **ordered** (lower is stricter).

agent_messages_per_channel_hour.description: The most messages one agent posts in one org channel in an hour.

question_timeout_hours.description:
How long a question to a person waits before it escalates to the board — the people who can
answer what the people asked did not; a product owner is an agent, and answers no question
put to a person.

CommunityAcceptance.description:
Whether an organization's pipelines may run Community-tier providers. `disabled` (the default)
refuses them; `any` admits any Community provider in the catalog; `verified_only` admits only
those whose publisher namespace is verified.

CompareOp.description: How a measurement is compared against its threshold.

CompareResponse.description:
Comparison between two branches: the divergence (ahead/behind), a bounded
preview of the commits `head` adds over `base`, and the three-dot file diff.

ahead.description: Commits on head not on base.

base_sha.description: Tip commit of the base (target) branch.

behind.description: Commits on base not on head.

commits.description: Bounded, newest-first preview of the commits head adds over base.

commits_truncated.description: `true` when there are more commits than the preview cap returned.

diff.description:
Three-dot file diff. Note `diff.base_sha` is the merge base (or the base
tip when histories are unrelated), not `CompareResponse.base_sha`.

head_sha.description: Tip commit of the head (source) branch.

oneOf.description:
Common ancestor of base and head. `null` when the two branches have
unrelated histories (no common ancestor); the diff then degrades to a
direct two-dot comparison against the base tip.

total_commits.description: Total commits the comparison contains (== `ahead`, uncapped).

CompleteAiModelConnectionRequest.description: Finish connecting: what the provider sent the browser back with.

ComponentBlastRadius.description:
What a publish would do to the pipelines already referencing this component.

Read-only and advisory throughout. It reports what *would* break and does not block the publish,
because the publisher is not always the party who can fix a downstream pipeline.

floating_pipelines.description: Pipelines whose reference would resolve to this version.

sampled.description: How many of them were re-expanded and re-validated.

ComponentBody.description:
What a component contains: its stage slots, parameters, steps, connections and the ports it
exposes. Drafts and published versions share this shape.

component_instances.description:
Other components this component uses. Always empty in a published version, where they have
already been expanded into steps.

edges.description: Connections between the component's own steps; both ends must be steps of this component.

stage_slots.description:
The positions the component's steps occupy, in order. A pipeline using the component maps
each slot to one of its own stages.

ComponentInputPort.description:
An input the component exposes, feeding one or more of its steps' input ports — a component
taking `source` for both its build and its test step declares it once. Its type comes from the
ports it feeds.

ComponentInstance.description:
A component used in a pipeline. It acts like a step: connections reach it through the
component's ports, and it expands into the component's steps.

component_id.description:
The component used, by id. Creating another component with the same name later never
changes what this instance runs.

component_ref.description:
The reference as the author wrote it, kept for display. It is not used to find the
component.

id.description:
The instance's id, unique among the pipeline's step ids. Connections use it as they use a
step id.

name.description: Display name, also put in front of the display names of the steps it expands into.

params.description: Values for the component's parameters, by parameter name.

stage_map.description:
Maps every stage slot the component declares to a stage of this pipeline, keeping the slots'
order.

ComponentLifecycleState.description:
Where a published version sits in its retirement.

A `deprecated` version still resolves for an exact reference and still runs, but no floating
reference selects it — which is what makes deprecating the safe way to retire one. A `sunset`
version refuses to resolve at all, exact reference included.

inherited.description:
Whether the component belongs to a group above the group or repository being listed,
rather than to it.

unsatisfied_capabilities.description:
Capabilities the latest active version needs that no provider installed here supplies.
Left out when there are none.

ComponentListItem.description: A component this group or repository may use, and whether everything it needs is installed.

ComponentNode.description:
A step in a component: an ordinary pipeline step placed in one of the component's stage slots.
`changes`, `approval` and `resource_group` are not allowed on it.

param_slots.description: Step fields whose values come from the component's parameters rather than from the step.

stage_slot.description: Which of the component's stage slots this step is placed in.

ComponentNodeParams.description:
Step fields whose values a component parameter supplies, each naming the parameter to take the
value from. A step's `config` reads parameters directly instead, with `{"$param": "<name>"}`.

oneOf.description:
The parameter naming the environment whose plain variables this step reads without
deploying there.

ComponentOutputPort.description: An output the component exposes, taken from exactly one of its steps' output ports.

ComponentParamType.description: The JSON shape a parameter's value must have.

ComponentParameter.description: A typed value a consuming pipeline supplies.

allowed_values.description:
The only values this parameter accepts. Absent means any value of its type. On a published
parameter, adding this list or removing a value from it is a major version change; adding a
value is a minor one.

required.description:
Whether a pipeline using the component must supply a value. A required parameter cannot
have a default.

ComponentRepinReport.description: What a re-pin did, or would do.

candidates.description: Consumers matching the filter that the sweep looked at, before authorization or validation.

dry_run.description: True when nothing was written and the report describes what would have happened.

truncated.description:
True when the component has more consumers than one sweep examines. The remainder are
reached by running the sweep again.

ComponentSourceFile.description: One file a published version was compiled from, as it was written.

path.description: The file's path from the repository's root.

ComponentUpgradeEntry.description: One consuming pipeline, and where it stands relative to the target version.

oneOf.description:
The version the pipeline's reference selects at the moment — for a floating reference,
possibly newer than when the pipeline was last saved. Absent when it selects none.

sampled.description: How many consumers were re-expanded against the target to see whether they still validate.

truncated.description:
True when the component has more consumers than one report covers. The remainder are reached
by narrowing to a target version, or by reading the usage listing directly.

ComponentUsageEntry.description: One pipeline that references a component, and the reference it wrote.

language_version.description: The version of the pipeline language the files are written in.

source.description: The component's files as they were written at the commit it was published from.

ComponentVersionResponse.description: A published version with the body it froze, and the files it was published from.

ComponentVersionSummary.description: A published version's metadata, without its body.

examples.changelog: Waits for the function update to finish before reporting success.

capability_requirements.description: The provider capabilities the version's steps use.

commit_sha.description: The commit whose files it was published from.

contract_digest.description:
A SHA-256 fingerprint, in hex, of what a pipeline using the version must satisfy: its
parameters, its ports and the variables it reads. It changes only when that contract does.

depth.description: How many levels of components the version spans: 1 when it uses no other component.

expanded_node_count.description: How many steps the version expands into.

tag_name.description:
The tag that published it: `<name>/<version>`, or a plain `<version>`. Absent on a version
published before versions were published by tag.

variable_requirements.description:
The variables the version's steps read from the pipeline that uses it. Each must be declared
on the environment those steps run in, or on a group or repository above the pipeline, or
a run is refused when it starts.

ConcurrencyKey.description:
The lock a step takes so that only one step holding it runs at a time: `env:` followed by an
environment's id, or `rg:` followed by your organization's id and a resource group's name. Set
by the platform.

ConcurrencyMode.description:
What happens when a run wants to deploy while another run holds the lock: `queue` (the
default) waits its turn, `skip` skips the step, and `cancel_previous` cancels the other run.
`cancel_previous` is available on environments only, not on a step's resource group.

ConcurrencyPolicy.description:
Whether deploys to an environment run one at a time, and what happens to a deploy that has to
wait.

exclusive.description: Whether deploys to this environment run one at a time. Off by default.

max_lock_wait_seconds.description:
How long a queued deploy waits for its turn before failing, in seconds: from 60 (shorter
values are rounded up) to 21600. `0`, the default, means it waits for as long as the
pipeline's timeout allows.

ConfigChange.description:
One change a draft makes to the live revision: where it is, its class, the value before and
after, and when it takes effect.

after.description: The value in the draft; absent when the draft removes it.

before.description: The value in the live revision; absent when the draft adds it.

path.description:
Where the change is, as a dotted path that names list items by their keys rather than
their positions: `agents.ada.profile.persona`, `rituals.daily-stand-up.cadence`,
`autonomy.gates.merge_protected`.

old_path.description: Where the file was before a rename, when a rename is part of the conflict.

resolvable.description: Whether this file can be resolved in the browser.

sections.description:
The file as runs and blocks, for a `content` or `add_add` conflict the browser can resolve.
Empty for every other kind, which is resolved by a choice of the whole file.

oneOf.description: The file's mode on the merge request's branch; absent where that side has no file.
The file's mode on the target branch; absent where that side has no file.

ConflictKind.description: What kind of conflict a file has. Closed: a client offers different choices for each.

ConflictResolution.description: The resolution of one conflicted file.

ConflictSection.description:
A run of one conflicted file: lines both sides agree on, or a block where they differ.

Every line keeps its terminator, so joining a resolution's lines reproduces the file's line
endings and its final newline exactly.

oneOf.description: Lines the merge settled on its own.
A block the two sides wrote differently.

base.description: What both started from, when there was a common version.

id.description: `c1`, `c2`, … in file order — stable for a given pair of heads.

ConflictSummary.description:
The merge gate's view of a merge request's conflicts — enough to offer the right action without
reading every conflict.

resolvable_in_browser.description: Whether they can all be resolved in the browser; when not, they are resolved with git.

resolve_refusal.description: Why not, when they may not.

viewer_can_resolve.description:
Whether the caller may resolve them: resolving pushes a merge commit to the merge request's
branch, so this is whether they may push there.

ConnectionAuthMode.description:
How a connection authenticates to its provider's cloud: `static_credentials` (stored
credentials, the default) or `oidc_federation` (nothing stored; each run assumes a cloud role
with a short-lived identity token gitmoap issues).

ConnectionProvider.description: A provider an organization may connect an account of its own with.

ContactMessageBody.description: What you want to say: 10 to 5000 characters, with no control characters but newlines and tabs.

ContactMessageId.description: The reference of a message sent through the contact form — quote it if you write again about the same thing.

ContactName.description: The name to address a reply to: 1 to 100 characters, no control characters.

ContactReceipt.description:
A message, as its sender is told it arrived. A person replies by email to the address given;
nothing is sent to it before then.

message_id.description: The reference to quote if you write again about the same thing.

ContactReplyAddress.description: One email address the reply goes to, such as ada@example.com — never a list, and never a name with an address.

ContactTopic.description: What a message is about, which chooses the desk it is forwarded to.

ContinueAiSessionRequest.description:
Continue an ended session: what the person adds, read by the continuation after the ended
session's conversation.

examples.instruction: The push rule now allows your branch; push again and open the merge request.

instruction.description:
Why the agent stopped and what has changed since, 1 to 4,000 characters. It is the
continuation's first input.

ContractChange.description: How far the contract moved between the last published version and the draft.

ContributionBreakdown.description: Contributions by kind, counted the same way as the contribution heatmap.

ContributionByType.description: Per-type breakdown of a single day's contributions.

ContributionCell.description: One populated day in the heatmap (days with no activity are omitted).

The contribution heatmap for a principal over an inclusive UTC date range.

cells.description: Sparse, ascending by `date`. Only days with activity.

longest_streak.description: Longest run of consecutive active days within the range.

principal_id.description: The subject user, service account or agent id.

principal_type.description:
`user`, `service_account` or `agent` — or, for a pipeline run reading its own (never
credited, so always empty), `pipeline_run`.

total.description: Sum of `count` across all cells in range.

Contributor.description: A repository contributor: one distinct commit-author identity, with its totals.

name.description: The author name from git, as spelled in the most recent attributed commit.

oneOf.description:
The gitmoap principal this git identity resolves to, absent when the author
email matches no registered user or service account.

CopiedRef.description: A branch or tag the copy brought, and the commit it arrived at.

CreateAccessGrantsRequest.description: Give one role to one or more people, service accounts or teams on a group or repository.

expires_at.description: When the access ends. Omit it for access that lasts until it is revoked.

oneOf.description: Why the access is given, shown beside the grant and kept in the audit log.

subjects.description: Who receives the role — at most 50 subjects in one request.

CreateAccessGrantsResponse.description: What granting access did — or, with `dry_run=true`, what it would do.

grants.description: The grants made. Empty for a preview.

oneOf.description: Present only for a preview: who would gain what. Nothing was written.

unchanged.description: Subjects that already held the role here and were left as they were.

CreateAccessLimitRequest.description: Cap a subject on a group or repository and everything beneath it.

oneOf.description: Why the limit exists — shown beside it, and in access reviews.

CreateAccessTokenRequest.description:
Request body for minting an access token. Scopes may be individual
`{domain}:{verb}` strings or convenience bundles (`read_api`, …).

expires_in_days.description: Days until the token expires. Omit for a non-expiring token.

oneOf.description: Optional resource binding restricting the token to one subtree.

CreateAccessTokenResponse.description:
Response to a token-creation request. The plaintext `token` is shown only
here and is never recoverable afterwards.

token.description: The plaintext token. Store it securely — it is not shown again.

CreateAiOrgRequest.description: Create the `draft` organization the setup works in.

region.description: Where model calls are served. Fixed once chosen.

CreateAiProfileDraftRequest.description: Draft an agent's persona from a brief.

brief.description: What the agent is for, in your words.

oneOf.description:
The model to draft with: any active model served in the organization's region, as the
model catalogue lists them. Leave it out and the economical tier's default model is used.

The position to write the persona for. Leave it out and the drafter chooses one and says
which.

repository_ids.description:
Up to five repositories of the organization to ground the persona in. Leave it out and the
five pushed to most recently are used, among those everyone who can see the organization
can read.

pinned_at_sha.description:
The commit the path and line range refer to. It must be reachable from the default branch,
since the platform follows the region along that branch.

assigned.description:
The suggested owners who were assigned — only when the `default_assignee_from_codeowners`
setting is on and the work item had no assignee. An owner who cannot access the work item
stays a suggestion.

suggested_assignees.description:
The people and service accounts the repository's CODEOWNERS file names as owners of the
anchored path. Whether any were assigned is in `assigned`.

CreateAnchorResponse.description: The anchor that was created, plus who owns the code it points at — taken from the repository's own ownership rules.

oneOf.description: A branch pattern such as `main` or `release/*`; absent means every branch.

approvers.description: Who may satisfy it. Absent means anyone who may approve merge requests here.

enforcement.description:
`enforced` applies the rule to everything beneath and lets it only be strengthened there.
Only someone who administers access here may define one.

oneOf.description:
An enforced rule defined above, to strengthen here: this rule then applies in its place, and
must be at least as strong in every field.

CreateAssetRequest.description: Registers a file to attach to a release, and returns a URL to upload it to.

size.description: The file's exact size in bytes. An upload of any other size is rejected.

CreateAttachmentRequest.description: A file to upload into a repository or group.

content_type.description:
Its media type. `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif` and `image/webp` render in place; any
other is stored as `application/octet-stream`, and the upload must then be sent as that.

filename.description: Its name, 1–255 characters, without a path.

size.description: Its exact size in bytes, at most 25 MiB — the upload is refused at any other size.

CreateAttentionBookmarkRequest.description: Bookmark something into your own attention inbox.

CreateBalanceAdjustmentRequest.description: An operator's adjustment to a namespace's balance — signed, attributed and explained.

amount_micros.description: Micro-dollars to add (positive) or take away (negative); never zero.

CreateBlueprintRequest.description: Create a blueprint on a scope.

blueprint_id.description: The custom-type slug, unique within the scope.

enforcement.description:
On a group, `enforced` holds every group and repository beneath to this rule or a stricter
one for the same pattern. Only someone who administers access on the group may set it.

CreateChannelRequest.description: A new channel in a group.

name.description: The channel's name, unique in the group.

oneOf.description: What the channel is for.
Who reads it: `group` (the default) or `private`, read by its members — you first.

start_line.description:
For a comment on a range, its first line — on `start_side` — with `old_line` or
`new_line` its last. At most 500 lines; a range on one side runs forwards.

oneOf.description: The side of the diff `start_line` is on.

CreateCommitRequest.description:
One commit, written from a list of file changes: the branch it lands on, its message, and each
file to create, update, delete, move or make executable.

actions.description: The file changes, at most 100, each path touched once.

branch.description: The branch the commit lands on.

oneOf.description:
The head the commit must land on. Omitted, the commit lands on the branch's current head as
long as every file it changes is still the one the caller edited.

message.description: The commit message, taken as written — trailers such as `Signed-off-by` included.

oneOf.description:
Create `branch` from this branch's head and land the commit on it, in one step. `branch`
must not exist yet.

CreateCommitResponse.description: A commit written in the browser, landed.

branch_created.description: The commit created `branch` (from `start_branch`, or as a repository's first commit).

CreateCriterionRequest.description: Create one criterion on a work item's Definition of Done.

oneOf.description: The typed binding. Absent (or `null`) is a manual checkbox.

checked.description: For a manual criterion, whether it starts ticked. Must be `false` or absent for a bound one.

ordinal.description: Where to place it; appended to the end when absent.

required_for_close.description:
Whether this criterion must be satisfied before the work item can be closed or verified.
Defaults to `true`; set `false` for an aspirational one.

text.description: The human statement — the criterion's title.

oneOf.description: The reference an error gave, when the report is about one.

More about it, in at most 5000 characters: what you did, what you expected, what happened
instead. The same rule as the summary: the problem, never the data.

kind.description: What the report is about: something broken, something missing, or something confusing.

oneOf.description:
The path of the page the report is about, such as `/acme/api/-/merge_requests/87`. The path
alone: a query string or a fragment is refused.

summary.description:
What happened and what would have helped, in at most 500 characters. Never repository
content, code, secrets or anything personal.

oneOf.description: The MCP tool the report is about, when it is about one.

CreateForkRequest.description: The body of a request to fork a repository.

oneOf.description: Copy only the default branch (the default), or every branch.

description.description: The fork's description. Defaults to the upstream's.

display_name.description: The fork's display name. Defaults to the upstream's.

group_id.description: The group the fork is created in. You need to be able to create repositories there.

include_tags.description: Copy the upstream's tags. Defaults to `true`.

oneOf.description:
`fork` (the default), or `private_fix` — a private fork for preparing a security fix to the
upstream, which needs a Maintainer of the upstream.
The fork's name. Defaults to the upstream's.

The fork's visibility. Defaults to the most visible the upstream and the destination group
allow; a fork of a private repository is always private.

examples.description: A refund above 10,000 EUR waits on the fraud check and times out after 30 seconds.
examples.title: Refunds over 10,000 EUR time out

oneOf.description:
Put the item in an iteration as it is created — one of its own group's, or of a group above
it. An iteration it cannot join is a `404`, and nothing is created.
Defaults to the effective status set's default status.

File the item as a custom type, naming a blueprint defined where the item is filed or on a
group above it. The blueprint's base type replaces `work_item_type`, and the item is created
with the blueprint's facets already added to its Definition of Done as criteria.
Defaults to the scope's effective `default_issue_type`.

name.description: Its name, 1–80 characters.

position.description: Its place in the list; after the others when absent.

CreateIterationCadenceRequest.description: A cadence: the schedule its iterations follow and how far ahead they are created.

active.description: Whether it starts generating straight away. Defaults to true.

cool_down_weeks.description: Weeks left between iterations that belong to none: 0 to 4. Defaults to 0.

duration_weeks.description: How long each iteration runs, in weeks: 1 to 12. Defaults to 2.

first_start_date.description:
The date the schedule starts from. The first iteration begins on the first start day on or
after it.

iterations_in_advance.description: How many upcoming iterations to keep created ahead of today: 1 to 12. Defaults to 4.

oneOf.description: The weekday iterations begin on. Defaults to Monday.

title.description: Its title. Each iteration it generates is titled with it and the iteration's number.

CreateIterationRequest.description: A hand-made iteration: a title and the days it runs.

examples.description: Fix what the launch found.
examples.title: Hardening week

description.description: What it is for, in Markdown, up to 16 KiB.

due_date.description: Its last day, included. On or after the first day.

key.description:
A `scoped::key` is the mechanism behind mutual exclusion: two labels sharing a
prefix cannot sit on one issue.

title.description: Its display name, 1–64 characters; without one it shows its key.

examples.description: A timed-out authorization is retried once, with the same idempotency key.
examples.title: Retry card authorizations on gateway timeouts

acknowledge_publication.description:
For a merge request from another repository: consent to publish the source branch's commits
to everyone who can read this repository. Required `true` when the preview reports a
widening; nothing defaults it.

acknowledged_blobs.description:
For a merge request from another repository: blobs the credential check flagged that you
confirm hold no credential — a test fixture, a documented example. At most 100.

allow_maintainer_edits.description:
For a merge request from another repository: let this repository's mergers push to the
source branch — fast-forward only, while the merge request is open. Defaults to `false`.

closes_issue_ids.description:
Work items of this repository the merge request closes when it merges, by number. Each is
written into the description as `Closes #n` — the description is what the links follow —
and linked with the merge request.

reviewer_ids.description:
People or service accounts to ask for review, added with the merge request. Each must be
able to read it; one who cannot is refused before anything is written, the refusal's
`field` naming its place (`reviewer_ids[2]`).

oneOf.description:
The repository the source branch is in, for a merge request from another repository of the
same fork network. Absent — or this repository — for a merge request between two of its own
branches.

CreateOAuthAuthorizationRequest.description:
Starts the consent step of an OAuth sign-in: the consent page passes on, unchanged, the query
string the client sent to `/oauth/authorize`.

query.description: The authorization request's query string, with or without its leading `?`.

CreateProviderConnectionRequest.description:
Creates a provider connection. Credentials are checked against the provider's `auth_schema`
and stored securely; they are never returned.

auth_mode.description: How the connection authenticates. Defaults to `static_credentials`.

credentials.description:
The provider's credentials, in the shape its `auth_schema` describes. Required for
`static_credentials`; refused for `oidc_federation`.

environment_ids.description:
Binds the connection to these environments, so only a step deploying to one of them may
use it. Each must be an environment the connection's pipelines can deploy to: one this
group or repository owns, a group above it, or — for a group's connection — a group or
repository beneath it. Leave it out to let any step use the connection. At most 20.

oneOf.description:
The federation target. Required for `oidc_federation`; absent for
`static_credentials`.

protected.description:
Whether only a run on a protected branch or tag may use the connection: one a branch or
tag rule protects, building a commit in that ref's history. Defaults to `false`.

CreateReleaseRequest.description: Creates a release for a tag, creating the tag first when it does not exist.

oneOf.description: Release title; defaults to `tag_name` when omitted.
A commit SHA or branch to create the tag from when it does not yet exist.

examples.description: Card payments: authorization, capture and refunds

added.description: Permission keys to add. Each brings the permissions it needs.

removed.description: Permission keys to remove from the base.

slug.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; unique in the organization.

name.description: What it is for, such as the identity provider it is given to. 1–100 characters.

campaign_active.description:
Whether to switch the campaign on from the start. Setting it to `true` requires the Owner
role.

campaign_max_items.description:
How many work items the campaign may file each time it is switched on. Defaults to 200; at
most 1,000.

name.description: Defaults to the slug.

oneOf.description:
The group that owns this service. Naming a group here requires Maintainer on that group as
well, since it makes that team responsible for the service.

The team that owns this service. Naming a team here requires maintaining that team, or
managing the organization's teams.

CreateSsoInviteRequest.description:
An invitation for someone without a gitmoap account to join the organization at their first SSO
sign-in.

expires_at.description:
When the invite stops letting the address in — within a year. Omit it for an invite that
waits until it is used or revoked.

oneOf.description: Why the address is invited, shown beside the invite.

The role given at the top-level group on first sign-in — a built-in role, or one of the
organization's own (default: the connection's default role).

allowed_to_create.description:
The lowest access level that may create, move or delete a matching tag: `developer`,
`maintainer` or `owner`. `maintainer` when left out.

enforcement.description:
On a group, `enforced` holds every group and repository beneath it to this rule or a
stricter one for the same pattern; only an Owner of the group may set it. A repository's
rule is always `default`.

tag_pattern.description:
A tag name, or a glob where `*` matches any run of characters, `/` included — `v*`,
`release/*`, `v1.2.0`.

members.description: The people to put on the team. You become a maintainer unless you list yourself otherwise.

slug.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; unique in the organization.

CreateWebhookRequest.description: Creates a webhook that is called when the chosen events happen.

active.description: Whether deliveries are sent. Defaults to `true`.

events.description: The events that trigger a delivery.

secret.description:
The secret each delivery is signed with, so your endpoint can check it came from gitmoap.
Stored encrypted and never returned.

CreateWikiAttachmentRequest.description: Ask for somewhere to put a file.

message.description: The commit message. Defaulted from the action when absent, the way a browser edit works.

CredentialFormat.description: A credential format a line matched — named, never quoted. `gitmoap_token`: a Gitmoap access token. `pem_private_key`: a PEM private key, of any key type, encrypted or not. `aws_access_key_id`: an AWS access key ID. `github_token`: a GitHub personal access, OAuth, app or refresh token. `gitlab_token`: a GitLab personal access token. `slack_token`: a Slack token. `stripe_secret_key`: a Stripe live secret or restricted key. `google_api_key`: a Google API key. `npm_token`: an npm access token.

CriteriaHeadState.description: Where the acceptance-criteria merge check stands. `passed`: every required criterion is satisfied at the head. `pending`: none has failed, and some are waiting for a pipeline. `failed`: at least one is not satisfied for a reason waiting will not fix.

CriteriaSummary.description: The counts a card and a work item's header render.

required.description: Of the `required_for_close` ones — the set that actually gates `Verified` and a close.

Criterion.description:
One line of a work item's Definition of Done: a statement, optionally bound to evidence the
platform checks, with its current verdict and the evidence behind it. It moves with its work
item.

examples.text: A refund above 10,000 EUR completes within 5 seconds at p99

binding_expr.description: The binding's `@`-expression, as written. Absent for a manual criterion.

binding_key.description:
The normalised form of `binding_expr`, which two equivalent spellings share. Absent for a
manual criterion.

checked.description:
Whether the box is ticked. Meaningful only for a manual criterion — a bound one is ticked by
its `state`, and ticking it by hand is refused with a `409`.

criterion_id.description:
The criterion's identifier. It never changes, so rewording or re-binding a criterion keeps
its identity and its evidence.

description.description:
An optional longer description (markdown) — the per-criterion detail a flat checkbox could
never hold.

oneOf.description:
The blueprint facet this criterion belongs to, when a blueprint added it. Absent for a
criterion written directly. A facet's state is rolled up from the criteria carrying its key.

The pipeline whose run last provided evidence for this criterion. Only a later run of the
same pipeline can make the criterion `stale`.

last_evidence_value.description: The observed value, for a `Metric` or `Coverage` binding.

ordinal.description: Position in the description, so the list round-trips in authoring order.

required_for_close.description: `@optional` opts out. Everything else in a Definition of Done is required *by definition*.

text.description: The human statement — the criterion's title. The *label*, not the identity.

CriterionAtHead.description: One required acceptance criterion, at a merge request's head.

examples.text: Retrying a payment never charges twice

carried_from.description:
When the step that proves it did not run at this head because nothing it watches changed:
the earlier head of this merge request whose run is being counted instead.

issue_uid.description: The work item the criterion belongs to.

oneOf.description: The step of that run whose report decided it.
The run that decided it, when one did.

reason.description: Why it is or is not.

value.description: The measured number, for a measurement or coverage criterion.

CriterionBinding.description:
What a criterion is bound to — the condition the platform checks on its behalf. A criterion with
no binding is a manual checkbox.

oneOf.description:
A named test. An **unqualified** binding matches the test id in *any* suite, which is what
an author who wrote `@test(empty_cart_rejected)` meant; a qualified one matches only its own.
A numeric measurement compared against a threshold.
Line coverage of the files matching a glob. Every matching file must clear `min_pct`.
A pipeline node succeeding — the coarsest binding, *"the deploy node went green"*.

A service-catalog scorecard check passing. Its verdict comes from the scorecard rather than
from a pipeline run, so a work item in a group may carry it. Only a scorecard campaign creates
one; a request that supplies it is refused.

CriterionBindingRow.description: A bound criterion, as seen from the repository whose pipeline runs evaluate it.

oneOf.description:
The step of the last evidence's pipeline that decided it. The `Stale` rule reads it: only
that step running again and reporting completely without the result means the result is
gone. `None` for evidence recorded before steps were kept, and for a `Node` binding's.

CriterionHeadReason.description: Why one required acceptance criterion is or is not satisfied at a merge request's head. `passing`: a pipeline that tested the head reported it passing. `failing`: one reported it failing. `pending`: a pipeline that applies to the head is still to finish, or its results are still being read. `not_reported`: the pipelines finished and sent reports, but none mentioned this test, measurement or file. `no_report`: the pipelines finished and none of their steps sent a test, coverage or measurement report. `skipped`: the step that would prove it did not run at this head and has never run on this merge request. `rerun_needed`: the criterion was bound after the last run, so run the pipelines again. `no_run`: no pipeline tested this head. `unchecked`: a criterion a person ticks, not yet ticked. `not_passing`: a service check the criterion names is not passing.

CriterionKind.description:
A kind of acceptance criterion. `Manual` is a human-ticked checkbox (no binding); the
rest bind to a predicate the platform evaluates from pipeline evidence.

CriterionKindCatalog.description: Every kind of acceptance criterion, each described well enough to build a form for it.

CriterionKindDescriptor.description:
One kind of acceptance criterion: what it is, and the fields it takes — both as a typed list
(`fields`) and as a JSON Schema (`config_schema`) a form can be rendered from.

config_schema.description: A JSON Schema over the fields — render a form from this.

evaluable.description:
Whether the platform evaluates this kind from evidence (i.e. it is a real binding, not a
manual checkbox).

proved_by.description: What proves a criterion of this kind, and therefore what a pipeline needs for it.

CriterionProof.description: What proves a criterion of this kind. `person`: someone ticks it. `step_outcome`: whether a pipeline step succeeds, which needs nothing more than the step. `test_reports`: a test report a step writes — JUnit XML, cargo-nextest JSON, go test -json or CTRF. `coverage_reports`: an LCOV, Cobertura or Go coverage report. `measurements`: a measurement a step writes as gitmoap.evidence/v1. `scorecard`: a service-catalog check.

CriterionView.description: A criterion with its evidence reassembled — what a client renders.

CustomRole.description: A custom role of an organization.

added.description: Permissions added to the base, by key.

base_role.description:
The built-in role this one starts from, and whose rank it counts as wherever a rank is
compared, such as a protected branch's minimum.

permissions.description: Everything the role holds: the base, the additions and what they need, less the removals.

removed.description: Permissions removed from the base, by key.

CustomerLogEvent.description: One line of a step's log output.

oneOf.description:
The step reads an environment's variables without deploying there, so that environment's
secrets are not given to it.

count.description: How many of its secrets the step does not receive.

oneOf.description:
What the step's reports said, read after the step ended — whether it passed or failed — for
the acceptance criteria of work items.

problems.description: The reports that could not be read in full, and why.

reports.description: How many report files the step left.

results.description: How many test, coverage and measurement results they held.

oneOf.description:
The step's reports could not be read, so nothing from this step counts toward acceptance
criteria.

reason.description: Why they could not be read.

phase.description: Which stage of the step's setup or teardown produced this line.

oneOf.description:
How the step ended, for a step that was stopped before it could say so itself.

A step stopped from outside — it ran out of memory, its capacity was reclaimed, someone
cancelled it — never gets to write a closing line, so its log simply stops wherever it had
reached. This record says what became of it, so a log that stops mid-way is not mistaken
for one that finished.

exit_code.description: The container's exit code, when one was reported. `137` means it was killed.

reason.description: Why the step was stopped, word for word as the machine running it reported it.

oneOf.description:
Lines that could not be stored, reported where the gap is.

A log that silently drops lines is worse than one that admits it did: a reader draws
conclusions from the absence, and nothing else in the stream says the absence was ours.

Output collection stopped at this step's log-size ceiling.

The step keeps running and its closing lines are still collected — only further output is
dropped — so a truncated log still shows how the step ended.
A log line the platform could not interpret, passed through as-is rather than dropped.

CycleBoundary.description: A point in a cycle of the organization's iteration cadence.

CycleTimeInsights.description:
How long work takes in a repository: the median and 95th percentile of time to merge, time to
first review, work item cycle time and pipeline duration.

DashboardSummary.description: The counters a dashboard renders before its widgets load.

attention.description: The inbox badge, with its own `truncated` flag preserved for clients written against it.

count_cap.description: The ceiling each counter was computed under.

truncated.description:
The names of the counters that reached `count_cap`, whose values are therefore a minimum
rather than the full count.

DecideAiGateRequest.description: Decide a gate: approve the action it waits on, or deny it.

decision.description: Approve or deny the exact action the gate names.

oneOf.description: What the agent should know about the decision, at most 2,000 characters.

DeleteRepoPreview.description: What deleting this repository would delete. Nothing was deleted. Every fork bound to the repository is deleted with it, since nobody else may read its code once the repository is gone; send `confirm_bound_forks` with the number given here to delete them.

bound_forks.description: Every fork bound to it, each deleted with it — deepest first, the order they are deleted in.

confirm_bound_forks.description:
The number to send as `confirm_bound_forks` to delete the repository with its bound forks.
`0` when it has none, and then nothing needs confirming.

decision_note.description: A required reason for the denial.

DependencyCounts.description: How many dependencies a service has in each direction.

hidden.description:
Dependencies left out, in either direction, because you cannot see the service at the far
end.

DependencyDetail.description:
Where an observed dependency came from: the package, the versions requested and resolved, and the
lockfile that records it. Absent for a declared dependency, which names none of these.

resolved.description: The version the lockfile actually pins.

version_req.description: What the manifest asked for, where the lockfile records it.
