DependencyGraphEdge.description: One dependency in a dependency graph, by service id. The graph's `nodes` carry the services.

depth.description:
How many hops from the root service this dependency was reached at, from 1 to the graph's
`depth`.

DependencyKind.description:
How a service depends on the far end of a dependency — not what the far end is. The same
`library` service can be consumed as a package by one service and called over HTTP by another.

DependencySource.description:
How a dependency came to be known, and therefore how far it can be trusted. A declared and an
observed dependency between the same two services are reported separately, so a declaration no
lockfile mentions, or a lockfile entry nobody declared, stands out.

Deployment.description: One deploy of one service to one environment, at one commit.

deployment_id.description:
The deployment's id. It is derived from the run, step and attempt that made it, so the same
attempt never records two deployments.

oneOf.description:
The pipeline run that made the deployment. Absent once that run's history has been removed;
the deployment record is kept.

DeploymentBoardCell.description:
One cell of the deployment board: what is currently deployed for one service in one
environment.

commits_behind.description:
How many commits the deployment is behind its repository's default branch. Only present
when the request asks for it.

DeploymentBoardResponse.description:
A page of the deployment board: services down the side, environments across the top, and the
current deployment in each cell.

DeploymentBoardRow.description: One service on the deployment board, with a cell for each environment.

DeploymentDriftResponse.description: How far each of a service's current deployments is behind its repository's default branch.

DeploymentDriftRow.description:
How far a service's current deployment to one environment is behind its repository's default
branch. A service spanning several repositories has one of these per repository.

commits.description:
The commits the deployment is missing, at most 100. When there are more, `truncated` is
`true` and `commits_behind` still gives the full count.

commits_behind.description:
How many commits the default branch has that the deployed commit does not. Absent when the
deployed commit can no longer be read, for example after a force-push.

DeploymentStatus.description:
Where a deployment is in its life. It starts `requested`; waits as `awaiting_approval` when the
environment needs approval, ending `rejected` if refused; then `running`, ending `succeeded`,
`failed` or `cancelled`. `skipped` means another deploy held the environment and its policy is to
skip. A successful deployment becomes `superseded` when a later one replaces it.

DeploymentSummary.description: A deployment in brief, as the deployment board, a service's overview and its history show it.

DeskMailState.description: Where a message to one of Gitmoap's desks is.

DetachForkRequest.description: The body of a request to detach a fork from its upstream: the fork's path, typed.

confirm_full_path.description: The fork's full path, typed out, so a detach is never a misclick.

collapsed.description:
The patch was intentionally withheld (generated or oversized) to save
bytes but is fetchable in full on demand via `GET .../diff-file`. Only
ever set when patches were requested (`include_patch=true`).

generated.description:
Detected generated/lock/minified file. Always computed from the path,
independent of `collapsed`, so a client can badge or auto-fold it.

patch_truncated.description:
The patch exceeds the hard per-file size cap and is omitted. Unlike
`collapsed`, this file is **not** expandable in place — a client reads it
piece-by-piece via `GET .../file-lines` instead.

DiffFileResponse.description:
One file's diff, force-expanded — the response of `GET .../diff-file`.
Keyed on the `base`/`head` SHAs the batch diff already returns, so it is
snapshot-consistent with (and cacheable independently of) the batch view.

file.description:
The single file, with its patch inlined (`collapsed` is always `false`).
A genuinely oversized patch still sets `patch_truncated`; the client then
falls back to `GET .../file-lines`.

DiffFileSummary.description: One changed file, without its patch: what it is called, what happened to it, and how much.

generated.description:
Looks generated — a lock file, a minified bundle, a snapshot — judged from the path. A page
read with patches also honours the repository's `.gitattributes`.

is_binary.description: A binary file: it has no line counts and no patch.

old_path.description:
The file's previous path, for a rename or copy. Pass it as `old_path` when reading the
file's own diff, or a renamed file reads as the whole file added.

DiffFilesResponse.description:
Every file a change touches, without patches, in path order — the response of
`GET .../diff-files`. Keyed on the same `base`/`head` as a batch diff, so the list and any page
of that diff describe one snapshot.

truncated.description: The change touches more files than are listed. `stats` still counts all of them.

DiffResponse.description: One page of a diff's files, in path order, with patches when they were asked for.

total_files.description: How many files the pages can reach — every changed file, unless `truncated`.

truncated.description: The change touches more files than any page can reach. `stats` still counts all of them.

DiffStats.description: Totals for a whole change, however many of its files a response lists.

additions.description: Lines added across the whole change.

deletions.description: Lines deleted across the whole change.

DigestFrequency.description: How often your email digest is sent.

DirectConversation.description: A direct conversation with an AI agent, and what you are told before your first message.

examples.disclosure: This conversation is with @ada-ai, an AI agent of Acme. Its board can read everything said here and write in it too, and @ada-ai's replies are written by an AI.

created.description: Whether this call opened it; false when it already existed.

disclosure.description: Who else can read it — the agent's organization's board — said before you write anything.

Discussable.description:
What a comment is about: a merge request (`repository_id` and `merge_request_id`) or a work item
(`scope` and `issue_uid`).

oneOf.description: A merge request, identified by its per-repository iid.

A work item, identified by its permanent `issue_uid`, with the group or repository it lives
in.

DoraSummary.description: The four DORA metrics for this scope. Two are reported today — release frequency and merge lead time — and are named for what they actually measure. The other two need deployment records, and each returns null with a reason until those are available.

oneOf.description: Not reported: it needs deployment records. `unavailable` gives the reason.

merge_lead_time_seconds_p50.description:
The median time from a merge request's creation to its merge, in seconds. Narrower than
commit-to-production lead time.

release_frequency_per_week.description: Published, non-draft releases per week over the window.

time_to_restore_seconds.description: Not reported: it needs to know when service was degraded. `unavailable` gives the reason.

unavailable.description:
For each metric above that is never reported, its field name and the reason — as opposed to
a metric that is null only because this window had no data.

DriftCommit.description: One commit between what is deployed and the default branch tip.

Edge.description:
A connection between two steps: either a data connection from an output port of one to an input
port of the other, or, with no ports named, a dependency that only makes the target wait for the
source and passes nothing. Name both ports or neither.

oneOf.description: Absent on a dependency-only edge.
Absent on a dependency-only edge.

EditChannelMessageRequest.description: An edited message's new text. The previous text is kept.

examples.body: The release branch is cut — the changelog is next.

EffectiveAccess.description: What an explained principal may do here.

permissions.description: Every permission they hold here, by key.

EffectiveIssueSettingsResponse.description:
The work item settings in force for a repository, with every inherited and default value filled
in.

auto_close_on_verified.description:
Whether a work item closes as soon as it is verified. Defaults to `false`: passing criteria
make an item verified, and merging the merge request that closes it makes it done.

auto_reopen_on_orphaned_close.description: A closed item whose closing commit is in no branch any more reopens itself.

binding_change_resets_evidence.description: Reset a criterion's evidence when its binding changes. Default **true**.

closing_branches.description:
Branch globs whose commits close work items, in addition to the default branch, which always
does. Empty by default.

todo_ignore_paths.description:
Path globs never scanned for TODO comments. Defaults to the usual locations of vendored
code.

allow_merge_without_pipeline.description:
While `require_pipeline_success` is on: whether a merge request that no pipeline applies to
— none is defined, or none matched its branch, paths or actions — may merge. Off by
default, which blocks it.

require_pipeline_success.description:
Block the merge until every pipeline that applies to the merge request's head has
succeeded. Off by default.

EffectivePipelineVariable.description: One variable that applies to a repository's pipelines, with the scope that declared it. A secret's value is absent.

protected.description:
Whether only a run on a protected branch or tag receives the variable. A run on any other
ref receives neither this value nor a value the same name has further up.

shadowed.description:
`true` when a group further up also declares this name, so removing this declaration would
uncover that one rather than remove the variable.

EffectivePipelineVariableListResponse.description:
The pipeline variables that apply to a repository's pipelines, including those declared on the
groups above it.

limit.description: How many variables the repository may declare itself; each group above has the same limit.

max_value_bytes.description: The longest value a variable may hold, in bytes.

variables.description: The variables that apply, each naming the scope that declared it.

EffectiveProviderPolicy.description:
The provider policy in effect for a group or repository, after inheriting from the groups above
it and applying defaults.

accepted_tiers.description: The provider tiers this policy accepts in some form. `platform` is always included.

require_changelog_ack.description:
When set, moving to a newer provider version requires acknowledging its changelog first. Off
by default.

scope_id.description: The id of the group or repository asked about.

source_scope_id.description:
The id of the group or repository whose policy supplied these values — possibly a group
above the one asked about. Absent when no policy is set anywhere and the defaults apply.

oneOf.description:
Who last changed the policy that supplied these values. Absent when no policy is set
anywhere and the defaults apply.

EffectiveProviderSettings.description:
One entry of the effective-settings view, annotated with the
scope the install resolved from and the provider's catalog tier.

oneOf.description:
Lifecycle of `latest_version`, so the UI can warn on a deprecated latest.
`None` when not resolved (the trigger-validator path leaves it `None`).
The provider's catalog `latest_version` (excludes sunset; D3).

The owning org (root group) of a Private provider; `None` for public tiers.
Used by the trigger-time tier gate (own-org vs foreign-org private).

publisher_verified.description: Whether the owning publisher's namespace is verified.

tier_accepted.description: Whether the provider's tier is accepted by the resolved per-org policy.

track_latest.description:
Whether this install tracks the provider's latest published version.
When `true`, an unpinned node resolves to `latest_version` at trigger.

update_available.description:
Whether a newer version than the install's `default_version` is published
— a pure semver compare that never mutates the install (D5 K6).

require_closing_issue_reference.description:
Stricter: the reference must carry an intent to *close* (`Fixes #412`), not merely
mention. Implies `require_issue_reference`.

require_issue_reference.description:
Whether every pushed commit must reference a work item. A push with a commit that does not is
rejected as a whole.

EgressWindowUsage.description: One budget window: what has been charged, against what it is allowed.

limit_bytes.description:
The limit for this window, in bytes — reported even where the limit is not enforced, so
you can see what you would be held to.

used_bytes.description: Bytes charged to this window so far.

window.description:
The period this covers: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH` for an hour, `YYYY-MM-DD` for a day, `YYYY-MM` for a
month.

EnablingEnvironment.description: An environment a pipeline file names that resolves for this repository, with where it comes from and what protects it. One a group above defines is `inherited`: for a fork placed in an organization, the organization's own environments — guarded only by their `allowed_scopes`, which `available` reflects, and their `allowed_refs`.

allowed_refs.description: The refs allowed to deploy to it. Empty allows any.

available.description:
Whether its `allowed_scopes` admit this repository. A run naming one that does not is
refused before it starts.

deployed_to.description: Whether a step deploys to it, rather than only reading its plain variables.

inherited.description: Whether a group above the repository defines it, rather than the repository itself.

named_by.description: The pipeline files that name it.

owner_full_path.description: The path of the group or repository that defines it.

slug.description: The environment's slug, as the files name it.

EnablingPipeline.description: A pipeline file on the repository's default branch, and every condition that would start it once pipelines are on. A file that does not validate starts nothing.

name.description: The pipeline's name, as the file declares it. Absent when the file does not validate.

path.description: The file's path on the default branch.

valid.description: Whether the file validates. One that does not starts nothing until it is fixed.

EnablingSchedule.description: A schedule that would fire once pipelines are on, and the account its runs would start as: whoever's change put the file on the default branch. Absent until a change to the default branch applies the file.

cron.description: When it fires: five fields, UTC.

path.description: The file that declares it.

oneOf.description:
The account its runs start as. Absent when no change to the default branch has applied the
file yet; the next one that does decides it.

EnablingTrigger.description: One condition that would start a pipeline: its kind — `push`, `merge_request`, `tag`, `schedule` or `manual` — with the branch or tag pattern it is limited to, or a schedule's cron.

cron.description: A schedule's cron, five fields, UTC.

pattern.description: The branch or tag pattern the trigger is limited to. Absent means every branch or tag.

Environment.description: A named place software runs, and the policy governing deploys to it.

approval_enforced.description:
Whether the platform enforces `protection.requires_approval` on deploys, so a client can tell
a policy that is applied from one that is only recorded.

archived.description:
Whether the environment is archived. An archived environment can no longer be deployed to
but keeps its deployment history, and archiving can be undone. An environment with
deployments cannot be deleted, only archived.

owner_full_path.description:
The full path of the group or repository that owns the environment (e.g. `acme/platform`),
which shows when an environment in a repository's listing comes from a group above it. With
the slug it forms the environment's OIDC claim, `{owner_full_path}:{slug}`.

scope.description:
The group or repository that owns the environment. Groups and repositories beneath it can
use it too.

variable_count.description: How many variables the environment holds.

version.description:
Increases with every change. Send it with an update to have the update refused with `409`
if someone else changed the environment first.

EnvironmentField.description: A field of an environment that an update changed.

EnvironmentProtection.description:
The rules for deploying to an environment: whether a deployment needs approval and from whom,
which refs may deploy, and which groups and repositories may use it. Approvers are checked when
the approval is given, so a change in who belongs to a team applies at once.

oneOf.description:
Which kinds of approval count. A deployment approved by a bot is rarely what anyone meant,
so the default is people, signed in.

allowed_refs.description:
Globs the ref a run was started from must match for it to deploy here, in the same pattern
language as branch rules. Empty allows any ref.

allowed_scopes.description:
The only groups and repositories allowed to deploy to this environment. Absent means the
group or repository that owns it and everything beneath it.

approvers.description:
Who may approve: people, teams, or a role at a group or repository. Authority to approve a
deployment comes from being named here, never from a role alone.

prevent_self_approval.description:
Whether the person who started the run is barred from approving its deployment. What counts
is who started the run, not who wrote the commit: deploying somebody else's commit is still
your deploy.

required.description: Distinct approvals needed before the deployment starts, 1–10.

requires_approval.description:
When set, a deployment to this environment waits for approval before it starts. Nothing runs
and no credentials are issued while it waits.

wait_timer_seconds.description:
How long a deployment waits before it may start, in seconds, up to one hour. `0` means no
wait.

EnvironmentSummary.description: An environment in brief, as listings and the deployment board show it.

EnvironmentTier.description:
What kind of environment this is, whatever it is called: `development`, `testing`, `staging`
or `production`. A `production` environment is protected by default.

EnvironmentVariable.description: One environment variable. Both kinds reach a pipeline step as environment variables; `secret` decides whether the value is returned by the API. A secret's value is write-only — it is redacted from step logs and never comes back out of a read.

value.description: The variable's value. Absent for a secret, whose value can be written but never read back.

code.description:
The coarse category, tied to the status: `NOT_FOUND`, `CONFLICT`, `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`. Every
error has one; the API reference's error catalogue lists them all.

field.description:
On a `400` that refused one field's value, the field, as its JSON path: `email`,
`items[0].name`. Put the message under that input. Absent on every other error.

message.description: What went wrong, for a person. Written to be read, not parsed: match on `reason` or `code`.

reason.description:
The specific code, when the error has one: `LAST_ORGANIZATION_OWNER`, `BRANCH_PROTECTED`.
The message starts with it too. Match on this when it is present, and on `code` otherwise.

required_scope.description: The scope the access token was missing, on `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`.

violations.description:
Present on the structured-validation errors (`PROVIDER_VALIDATION_FAILED` per-node,
`PIPELINE_VALIDATION_FAILED` DAG): a JSON array of the offending elements, so a caller can
fix every one in a single round-trip. Absent (omitted) on every other error.

error.message: Conflict: LAST_ORGANIZATION_OWNER: the organization would be left with no Owner — make someone else an Owner first

Evidence.description: What a pipeline run observed, and where.

observed_at.description: When the run that produced the evidence finished, RFC 3339.

ExcludedBytes.description:
The bytes that are in the tree and not in the breakdown, by why.

Returned rather than silently dropped because *"why does my repository claim to be 94%
JavaScript?"* is the standing complaint about this feature on every host that ships it, and on
every one of them it is unanswerable without cloning the repository.

generated.description: Lock files, minified bundles, source maps.

unclassified.description:
Binaries, symlinks, submodules, data and prose languages, and anything the vocabulary
could not settle.

vendored.description: Third-party code the repository carries but did not write.

ExecutableChange.description: A changed file a build runs rather than reads, and what kind of file it is.

kind.description: What kind of file it is.

path.description: The file's path.

ExecutableChangeKind.description: What kind of file a build runs rather than reads: `pipeline_definition` (`.gitmoap/pipelines/` or `.gitmoap/components/`), `ci` (another CI system's configuration), `build_script` (a Makefile, `build.rs`, `setup.py`, a build tool's configuration), `manifest` (a package manifest or lockfile, whose scripts and dependencies install), `container` (a Dockerfile or compose file), `git_hook`, `test_runner` (a test runner's configuration or fixtures file), or `script` (a script, or a file under `scripts/` or `bin/`).

ExecutableChanges.description: Every file the merge request changed since `since_sha` that a build runs rather than reads — pipeline files, build scripts, test runners, package manifests and lockfiles, container files, git hooks, scripts. A classification of paths, not a verdict: a file it lists may be harmless and one it leaves out may not be, so read the changes before approving.

paths.description: Each changed file a build runs, by path.

since.description: Where the changes are counted from.

since_sha.description: The commit they are counted from.

truncated.description: Whether more such files changed than are listed.

ExecutableChangesSince.description: Where the changes are counted from: `approved_head`, the last head of this merge request a Maintainer approved with a trusted re-run, or `target_branch`, where the merge request left the target branch.

ExistingFork.description: A fork of the same network already in the destination.

ExpandPipelineRequest.description: Expand an unsaved definition instead of the stored one, so a builder can preview an edit.

ExpandPipelineResponse.description: The flattened graph a builder or a reviewer renders.

definition.description: The flattened definition, with no component instances left in it.

ExpandedInstanceInfo.description: What one instance contributed to the flattened graph.

component_id.description: The component used; the nil UUID for one of the repository's own, which has no row.

node_ids.description: The identifiers expansion minted for this instance's nodes.

oneOf.description:
The published version the reference resolved to; absent for one of the repository's own
components, which is its file rather than a version.

source_blob.description:
For one of the repository's own components, the blob it was read at — the exact text that
expanded.

source_path.description: For one of the repository's own components, the file it was read from.

ExplainedBinding.description: How a fork's binding cut a principal's access to it.

removed.description: Permissions the grants gave that the binding took away, by key.

unreadable.description:
The repositories the fork is bound to whose code the principal cannot read — each named only
when you can see it.

ExplainedBoundRepository.description: A repository a fork is bound to, named only to an explainer who can see it.

oneOf.description: The repository's full path. Absent when you cannot see it.
The repository's id. Absent when you cannot see it.

visible.description: Whether you can see the repository. When `false`, nothing else is named.

ExplainedLimit.description: One limit that applied in an explanation.

oneOf.description: The most the limit lets its subject hold. Absent when it allows nothing at all.

removed.description: Permissions the grants gave that this limit took away, by key.

FacetBindingTemplate.description:
How the criterion a facet adds is bound: `manual` (the default), or `bound` to evidence the
platform checks. A blueprint whose base type lives only in a group, such as `epic`, may use only
`manual`.

oneOf.description: A person ticks it. The default.
Bound to evidence the platform checks, given as a complete binding.

FacetRollup.description:
One facet's rollup over the criteria that carry its `facet_key` — the facet-panel projection,
computed wherever `verification` is computed and needing no new query.

criterion_ids.description: The criteria under this facet, in ordinal order.

required.description: Whether any criterion under the facet gates close.

satisfied.description:
Green iff every **required** criterion under the facet is satisfied — the same set the merge
gate keys on, so the rollup is presentational and never a second source of truth.

FacetTemplate.description:
One completion dimension of a blueprint. On an issue, a **named group of criteria** — seeded as
one starter criterion carrying the facet's `key` and `category`.

binding.description: How the seeded criterion is bound. Defaults to a manual checkbox.

category.description:
The facet's category — any value you choose. Facets with the same category are grouped
together.

hint.description: The starter criterion's text. When absent the criterion is titled by the facet `label`.

key.description:
The facet's identifier within the blueprint. It stays the same when the label changes, so a
work item re-applying the blueprint updates the facet in place.

label.description: The facet's display name, such as "Observability".

required.description:
Whether the facet's criterion must be satisfied before the work item can be closed or
verified. Defaults to `true`.

FactSource.description:
A kind of fact a check needs before its question means anything. A service with none of the
facts a check needs is `not_applicable` for that check rather than failing it.

FeedbackChannel.description: How a report arrived. Decided by the platform from the request, never claimed by the caller.

FeedbackDetails.description: More about a report: 1 to 5000 characters, with no control characters but newlines and tabs.

FeedbackPage.description: The path of the page a report is about, such as /acme/api/-/merge_requests/87 — the path alone, never what follows a ? or a #.

FeedbackReceipt.description: A report, as its author is told it was received.

feedback_id.description: The report's reference — quote it if you write again about the same thing.

FeedbackView.description: A report, as a platform administrator reads it.

examples.client: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 14_6) AppleWebKit/605.1.15
examples.summary: The merge button stays disabled after the pipeline passes.

oneOf.description: The reference an error gave, when it is about one.

channel.description: How it arrived: from the web app, through an MCP tool, or over the API.

client.description:
The client application: the name an MCP client gave itself, or the `User-Agent` the request
carried.

oneOf.description: Where the support desk's notice of it is, for a report that owes one.
More about it, when the sender gave more.

oauth_client_id.description: The app the person approved, when the token came from connecting it by signing in.

oneOf.description: The path of the page it is about, when it came from the web app.

sender.description: The person or service account that sent it, as they are named now.

summary.description: What happened and what would have helped, in the sender's words.

oneOf.description: The MCP tool it is about, when it is about one.

FieldDescriptor.description: One typed argument field of a criterion kind.

FieldType.description: The type of a criterion-kind field, which decides the form control that suits it.

oneOf.description: A free-text string.
A file-path glob.
A number, optionally bounded.
One of a fixed set of choices — renders a dropdown.

FileAction.description:
One file change in a commit written in the browser.

Every change to a file that exists names the blob the caller started from
(`expected_blob_sha`, the `blob_sha` a blob read returned): if the file has changed since, the
commit is refused rather than overwriting someone else's work.

oneOf.description: Add a file that does not exist yet.

encoding.description: How `content` is encoded: `utf8` text, or `base64` for any bytes.

executable.description: Make the file executable. Defaults to a regular file.

oneOf.description: Replace a file's content. Its mode is kept.
Remove a file. A directory is removed by naming its files.
Move a file to `path`, keeping its mode — and its content, unless `content` replaces it.
Set or clear a file's executable bit, keeping its content.

FileLinesResponse.description:
A bounded window of a file's lines at a ref — the response of
`GET .../file-lines`. Powers context expansion above/below a hunk and reading
a file larger than the per-file patch cap piece-by-piece.

end.description: 1-based line number of the last returned line (inclusive).

is_binary.description: The file is binary; `lines` is empty (line windows are text-only).

ref.description: The ref the lines were read at (echoes the request `ref`).

start.description: 1-based line number of the first returned line.

FileMode.description: A tree entry's mode: what kind of file git records at a path.

ForkAutoSyncView.description: Whether pushes to the upstream branch fast-forward the fork's tracked branch automatically, as whom, and why it stopped if it did.

oneOf.description: The person it runs as.
Why it stopped, when it did.

ForkBranches.description: `default_branch`: only the upstream's default branch. `all`: every branch.

ForkCopyView.description: What the fork copied from its upstream when it was created.

ref_count.description: How many refs it copied in all.

refs.description: Up to a hundred of the refs it copied, with the commit each arrived at.

tags.description: Whether it copied tags.

ForkFailure.description: `authority_revoked`: the person forking could no longer fork the upstream when the copy ran. `upstream_deleted`: the upstream was deleted during the copy. `upstream_narrowed`: the upstream became less visible during the copy — fork it again to be classified afresh. `storage_quota`: the copy would not fit in the destination's storage. `copy_failed`: the copy itself failed.

ForkFailureView.description: Why the copy stopped for good.

examples.message: The upstream repository became less visible while it was being copied. Fork it again to be classified afresh.

ForkFilter.description: Whether forks are listed: `include` lists them with every other repository, `exclude` leaves them out, and `only` lists nothing but forks.

ForkGovernancePreview.description: What a governance action would do, decided and changed nothing.

newly_readable_by.description:
For a release that leaves no binding: the people who hold a grant on the fork and cannot
read this repository, who would newly read the fork. Empty while any binding remains.

open_merge_requests.description: Open merge requests in the fork, which a recall closes with it.

remaining_bindings.description: For a release: how many bindings would remain — the fork stays bound while any does.

size_bytes.description: How much storage the fork holds, in bytes.

ForkInventoryRow.description: A fork bound to your code: where it is and who holds it — never its content, branch names or commit messages.

oneOf.description: Who created the fork.

creator_still_reads_upstream.description: Whether the person who forked it can still read the upstream's code.

group_id.description: The group that holds the fork.

kind.description: Whether the fork is bound or independent.

open_merge_requests.description: Open merge requests in the fork.

purpose.description: Whether it is an ordinary fork or a private fix fork.

size_bytes.description: How much storage the fork holds, in bytes.

upstream_full_path.description: The path of the repository it is bound to.

upstream_id.description: The repository this fork is bound to that the inventory was asked of.

ForkKind.description: `bound`: a fork of private code, or a private fix fork — only people who can read the repositories it is bound to can read it, and it never leaves its upstream's organization. `independent`: a fork of a public or internal repository, whose audience is its own within its visibility ceiling.

ForkListScope.description: `children`: the repository's direct forks. `network`: every fork descended from the repository's network root.

ForkMergeRequestPolicy.description: `disabled`: nobody. `members`: only people who hold a grant on the repository. `everyone`: anyone who can read it.

ForkNetworkView.description: The network a fork belongs to: every repository descended by forking from one root.

depth.description: How many forks lie between this one and the root, itself included.

id.description: The network's id: its root's repository id, which outlives the root.

root.description: The root, as far as you can see it.

ForkPolicy.description: `disabled`: never. `organization`: only into, or towards, the repository's own organization. `anywhere`: any group the person may create repositories in, or any repository of the network. A private repository's `anywhere` is `organization`: private code never forks out of its organization.

ForkPreview.description: What forking would do, decided and copied nothing: where the fork would be, what it would be, what it would cost, and — when it would be refused — the error the create would answer.

examples.pipelines: Off until a Maintainer turns them on: 3 pipeline files

estimated_bytes.description: The upstream's size: what the copy reserves in the destination.

existing_forks_here.description: Forks of the same network already in the destination group.

kind.description: Whose audience its code would have.

pipelines.description: What would run in the fork: nothing, until one of its Maintainers turns pipelines on.

oneOf.description:
The error the create would answer, when it would be refused — so a form can explain it
before anyone fills it in.

visibility_ceiling.description: The most visible it could ever be.

ForkPurpose.description: `fork`: an ordinary fork. `private_fix`: a private fork in which a security fix to its upstream is prepared out of view and landed in one step.

ForkRelationship.description: `linked`: the fork can sync from its upstream and propose to it. `detached`: its Owner ended that relationship; it no longer syncs or proposes, and a bound fork stays bound.

ForkSettingValue_AccountAgeDays.description: One effective fork setting: its value, where it came from — `default`, `repository`, or `group:<id>` — and whether a group above enforces it as a ceiling.

enforced.description:
Whether a group above enforces this field: a scope beneath may tighten it and never loosen
it. Absent for a field that cannot be enforced.

source.description: Where the value comes from: `default`, `repository`, or `group:<id>`.

value.description: Accounts younger than this many days may not open a cross-repository merge request: 0 to 30.

ForkSettingValue_ForkMergeRequestPolicy.description: One effective fork setting: its value, where it came from — `default`, `repository`, or `group:<id>` — and whether a group above enforces it as a ceiling.

enforced.description:
Whether a group above enforces this field: a scope beneath may tighten it and never loosen
it. Absent for a field that cannot be enforced.

source.description: Where the value comes from: `default`, `repository`, or `group:<id>`.

value.description: `disabled`: nobody. `members`: only people who hold a grant on the repository. `everyone`: anyone who can read it.

ForkSettingValue_ForkPolicy.description: One effective fork setting: its value, where it came from — `default`, `repository`, or `group:<id>` — and whether a group above enforces it as a ceiling.

enforced.description:
Whether a group above enforces this field: a scope beneath may tighten it and never loosen
it. Absent for a field that cannot be enforced.

source.description: Where the value comes from: `default`, `repository`, or `group:<id>`.

value.description: `disabled`: never. `organization`: only into, or towards, the repository's own organization. `anywhere`: any group the person may create repositories in, or any repository of the network. A private repository's `anywhere` is `organization`: private code never forks out of its organization.

ForkSettingValue_MaintainerEdits.description: One effective fork setting: its value, where it came from — `default`, `repository`, or `group:<id>` — and whether a group above enforces it as a ceiling.

enforced.description:
Whether a group above enforces this field: a scope beneath may tighten it and never loosen
it. Absent for a field that cannot be enforced.

source.description: Where the value comes from: `default`, `repository`, or `group:<id>`.

value.description: Whether the author of a merge request from a fork may let the people who can merge it push to its source branch.

ForkSettingValue_ProposalRetention.description: One effective fork setting: its value, where it came from — `default`, `repository`, or `group:<id>` — and whether a group above enforces it as a ceiling.

enforced.description:
Whether a group above enforces this field: a scope beneath may tighten it and never loosen
it. Absent for a field that cannot be enforced.

source.description: Where the value comes from: `default`, `repository`, or `group:<id>`.

value.description: How many days a closed or merged merge request's proposed commits are kept: 7 to 365, or "forever".

ForkSettingValue_ProposalRunPolicy.description: One effective fork setting: its value, where it came from — `default`, `repository`, or `group:<id>` — and whether a group above enforces it as a ceiling.

enforced.description:
Whether a group above enforces this field: a scope beneath may tighten it and never loosen
it. Absent for a field that cannot be enforced.

source.description: Where the value comes from: `default`, `repository`, or `group:<id>`.

value.description: `approve_each_head`: run nothing until a Developer approves that exact commit. `run_untrusted`: run every such head at once, without secrets — spending the repository's minutes on every contribution.

ForkSettingsView.description: The effective fork policy: every field as it applies here, with where it came from.

allow_maintainer_edits.description: Whether authors may let its mergers push to their source branch.

closed_proposal_retention_days.description: How long a closed proposal's commits are kept.

fork_merge_requests.description: Who may open a cross-repository merge request into it.

forking.description: Who may fork, and where to.

outbound_merge_requests.description: Which targets it may propose to.

override_group_settings.description:
For a repository: whether its own row counts. A repository's settings apply only while this
is on.

proposal_runs.description: What its pipelines do with a proposal head nobody vouched for.

ForkSort.description: `newest`: most recently forked first. `recently_pushed`: most recently changed first. `most_starred`: most stars first.

ForkState.description: `copying`: the upstream's branches and tags are still being copied, and the fork serves nothing yet. `ready`: the copy is complete. `failed`: the copy stopped for good; `failure` says why.

ForkStayingVisible.description: A fork of this repository, in the same organization, that stays more visible than this repository will be. It holds this repository's history as of its last sync.

can_narrow.description: Whether you may change this fork's visibility, so that `narrow_forks` narrows it too.

visibility.description: The fork's visibility, which stays as it is unless `narrow_forks` narrows it.

ForkSummary.description: A fork you can see. In a network listing, its upstream and depth are named only where you can see the upstream.

ahead.description: As of `as_of`: commits the tracked branch has that its upstream branch lacks.

behind.description: As of `as_of`: commits the upstream branch has that the tracked branch lacks.

depth.description: Forks between this one and the root, when you can see its upstream.

kind.description: Whether the fork is bound to the code it came from or independent of it.

stars.description: How many people starred the fork.

oneOf.description: The fork's upstream, when you can see it.

ForkSyncResult.description: What a sync did — or, for a dry run, would do.

after_sha.description: Where it is now — or would be.

ahead.description: Afterwards: commits the fork branch has that the upstream branch lacks.

behind.description: Afterwards: commits the upstream branch has that the fork branch lacks.

commits_brought_in.description: Upstream commits the fork branch now has.

commits_discarded.description: The fork's own commits a `reset` discarded.

discarded.description: For a dry run of a `reset`: the commits it would discard, newest first, at most fifty.

dry_run.description: Whether this was a dry run, which moved nothing.

mode.description: How the upstream branch was brought in.

ForkTrackingView.description: How far the fork's tracked branch is from its upstream branch, as of the last refresh — never computed on a read.

ahead.description: Commits the fork branch has that the upstream branch lacks.

behind.description: Commits the upstream branch has that the fork branch lacks.

oneOf.description: The fork branch that follows the upstream.

sync_available.description: Whether a sync could run now.

sync_unavailable_reason.description: Why not, when it could not.

oneOf.description: The upstream branch it follows.

upstream_sha.description: The upstream commit the counts were taken against.

ForkUpstreamRef.description: The repository a fork was created from, as far as you can see it: `visible: false` names nothing, because the upstream is a repository you cannot see.

deleted.description: `true` once the upstream has been deleted; the fork stays, and says so.

oneOf.description: The upstream's current path, when you can see it.
The upstream's id, when you can see it.

visible.description: Whether you can see the upstream. When `false`, nothing else about it is named.

ForkView.description: A repository's fork relationship: where it came from, how it is bound, how far it has drifted. A repository you cannot see is named only as `{ "visible": false }`.

bound_to.description:
The repositories its code belongs to — empty for an independent fork — each as far as you
can see it.

oneOf.description: Who forked it.

detach_closes_merge_requests.description:
On a detach preview only: how many open merge requests between this fork and the rest of
its network — from it, and into it from other forks — the detach would close.

oneOf.description: Why the copy failed, when it did.

purpose.description: An ordinary fork, or a private fix fork.

relationship.description: Whether it still follows its upstream.

upstream.description: What it was forked from, as far as you can see.

viewer.description: What you may do with it.

visibility_ceiling.description: The most visible the fork may ever be.

ForkViewerView.description: What you may do with this fork.

can_detach.description: You may detach it from its upstream.

can_enable_pipelines.description: You may turn its pipelines on.

can_sync.description: You may sync it from its upstream.

FreshSignIn.description: Whether the sign-in in use is recent enough to close the account.

max_age_seconds.description: How recent a sign-in must be, in seconds.

satisfied.description:
Whether you signed in within `max_age_seconds`. When not, sign in again — closing is
refused with `REAUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` until you do.

GateApprovers.description: Who decides one gate. A gate the revision names nobody for is decided by the board.

users.description: The people who decide it. Each still needs `ai_org.approve` on the organization's root group.

GateNote.description: What the person deciding a gate writes for the agent, at most 2,000 characters.

GateOverride.description: One gate set off its level's preset.

setting.description: What it does at this organization: allow, notify or ask.

GateSetting.description:
What a gate does when its action comes up, from strictest to loosest: wait for a person, go
ahead and tell the approvers, or go ahead.

GovernanceReason.description: Why it was done, in 1 to 500 characters — kept with the record of it.

GrantOutcomeView.description: What became of one grant in an explanation.

GrantRoute.description: How a grant reaches the explained principal.

oneOf.description: The grant names them.
They are a member of the team the grant names.

team.description: They are a member of the team the grant names.

GraphSource.description: Where a run's steps came from: `stored`, resolved by the platform from a saved pipeline, or `caller`, supplied in the request that started the run. Set by the platform whatever a request says. A run whose steps the caller supplied proves nothing about work items' acceptance criteria and never counts toward a merge request's pipelines.

GrepMatch.description: One matching line in a content search.

after.description: The lines just after the match, in file order.

before.description: The lines just before the match, in file order.

line.description: The line number of the match, counting from 1.

path.description: The file the match is in, relative to the repository root.

text.description: The matching line. A very long line is shortened and ends with `…`.

GrepResponse.description:
The answer to a content search: the matching lines at one commit, each with the lines around
it.

matches.description: Matching lines, grouped by file in path order and by line within a file.

sha.description: The commit that was searched. Repeating the search at this commit returns the same lines.

truncated.description:
The search stopped before it finished — it reached its match limit, its size limit or its
time limit. More matches may exist; narrow the search with a path or a more specific
pattern to see them.

GroupCodeSearchStatus.description: A subtree's coverage, as far as the caller can read.

excluded.description: The readable repositories left out, at most 100, by path.

oneOf.description: The organization's totals: at a top-level group, for a caller holding `billing.view` there.

repositories.description: The readable repositories beneath the group, by state.

GroupSpecStatus.description:
A summary of the specs across a group and its subgroups. It counts only repositories you can
see.

Handoff.description:
An agent leaving the organization hands its open work to another: which one, by key. Read by
the publish that retires `from`. **Structural.**

to.description: The agent of this revision that takes its open work.

HeldName.description: A name held back after its group is deleted.

name.description: The name.

until.description:
Until when nobody can take it. Absent when it is held for good, because a repository in the
group was public or a package was published in it.

InheritanceAuditChange.description: A scope's inheritance switched, for the audit record.

start_line.description:
For a comment on a range, its first line; `old_line` or `new_line` is its last. Absent for
a comment on one line.

oneOf.description: The side of the diff `start_line` is on.

InsightBucket.description: One bucket of the series. Every field is the bucket's own total, not a running one.

InsightMeans.description:
Averages over the window, in seconds. These are means, not medians. Each is absent when there
was nothing to measure.

InsightTotals.description: One scope's throughput totals over the window.

active_contributors.description: How many different people and service accounts contributed in the window.

acknowledge_unverified.description:
Must be `true` to install a Community/Private (unverified) provider — the
per-install trust acknowledgement. Ignored for Platform/Verified.

oneOf.description: The versions a node may declare. Absent ⇒ `AnyPublished`.

track_latest.description:
Opt this install into tracking the provider's latest published version
(unpinned nodes auto-advance). Absent ⇒ pin the resolved `version`.

oneOf.description:
Becomes the scope's `default_version`. Defaults to the provider's
`latest_version` when omitted.

IntakeRefusal.description: Why a proposed update was refused, by commit and file. A refusal never quotes what it refused: one about a credential names its format, the commit, the file, the line and the id of the file's content, and nothing more.

examples.message: Line 12 of `config/deploy.env` in commit 9fceb02d0ae5 matches the format of an AWS access key ID. If it is one, revoke it and rewrite the branch without it; if it is not, acknowledge this file on the merge request to let it through.

blob.description: The id of that file's content. For a credential, it is what acknowledging the file names.

commit.description: The commit the refusal is about, when it is about one.

oneOf.description: The credential format the line matched — never the line itself.

line.description: The line of that file, for a credential.

message.description: What was refused and what to do about it, in words.

path.description: The file the refusal is about, when it is about one.

rule.description: The rule that refused the update.

IntakeRule.description: Which rule refused a proposed update. `update_size`: the update brought more new data than one update may. `proposal_size`: the merge request's proposed versions would hold more than one merge request may. `author_budget`: the author's open merge requests into the repository would hold more than one author may. `repository_budget`: the repository holds as much as it accepts from people without Developer access to it. `purged_commits`: the branch still contains a commit of a version that was purged. `file_size`: a file is larger than the repository accepts. `prohibited_name`: a commit adds or changes a file whose name the repository does not accept. `credentials`: a line a commit adds matches the format of a credential. `too_large_to_check`: the update is too large to be checked.

InvoiceStatus.description:
Stripe invoice status, mirrored. A thin projection value — gitmoap never
computes it, only records what Stripe reports.

InvoiceView.description: The customer-facing invoice view — scalars plus the two Stripe-hosted links.

Issue.description:
A work item — an epic, story, bug, task or other tracked piece of work — living in a group or a
repository.

ancestor_group_ids.description: The groups the item sits beneath, nearest first.

ancestor_issue_uids.description:
The item's ancestors' permanent identifiers, nearest first, for display. It can briefly lag
behind a change of parent higher up the chain.

assignee_ids.description: The people assigned to the work item. Absent when nobody is.

assignees.description:
The assignees, named. Filled by the reads of one work item; empty on a listing's rows, which
carry `assignee_ids` alone.

author_can_push.description:
Whether the author can push to where this work item lives — its repository, or a group
work item's group. False for a drive-by contributor's text. Absent where it was not
computed.

oneOf.description: Who closed it, named. Filled by the reads of one work item.

created_by.description: Who created the work item, as they were when they created it.

oneOf.description: The iteration the work item is in, named and dated. Absent when it is in none.

The iteration the work item is in — one of its own group's, or of a group above it. Absent
when it is in none.

labels.description: The keys of the labels applied to the work item. Absent when it has none.

oneOf.description:
Whether the item's milestone belongs to a group or a repository — not necessarily the
item's own, since a group milestone can hold work items from several repositories.
The parent's current address, for display. Absent when the item has no parent.
The parent work item's permanent identifier, if the item has a parent.

The commit whose evidence proved the regression — the first known bad commit, and the
upper end of the range of suspect commits.

The commit at which the item was last verified, kept when it regresses — the last known
good commit.

root_scope_id.description: The top-level group the item's group or repository belongs to.

scope_type.description:
Whether the item lives in a group or a repository. With `scope_id` and `iid` it forms the
item's current address — the `#412` a person types — which changes when the item moves.

status_category.description:
The fixed category of the item's current status, which boards, filters and progress
rollups work from.

oneOf.description:
The custom type this item was filed as, pointing at the group or repository where the
blueprint is defined. `work_item_type` still decides where the item may live, its children
and its fields; the blueprint adds a display label and facets. Absent for an item filed as
a plain built-in type.

uid.description:
The work item's permanent identifier. Unlike its number, it never changes, even when the
item moves to another group or repository.

updated_at.description: When the work item last changed, ISO 8601. Listings order by it, newest first.

oneOf.description: The commit at which CI proved the acceptance criteria. Absent until a pipeline run has.

version.description:
The work item's revision, incremented on every change. Send it back with an update; if the
item has changed since you read it, the update is refused with a `409`.

IssueActivity.description: One entry in a work item's timeline. The timeline moves with the work item.

scope.description:
The group or repository the item lived in when this happened. Together with `iid` it is the
item's address at that time, and a later move does not change it.

IssueActivityType.description:
What happened, in one entry of a work item's timeline. Deleting a work item deletes its timeline,
so there is no entry for a deletion.

content_digest.description:
A SHA-256 digest of the region's lines with formatting normalised, identifying its content
rather than its position, so reformatting the code does not count as changing it.

drift_score.description:
Similarity of the region's content at `resolved_at_sha` to its content at
`pinned_at_sha`, in `[0, 1]`. `1.0` while the region is byte-identical.

oneOf.description:
The last commit that changed the anchored region itself — unlike `resolved_at_sha`, which
advances on any push that touches the file.

last_transport_at.description:
When the last push the anchor was followed through was made. Absent until a push has moved
it.

path.description: The region, in the coordinates of `pinned_at_sha`.

pinned_at_sha.description:
The commit the pinned `path` and line range refer to. With them it forms a permanent link to
the code as it was pinned, and it never changes.

resolved_at_sha.description: The default-branch commit that `resolved_path` and the resolved line range refer to.

IssueAnchor.description:
A work item pinned to a region of code. The platform follows the region as later pushes to the
default branch move or change it, and reports where it is now and how much it has changed.

IssueAnchorLink.description:
An anchor, as seen from its work item: which anchor, in which repository, and the file it
currently points into.

IssueAnchorMetadata.description: The `metadata` an anchor event and its timeline activity carry.

oneOf.description: The file the anchor was in before this change, when it moved. Absent on creation.
Why an orphan is an orphan.

IssueBranchCreatedMetadata.description: A branch was created for this work item.

IssueCard.description:
A work item as a board or backlog shows it: the item with its author, assignees, labels,
milestone, children's progress and counts resolved.

author_can_push.description:
Whether the author can push to where this work item lives — its repository, or a group
work item's group. False for a drive-by contributor's text. Absent where it was not
computed.

blocked_by.description:
How many **open** work items block this one. A count, never an identity: a blocker the
caller cannot see still blocks, and naming it would leak the private item's existence.

children.description: The progress of the item's children. All zeros when it has none.

oneOf.description: The iteration the work item is in, named and dated. Absent when it is in none.

IssueChildLink.description: A child of a work item, with the fields its parent's progress is computed from.

child_ref.description: The child's current address: the group or repository it lives in, and its number there.

status_category.description: The status category the child is in.

IssueCommentMetadata.description: A comment, or a transition of the thread it roots.

agent_mentions.description:
The agents of the work item's organization the comment `@`-mentioned. Absent when it
mentions none.

mentions.description:
The people and service accounts the comment `@`-mentioned, as they were identified when it
was written. Absent when it mentions nobody.

IssueCommitLinkMetadata.description: The details of a commit message referencing the work item.

branch.description: The branch the commit landed on. Whether it closes anything is decided from this.

repository_id.description:
The repository the commit is in — not necessarily the work item's own, since an epic lives
in a group and is referenced from many repositories.

IssueCommitView.description: A commit whose message names the work item, with the commit itself.

oneOf.description:
The commit. Absent in the rare case it can no longer be read from the repository; the
link and its SHA remain.

repository_id.description:
The repository the **commit** is in — which is not necessarily the work item's own. An
epic lives in a group and is named from many repositories.

IssueFacetCount.description: One value of a facet and how many work items carry it.

count.description: How many work items the listing's other filters keep that carry it.

oneOf.description:
What the assignee is — a person, a service account or an agent — on the assignee facet, so
a client links each to the right page.

name.description: The assignee's username, on the assignee facet.

value.description:
The value: a status category, a label key, or an assignee's principal id — `none` for the
work assigned to nobody.

IssueFacets.description:
How a work-item listing's filters divide: the work items they keep, and per value of each facet
how many the *other* filters keep — so a filter bar can say what choosing a value would leave.

assignee.description: Per assignee, most first; `none` is the work assigned to nobody.

total.description: How many work items every filter keeps.

IssueIterationOutcome.description: What happened to one work item of a many-item change.

IssueIterationResult.description: One work item's answer in a many-item change.

oneOf.description:
Why it was refused — the error a request for this one item alone would have answered.
Absent unless `outcome` is `refused`.

item.description: The work item, as the request named it.

IssueLabel.description: A label definition, scoped to a group or a repository.

examples.description: Card payments: authorization, capture and refunds

title.description: Its display name, free to change; absent when it shows its key.

IssueMrLinkMetadata.description: The details of a merge request referencing the work item.

IssueMrView.description: A merge request a work item is linked to, as a reader wants it.

closing.description:
Whether the merge request says it finishes the work item (`Closes #412`) rather than
merely mentioning it. Merging a closing merge request closes the item.

repository_id.description: The repository the **merge request** is in.

IssueQuickActionDeniedMetadata.description: The details of a quick action in a commit message being refused.

reason.description: Why it was refused — whether the commit's author or its pusher lacked the access it needs.

IssueRef.description: Names a work item from outside its own repository or group, since a number like `#412` only identifies an issue within one of them.

IssueRelationView.description:
A relation, with the work item at the other end summarised. A relation whose other end you
cannot see is left out entirely, so its existence is not disclosed.

IssueRollup.description:
A work item's progress, computed from its children. It counts only the children you can see,
and reports no hidden total.

completed.description:
Children in the `done` category only. A cancelled child is closed but not completed, and is
counted in `cancelled`.

IssueTransitionSkippedMetadata.description: The details of an automatic status change that the workflow's transition rules forbade.

IssueVerificationResponse.description: The Proof-of-Done view: every criterion, its state, and the evidence that produced it.

facets.description:
The criteria grouped by blueprint facet, each with its overall state. Absent for an item
filed as a built-in type; present for one filed as a custom type.

name.description: Its name, 1–80 characters.

position.description: Its place in its owner's list, from 0.

IssueViewId.description: The identifier of a saved work-item view.

IssueViewScope.description: Where a saved view looks: a repository or a group by id, or the owner's own work.

id.description: The repository's or group's id; absent for `mine`.

Iteration.description:
A dated container of work in a group, such as a sprint. Work items from the group and from any
repository beneath it can be put in it.

oneOf.description:
The cadence that generated it. Absent for an iteration created by hand, and for one whose
cadence was deleted.

description.description: What it is for, in Markdown. Absent when it has none.

sequence.description:
Its position in the cadence that generated it, counted from 1. Absent for an iteration
created by hand.

state.description: Whether it is upcoming, current or closed today, read from its dates — never stored.

IterationBurndown.description:
An iteration's burndown: one entry per day from its first day to its last, or to today while it
runs, replayed from its work items' timelines.

Only work items you can read are counted. Points are each item's estimate as it is now: changing
an estimate moves the whole line.

days.description: One entry per day, earliest first. Empty before the iteration starts.

truncated.description:
Whether more than 2,000 work items were ever in it, so the figures count only the first
2,000.

IterationCadence.description: A schedule that generates a group's iterations, keeping the next few always created.

active.description: Whether it generates iterations. A paused cadence generates nothing and keeps what it made.

at_limit.description:
Whether its group holds as many iterations as its plan allows, so nothing it owes can be
created until an iteration is deleted or the limit is raised.

cool_down_weeks.description:
Weeks left between one iteration's end and the next one's start, which belong to no
iteration: 0 to 4. Shape Up's cool-down between cycles.

duration_weeks.description: How long each iteration runs, in weeks: 1 to 12.

first_start_date.description:
The date the schedule starts from. The first iteration begins on the first `start_day` on or
after it.

followed_by_ai_organization.description:
Whether the group's AI organization runs its cycles on it — its live revision names it in
`calendar.cycle_cadence`. Such a cadence can be neither paused nor deleted.

generated_through.description: The number of the last iteration it has generated, or 0 before the first.

group_id.description: The group whose iterations it generates.

iterations_in_advance.description: How many upcoming iterations are kept created ahead of today: 1 to 12.

owed.description:
How many iterations it owes today and has not created: its group is at its iteration limit,
or the daily generator has yet to run. 0 when it is up to date, and while it is paused.

start_day.description: The weekday every iteration begins on.

title.description: Its title. Each iteration it generates is titled with it and the iteration's number.

IterationId.description: The identifier of an iteration — a dated container of work in a group, such as a sprint.

from_iteration_id.description: The iteration the work came from. Its completed and cancelled work stays in it.

moved.description: How many open work items moved — those you can read.

not_visible.description:
How many open work items stayed in the iteration because you cannot read them: work from a
repository or group you have no access to is left for somebody who has.

to.description: The iteration the open work went to.

IterationRollup.description: How an iteration is going, from the work items in it that you can see.

carry_over.description:
What carries over: the work items still open, which would carry into the next iteration if
this one ended now, and those already rolled over out of it, which did.

carry_over_points.description: The points of what carries over — of an item rolled over, the points it left with.

committed_points.description: The points of every work item in it that is not cancelled — what the iteration took on.

completed_points.description: The points of its completed work items.

IterationState.description: Where an iteration is in time, read from its dates against today.

IterationSummary.description:
An iteration as a work item and its card name it: enough to show it and link to it.

Served to anyone who can read the work item, wherever the iteration's group sits — which
iteration an item is planned in is a fact about the item, and its timeline records the same
title.

group_id.description: The group it belongs to — the item's own group, or one above it.

state.description: Whether it is upcoming, current or closed today, read from its dates.

IterationTitle.description: An iteration's title, such as Sprint 24: 1 to 255 characters, with no control characters.

IterationView.description:
An iteration and how it is going. The figures count only the work items you can see: an
iteration may hold work from several repositories, and access to one of them reveals nothing
about the others.

JoinableIterationGroup.description: A group whose iterations a work item can join.

full_path.description: Its full path, from the top-level group down.

JoinableIterations.description:
The iterations a work item in a repository or group can join: those of its own group and of
every group above it that you can read.

An iteration of a group above it that you cannot read is left out, though a work item can
still be put in one by someone who can.

groups.description:
The groups whose iterations are listed, nearest first: the work item's own group, then each
group above it that you can read.

truncated.description: Whether more iterations matched than one answer holds; narrow it with `state`.

Jwk.description:
A single RSA public key in JWK form (RFC 7517), published so a relying party
can verify gitmoap-minted OIDC tokens.

kid.description:
The key's id, equal to the `kid` header of the tokens it signs, so a relying party picks the
right key while keys are being rotated.

Jwks.description: JSON Web Key Set (RFC 7517) — one JWK per active signing-key version.

LandPrivateFixRequest.description: Land a private fix: merge the fix fork's merge request into this repository's branch it mirrors, judged by this repository's rules, publishing nothing before the branch moves. The merge request recorded here carries the title and description given, not the private review's.

examples.description: Requests whose Authorization header exceeds 8 KiB are refused before parsing.
examples.title: Reject oversized authorization headers

oneOf.description:
Its description, written for this repository's readers. The private review's stays in the
fix fork.

expected_head_sha.description:
The head of that merge request you reviewed. The landing is refused if its branch has moved
since.

merge_request_id.description:
The number of the fix fork's merge request to land — one of the fix fork's own, into the
branch that mirrors this repository's.

squash.description:
Land the fix as one commit. Defaults to `true`, so the fix's working history stays in the
fix fork.

title.description: The title of the merge request recorded here, written for this repository's readers.

LanguageSlice.description: One language's share of a breakdown.

bytes.description: Bytes attributed to this language. Authoritative; `share` is a convenience.

color.description: The CSS colour upstream renders this language with, when it defines one.

language.description: The language's name, as the vocabulary spells it.

type.description: `programming` or `markup` — the only two kinds that reach a breakdown.

LanguageSource.description: Where one contributing repository's half of a service breakdown came from.

repository_id.description: The repository whose paths this service binds.

truncated.description: Whether that repository's index is truncated.

LargeChangeThreshold.description:
The size above which an agent's change raises `large_change`: more changed lines, or more files,
than these. **Ordered** (lower is stricter).

version.description: The version accepted.

LegalAcceptanceMoment.description: Where an acceptance was asked for.

LegalAcceptances.description: The versions of legal documents you have accepted, newest first.

items.description: Each version you accepted, newest first.

kind.description: Whether it is an email address or a page.

label.description: What the Entity Details call it.

contact_languages.description: The languages the points of contact answer in.

contacts.description: The means of contact, as the Entity Details state them today.

documents.description: Every document with a published version. Empty until the first publication.

stage.description:

set.description: `true` when the limit was set, `false` when it was removed.

LimitIncreaseRequestView.description: Wire view of a limit-increase request.

LimitKey.description:
A recognised limit name — every `PlanLimits` cap plus the user-scoped
`max_root_groups`. The identity a limit-increase request and a
namespace override are keyed by.

LimitName.description: Which limit a usage-and-limits entry describes.

LimitRequestStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a limit-increase request. `Applied` is the terminal success
state (the override was written); `Approved` exists for symmetry but the
approve path applies immediately, so a persisted request is never left
`Approved`-but-not-`Applied`.

LimitScope.description:
What a per-resource limit applies to — each repository, each merge request, each team, and so
on. Usage against it is reported on that resource, not in the organization-wide view.

LimitSubjectEntry.description: Whom a limit caps, as a response shows it.

oneOf.description: The explained principal, by name.
A team the explained principal is a member of.

team.description: A team the explained principal is a member of.

oneOf.description: Everyone.
Every service account.
Every agent of an AI organization.

LimitWarning.description: Something worth knowing about a limit that did not stop it being set.

LinkTeamIdpGroupRequest.description: Mirror a team's roster from a group in the organization's identity provider.

idp_group.description: The group's name as the identity provider's groups claim spells it.

The earlier texts, oldest first; empty for a message never edited, or one deleted — a
deletion removes every earlier text with the message's own.

next_token.description: Pass as `next_token` for older messages; absent on the oldest page.

redirected_from.description:
With `name`: the name asked for, when no channel holds it and the channel answered was
renamed from it. A renamed channel keeps its old names, so an address written before the
rename still leads to it, and no other channel of the group may take them.

total.description:
Every contributor the repository has, not just this page — what a sidebar
renders as "N contributors" without walking the pages.

ListEnvironmentVariablesResponse.description: An environment's variables, with the limits that apply to them.

items.description: The variables, by name. A secret's value is never returned.

limit.description: How many variables the environment may hold.

max_value_bytes.description: The longest value a variable may hold, in bytes.

next_token.description: Never set: an environment's variables fit on one page.

items.description: The forks on this page.

next_token.description: Pass it back as `next_token` for the next page. Absent on the last page.

ListInvoicesResponse.description: Paginated list of a namespace's invoices, newest first.

ListIssueViewsResponse.description: A person's saved views, in their order.

items.description: The views.

ListMrParticipantsResponse.description:
Unpaginated by design: a merge request's participant set is bounded, and a
cursor over it would be ceremony with nothing to page.

ListNodeRunsResponse.description: A page of a pipeline run's steps.

commit_sha.description: The commit the ref pointed at; every pipeline in the listing was read there.

items.description: One page of the pipelines, in name order.

next_token.description: Where the next page starts; absent on the last page.

ref.description: The full ref the pipelines were read at.
