items.description: One line of a feed.

oneOf.description: Who did it. Absent when the platform did — a pipeline nobody triggered, a scheduled action.

metadata.description: Bounded free-form detail; the shape varies by `kind` and is documented per event.

occurred_at.description: When it happened. A feed is ordered by this.

items.description: One inbox item, as the API returns it.

oneOf.description: Who caused the item, as they are now. Absent when nobody did, such as for a bookmark.

note.description: Your own note, on a bookmark only.

oneOf.description:
On a notification's item: what the notification is about — its kind and the ids it names
(a ritual run, a gate, a session, a channel message, the organization), never its title.
It says which run an item whose `target` is the organization's group means.

allOf.description:
What is being discussed: a merge request (`repository_id` and `merge_request_id`) or a work
item (`scope` and `issue_uid`).

author_can_push.description:
Whether the author can push to where the discussed merge request or work item lives —
false for a drive-by contributor's text. Absent where it was not computed.

reactions.description: The reactions on the comment, one entry per emoji. `me` says whether you placed it.

examples.body: This retries on every 5xx, not only on gateway timeouts. Should a 502 from the fraud check be retried too?
Reproduced with a 12,500 EUR refund in staging: the fraud check answers after 41 seconds.

items.description: One deploy of one service to one environment, at one commit.

deployment_id.description:
The deployment's id. It is derived from the run, step and attempt that made it, so the same
attempt never records two deployments.

oneOf.description:
The pipeline run that made the deployment. Absent once that run's history has been removed;
the deployment record is kept.

items.description: A deployment in brief, as the deployment board, a service's overview and its history show it.
An environment in brief, as listings and the deployment board show it.

A work item — an epic, story, bug, task or other tracked piece of work — living in a group or a
repository.

ancestor_group_ids.description: The groups the item sits beneath, nearest first.

ancestor_issue_uids.description:
The item's ancestors' permanent identifiers, nearest first, for display. It can briefly lag
behind a change of parent higher up the chain.

assignee_ids.description: The people assigned to the work item. Absent when nobody is.

assignees.description:
The assignees, named. Filled by the reads of one work item; empty on a listing's rows, which
carry `assignee_ids` alone.

author_can_push.description:
Whether the author can push to where this work item lives — its repository, or a group
work item's group. False for a drive-by contributor's text. Absent where it was not
computed.

oneOf.description: Who closed it, named. Filled by the reads of one work item.

created_by.description: Who created the work item, as they were when they created it.

oneOf.description: The iteration the work item is in, named and dated. Absent when it is in none.

The iteration the work item is in — one of its own group's, or of a group above it. Absent
when it is in none.

labels.description: The keys of the labels applied to the work item. Absent when it has none.

oneOf.description:
Whether the item's milestone belongs to a group or a repository — not necessarily the
item's own, since a group milestone can hold work items from several repositories.
The parent's current address, for display. Absent when the item has no parent.
The parent work item's permanent identifier, if the item has a parent.

The commit whose evidence proved the regression — the first known bad commit, and the
upper end of the range of suspect commits.

The commit at which the item was last verified, kept when it regresses — the last known
good commit.

root_scope_id.description: The top-level group the item's group or repository belongs to.

scope_type.description:
Whether the item lives in a group or a repository. With `scope_id` and `iid` it forms the
item's current address — the `#412` a person types — which changes when the item moves.

status_category.description:
The fixed category of the item's current status, which boards, filters and progress
rollups work from.

oneOf.description:
The custom type this item was filed as, pointing at the group or repository where the
blueprint is defined. `work_item_type` still decides where the item may live, its children
and its fields; the blueprint adds a display label and facets. Absent for an item filed as
a plain built-in type.

uid.description:
The work item's permanent identifier. Unlike its number, it never changes, even when the
item moves to another group or repository.

updated_at.description: When the work item last changed, ISO 8601. Listings order by it, newest first.

oneOf.description: The commit at which CI proved the acceptance criteria. Absent until a pipeline run has.

version.description:
The work item's revision, incremented on every change. Send it back with an update; if the
item has changed since you read it, the update is refused with a `409`.

items.description: One entry in a work item's timeline. The timeline moves with the work item.

scope.description:
The group or repository the item lived in when this happened. Together with `iid` it is the
item's address at that time, and a later move does not change it.

items.description:
A work item as a board or backlog shows it: the item with its author, assignees, labels,
milestone, children's progress and counts resolved.

author_can_push.description:
Whether the author can push to where this work item lives — its repository, or a group
work item's group. False for a drive-by contributor's text. Absent where it was not
computed.

blocked_by.description:
How many **open** work items block this one. A count, never an identity: a blocker the
caller cannot see still blocks, and naming it would leak the private item's existence.

children.description: The progress of the item's children. All zeros when it has none.

oneOf.description: The iteration the work item is in, named and dated. Absent when it is in none.

items.description: A commit whose message names the work item, with the commit itself.

oneOf.description:
The commit. Absent in the rare case it can no longer be read from the repository; the
link and its SHA remain.

repository_id.description:
The repository the **commit** is in — which is not necessarily the work item's own. An
epic lives in a group and is named from many repositories.

items.description: A merge request a work item is linked to, as a reader wants it.

closing.description:
Whether the merge request says it finishes the work item (`Closes #412`) rather than
merely mentioning it. Merging a closing merge request closes the item.

repository_id.description: The repository the **merge request** is in.

items.description: One notification sent to you, or held, or not sent — and on which channel.

category.description: What it is about, by kind.

channel.description: Where it was meant to reach you.

digest.description: Whether it was, or will be, sent in your email digest.

link.description: Where in the web app it leads.

next_attempt_at.description: When it is next due, while it is still owed.

sent_at.description: When it reached your inbox or the mail service.

oneOf.description: Why it was not sent, when it was not.

waiting_for_email.description:
An email still owed while this deployment sends no notification email: it waits for email
to start, and is not late.

items.description: The cheap shape a listing renders.

One search result: what it is, where it lives, and enough text to show it. Fetch the resource
itself for everything else.

examples.excerpt: A refund above 10,000 EUR waits on the fraud check and times out after 30 seconds.
examples.title: Refunds over 10,000 EUR time out

excerpt.description: A short excerpt of the matching body, when the kind has one.

fork_of.description:
For a repository that is a fork: the path of the repository it was forked from, when you
can see that repository.

id.description:
The resource's own identifier, as its domain names it (an issue `uid`, a
repository id, a group id, a release `tag_name`).

iid.description:
The per-scope sequential number, for the kinds that have one. A comment carries the number
of the work item or merge request it was written on.

oneOf.description:
For a comment: what it was written on, `issue` or `merge_request`. With `scope` and `iid`
it addresses the thread the comment belongs to.

path.description:
For a spec: the document's file in its repository. For a wiki page: the page's path, which
is what reads it.

rank.description: How well the result matches the query; results are ordered by it, highest first.

oneOf.description:
The group or repository the result belongs to — a service's group, a comment's work item's
or merge request's scope. Absent for a group and a repository, which are one themselves.

items.description:
One entry in the service catalog listing: a service, and how far along the promotion track it
has got.

deployments.description:
At most one entry per tier, ordered `development`, `testing`, `staging`, `production`. Empty
for a `library`, an external service, or anything never deployed.

items.description:
One heading in a spec document. A heading is identified by its `name` and linked to by its
`anchor`; its number, when it has one, is for display only.

parent_ordinal.description: The enclosing block's `ordinal`, not its id — the tree is addressed the way it is read.

items.description: One indexed spec document: its metadata, its counts and the commit it was indexed at.

orphaned_at.description:
When the file stopped being present in the repository. The record is kept rather than
deleted, so an existing link still resolves and tells you it moved.

items.description: An HTTP operation (`METHOD /path`) a spec heading declares.
One problem the spec checker found in a document.

An identifier a spec declares, with how often the rest of the specs cite it. A count of zero
shows a rule nobody refers to.

doc_id.description:
The document declaring the identifier. Absent when that document has been removed; the
identifier is kept and cannot be reused.

items.description: An unresolved question found in a spec — an unchecked checkbox, collected across the repository into one backlog.

One typed entry extracted from a table in a spec document, or one checkbox item. `core` holds
the fields the record's `kind` defines; `extra` holds every other column of the table, as
written.
One cross-reference, and what it resolved to.

ListSsoDomainsResponse.description: The domains an organization has claimed for SSO.

ListSsoObservedGroupsResponse.description: The group names the organization's identity provider has asserted in the last ninety days.
