A repository's or a group's own tag rules, oldest first. A scope holds few, so they are listed
whole.

items.description: The rules, oldest first.

next_token.description: Absent: the rules are listed whole, so there is never a next page.

ListTemplatesResponse.description: The templates of one kind, or of every kind.

ListUsageEntriesResponse.description: A page of ledger entries, newest first.

ListingVersionView.description:
One version of a provider as its marketplace page lists it: its lifecycle, release notes,
signing and whether a software bill of materials is available.

sbom_available.description:
Whether a software bill of materials (SBOM) is available for this version, as it is for
platform and verified providers.

LocalOrigin.description: The repository's own component this step was expanded from, frozen as the commit the run built held it.

blob.description: The blob the component was read at: the exact text that expanded.

inner_node_id.description:
This node's identifier inside the component, before expansion prefixed it with the
instance.

instance_id.description: The component instance in the pipeline the author wrote.

path.description: The component's file — or the first file of its directory — from the repository's root.

LogDropReason.description:
Why lines are missing from a step's log: `backpressure` (the step wrote output faster than it
could be stored) or `upload_failed` (part of the log could not be stored).

LogRecord.description: One line of a step's log, with its position in the log and when it was written.

line.description: Position of this line in the whole log, counting from zero.

timestamp.description: When the line was emitted, RFC 3339.

LogSearchMatch.description: One search hit, addressed by line so the client can jump straight to it.

line.description: Position of the matching line in the whole log.

snippet.description: The matching text, clipped so one enormous line cannot dominate the response.

timestamp.description: When the line was emitted, RFC 3339.

LogStream.description: Which output stream a line of the step's own output came from: `stdout` or `stderr`.

ManualApproval.description:
An approval gate on a step. With no `approvers`, anyone with Developer access to the repository
may decide; a list narrows the decision to the people, teams and roles it names, as they stand
when the approval is given. On a step that deploys to an environment requiring approval, the
list may only name approvers the environment also names.

required.description:
Distinct approvals needed, 1–10. On a gated environment the larger of this and the
environment's own count applies.

MarkChannelReadRequest.description: How far you have read a channel.

seq.description:
The number of the newest root message you have seen. A lower number than one already marked
changes nothing.

marker.description: The marker's text, as it appears in the code — `TODO(#412): retry is not idempotent`.

text_digest.description:
Identifies the TODO or FIXME marker itself, so the same marker is still recognised after the
code around it moves.

MarkerKind.description:
The marker keywords the scanner recognises. **Uppercase only** — `todo:` and `Todo:` are
everywhere in prose, README files and variable names, and lowering the case sensitivity to be
"helpful" is how a scanner becomes a noise generator.

MarketplaceCategoriesResponse.description: Every marketplace category, with how many providers each holds.

MarketplaceProviderCard.description: One provider as it appears in the marketplace grid. The README, examples and changelog are not included — they load with the provider's detail page.

examples.description: Build and manage Docker container images
examples.name: Docker

featured_rank.description:
Where gitmoap features the provider: lower numbers are placed higher. Absent when it is not
featured.

install_count.description:
How many organizations have installed the provider. Absent for providers gitmoap builds
itself.

oneOf.description: Where the latest version is in its life: `active`, `deprecated` or `sunset`.

namespace_verified.description:
Whether the provider's publisher has verified its namespace. `false` for providers gitmoap
builds itself, which have no publisher.

signed.description:
Whether the latest version's images are signed by gitmoap, as platform and verified
providers' are.

MarketplaceSort.description: How the marketplace orders the providers it lists.

MatrixSpec.description:
The dimensions a step's matrix expands over. Every combination of their values becomes one copy
of the step, always in the same order: dimensions sorted by name, values in the order written.

dimensions.description:
Each dimension's name and its list of values. The step's `config` reads the current value
of a dimension with `{"$matrix": "<dimension>"}`.

McpAuditDetail.description:
The agent tool call a request belonged to, when an AI agent made it through the MCP server
rather than calling the API directly. One tool call can make several requests; each is recorded
as itself, and they share a request id.

client.description: The client application the tool call came from, as that application named itself.

oauth_client_id.description:
The app the access token was issued to, when an app connected through sign-in — its own
registered identifier, which, unlike the self-reported client name, the person consented to.

tool.description: The tool whose execution made the request.

MemoryNote.description: What changed in a memory page and why, at most 200 characters.

MemoryText.description: A memory page in Markdown, at most 16 KiB. Empty clears the page.

blocking.description:
Whether this check failing stops the merge. `false` for an advisory check —
`pipeline_stale` and `restack_required` — which reports something worth knowing and never
blocks; `mergeable` is every blocking check passing.

criteria.description:
For `issue_criteria`: every required acceptance criterion of every work item the merge
request closes, where it stands at the head and why.

oneOf.description:
For `issue_criteria`: the check as a whole — `pending` when nothing has failed and a
pipeline is still to finish, so a client can wait rather than report a failure.

evaluated_target_sha.description:
The target tip a `pipeline_stale` run was evaluated against — the evidence the check is
reporting on, so "stale" is inspectable rather than merely asserted.

oneOf.description:
The run a client should be sent to first, when the check read one: for `pipeline_result`
the first pipeline's run not to have passed, else the first; for `pipeline_stale`, the
first stale run.

For `pipeline_result`: the verdict over `pipelines`, the same value
`GET …/merge-requests/{mr_id}/pipelines` reports as `state`. A failed item with no
pipelines is otherwise three different answers — not decided yet, nothing applies, or the
evaluation was refused — and only this and `pipelines_evaluated` tell them apart without
reading `message`.

pipelines.description:
For `pipeline_result`: every pipeline that applies to the merge request's head and where
it stands. For `pipeline_stale`: each one whose run was tested against a target that has
since moved.

pipelines_evaluated.description:
For `pipeline_result`: whether the trigger engine has decided which pipelines apply to the
head. `false` is the few seconds after a push, when the check waits rather than judges.

privileged_paths.description:
For `privileged_paths`: the pipeline definitions, catalog declaration and code-owners files
a merge request from another repository changes, which someone holding
`pipelines.configure` here must approve at its head before it merges.

rules.description:
For the `approvals` check: every approval rule that applies, with each recorded approval and
whether it counts toward that rule.

stack_mr_iid.description:
The iid of the related stack member for the `downstack_unmerged` /
`restack_required` checks.

unverified_criteria.description: The acceptance criteria that are not green at the MR head, for the `issue_criteria` check.

oneOf.description:
When the branches conflict: how many files, whether they can be resolved in the browser,
and whether you may resolve them, with the reason when you may not. Absent when the
branches merge cleanly.

MergeConflicts.description:
A merge request's conflicts, between two heads.

A function of the two heads alone: the same pair always answers the same body, which is what
lets it be cached by them. Whether the caller may resolve them is on `merge-check`.

oneOf.description: Where the two branches diverged; absent when they share no history.

resolvable.description: Whether every conflict can be resolved in the browser. When `false`, `refusal` says why.

oneOf.description:
The head you reviewed. Required on a merge request from another repository, which merges
only while its proposal's current version is still this commit — so what merges is what
you saw. Optional, and checked when given, on a merge request between two branches of
this repository.

examples.description: A timed-out authorization is retried once, with the same idempotency key.
examples.title: Retry card authorizations on gateway timeouts

allow_maintainer_edits.description:
Whether the author lets this repository's mergers push to the source branch — fast-forward
only, while the merge request is open. Always `false` on a merge request between two
branches of this repository.

oneOf.description:
Who opened it, named — a person, a service account or an agent. Absent where a read does not
name it.

author_can_push.description:
Whether the author can push to the repository — false for a drive-by contributor's merge
request. Absent where it was not computed.

oneOf.description: Who closed it, named, once closed without merging.

created_by.description: The person or agent who opened it.

oneOf.description: Who merged it, named, once merged.

For a merge request from another repository: the version of the source branch's commits
this repository holds, which the merge request's diff, commits and pipelines read. Absent
otherwise.

restack_required.description:
Precise restack signal — set when this MR's downstack was squash-merged
(a rebase is genuinely required to drop the duplicated diff). Distinct from
the advisory `commits_behind`. Reset on the MR's next source-advancing write.

oneOf.description:
For a merge request from another repository: where its commits come from — the source
repository as far as you can see it, what opening the merge request published, and where
the proposal stands. Absent on a merge request between two branches of this repository.

The neighbouring merge requests in this stack. Returned when fetching a single merge request,
not in listings.

version.description:
Optimistic-concurrency counter. Bumped on every write; writes condition on
the read value.

MergeRequestCard.description:
A merge request as a list shows it: its main fields, with its author, reviewers, approvals,
comment and thread counts, diff size and merge readiness resolved.

examples.title: Retry card authorizations on gateway timeouts

author_can_push.description:
Whether the author can push to the repository — false for a drive-by contributor's merge
request. Absent where it was not computed.

is_stacked.description:
True when the merge request is part of a stack: an open merge request is based on it, or it
is based on one.

oneOf.description:
Your own review status on the merge request. Present only in the listing of merge requests
awaiting your review.

Where the merge request's pipelines stand at its head: `pending`, `running`, `failed`,
`passed`, or `empty` when no pipeline applies. Present only in a repository's own listing,
whether or not the repository requires the pipelines to pass.

auth_method.description:
How the review was made: through a sign-in session or with an access token. An approval
rule may count only the first.

principal_kind.description:
Whether the reviewer is a person, a service account or an agent. The same as
`reviewer.kind`, which every actor now carries; kept for the clients that read it here.

reviewer.description:
The reviewer — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — joined live from
`principals`, with `reviewer.kind` saying which.

stale.description:
Whether this reviewer's approval predates the current source-branch tip
(i.e. was cast against an older revision). Computed at read time; not
stored. Purely informational — whether staleness blocks a merge is
governed by the approval policy's `reset_on_push`, surfaced per approval
in the merge check.

Always present in responses; it is recomputed on every read.

MergeRequestSource.description:
Where a merge request from another repository proposes its commits from. Every read of such a
merge request carries it.

branch.description: The branch of the source repository the merge request proposes.

cross_repository.description: Always `true`: the commits come from another repository of the same fork network.

published_as.description: What opening the merge request published: the source's path and branch at that moment.

repository.description:
The source repository as far as you can see it: `visible: false` names nothing, and
`deleted: true` says it is gone.

MergeStackFailure.description: The MR that stopped a `merge-stack` run, with the reason it was blocked.

code.description:
The specific refusal's code, when the merge was refused with one — `PIPELINES_NOT_GREEN`,
`MERGE_CONFLICTS` — so a client can tell which gate stopped the stack without reading the
message.

reason.description: A short kind for the failure (e.g. `conflict`, `forbidden`, `bad_request`).

MergeStackResult.description:
The outcome of merging a whole stack from the bottom up. The merge requests in `merged` stay
merged even if a later one fails; merging stops at `failed`, and everything above it is
`skipped`.

MergeStatusSummary.description:
Whether the merge request can be merged right now. Reported only to signed-in callers, since it
depends on who is asking.

MessageAgentLabel.description:
What labels an AI agent's message wherever it renders: the agent's organization and position,
and the session that wrote it (`SEC-AIORG-AI-LABELLED`).

oneOf.description: The agent's position in the organization's live revision, when it still holds one.
The session that wrote the message.

MessageKind.description:
What a message is. People post `message`; an AI agent always says which of its kinds it posts,
so digests can summarize and screens can filter.

MessageTrust.description:
Whether what a message says may wake an agent. A message by someone the organization does not
trust is shown to agents marked untrusted and wakes nothing (`SEC-AIORG-UNTRUSTED-NO-WAKE`).

examples.description: Refunds are available to every merchant.
examples.title: Refunds GA

MilestoneItem.description: A work item in a milestone, with the fields the milestone's burndown is computed from.

issue_ref.description: The work item's current address: the group or repository it lives in, and its number there.

status_category.description: The status category the work item is in.

MilestoneView.description:
A milestone and its burndown. It counts only the work items you can see: a group milestone may
hold items from several repositories, and access to one of them reveals nothing about the
others.

MirrorResult.description: The result of copying a verified provider's images into gitmoap's registry, by capability.

ModelConnectionState.description: Whether the provider accepts a connection's calls.

ModelProvider.description:
Whose account an organization's agents call their models on: gitmoap's own, or the
organization's own account through its model connection. Its tiers follow that provider's
defaults, and every exact model it names must be that provider's.

MonthWeek.description: Which week of the month a monthly ritual falls in.

MoveIssueRequest.description: Move a work item to another scope.

MoveIssueResponse.description:
What a move did. The work item gets a new number in its destination, so the response gives
both its old and new address. Labels and milestones belong to a group or repository, so any
the destination does not define are dropped, and the response lists them.

dropped_labels.description: Labels that existed on the source and are not defined in the destination.

oneOf.description: Set when the item carried a milestone the destination does not define.

new_path.description:
Where the page is moving to. Named `new_path` rather than `path` because the URL already
carries the page's current one, and one name for two addresses is a coin toss for whoever
reads the request.

MrAction.description: Which merge-request transition an evaluation is for.

MrBuildTarget.description:
Which commit a merge-request trigger builds: `merge_result` (the default — the commit merging
would produce) or `source` (the source branch's own tip).

MrLinkKind.description: What a merge request did to the work item it referenced.

MrParticipant.description: Someone involved in a merge request, and every role they hold in it.

oneOf.description:
Absent only for a commit author whose email matches no registered
principal — every other role is a relational reference and always resolves.

roles.description: Sorted and deduplicated, so the response is stable across reads.

MrPipelineEntry.description: One pipeline that applies to a merge request's source head, and where it stands.

oneOf.description: Which commit a merge-request run built: the merge result, or the source branch's tip.

commit_sha.description:
The commit the run built — the merge result or the source tip, per `build` — which is the
commit `approve_pipeline_run` names. Absent when no run has started.

evaluated_target_sha.description: The target branch's tip the run was tested against, for a merge-request run.

oneOf.description:
What started the run: `merge_request` for a run started for this merge request, `push` or
`manual` for a run of the head commit on its own.

The pipeline. Absent for a pipeline only the source branch's file defines — one it adds —
which `pipeline_name`, its file's name, names until the file reaches the default branch.

The run that decides it: the pipeline's latest run that tested the head, preferring one
started for this merge request. Absent when none has started.

Why the pipeline did not start, when it applied and could not — a quota, a definition that
does not resolve, a merge conflict, pipelines switched off. `held` on a merge request from a
fork means it waits, `pending`, for a person to approve running it at this head; `approval`
says who may. Absent when it started or has yet to.

stale.description:
The target branch has moved since the run was tested against it, so its result no longer
describes what will land. Never blocks a merge on its own.

state.description: Where this pipeline stands at the head.

oneOf.description: That run's status.

Whether the run's code was trusted with the repository's connections and secrets. An
`untrusted` run's result was reached without them, and a person approving `commit_sha`
starts a trusted run that replaces it here. Absent when no run has started.

MrPipelineState.description: Where a merge request's pipelines stand at its source head. `pending`: the pipelines for this head have not been decided or started yet. `running`: one is still running. `failed`: one failed, timed out or was cancelled, or applied and could not start. `passed`: every pipeline that applies succeeded. `empty`: no pipeline applies to this head.

MrPipelines.description: A merge request's pipelines at its source head, and whether they let it merge.

allow_without_pipeline.description: Whether a merge request no pipeline applies to may merge (`allow_merge_without_pipeline`).

oneOf.description:
For a merge request from a fork whose head nobody this repository trusts vouched for: what
its pipelines wait for, and who may give it. Absent otherwise.

evaluated.description:
Whether the platform has decided which pipelines apply to this head. Until it has, the
state is `pending` whatever has already run.

oneOf.description:
For a merge request from a fork whose pipelines are held or ran untrusted: the files changed
since the last approved head — or since it left the target branch — that a build runs rather
than reads. Absent otherwise.

passes.description:
Whether the pipelines let the merge request merge. Always `true` when they are not
required.

pipelines.description: Every pipeline that applies to the head.

oneOf.description:
Set when deciding which pipelines apply was itself refused — the change that should have
started them named nobody the platform could act as. Running the pipelines again decides it.

required.description:
Whether the repository requires the pipelines to pass before a merge
(`require_pipeline_success`).

source_runs.description:
For a merge request from a fork: the fork's own runs at the proposed head, when you can see
them. Information about the contributor's own pipelines — never part of `state` or
`passes`.

source_sha.description: The source-branch commit the pipelines were judged at — the merge request's head.

target_sha.description: The target branch's tip now, which a run's `evaluated_target_sha` is compared with.

MrPipelinesApproval.description: What a merge request from a fork's pipelines wait for at its head. Its code ran nowhere with this repository's secrets: a person holding `release_permission` approves running the pipelines at `head_sha` without them, and a person holding `trusted_rerun_permission` approves an untrusted run's re-run with them.

can_approve_trusted_rerun.description: Whether you may approve an untrusted run's trusted re-run.

can_release.description: Whether you may approve running the pipelines at this head.

head_sha.description: The proposed head the approval is of. Send it as `head_sha` to run the pipelines at it.

held.description:
Whether the pipelines wait for that approval before anything runs: this repository asks for
each head from a fork to be approved.

release_permission.description:
The permission a person needs on this repository to approve running the pipelines at this
head, without its secrets.

trusted_rerun_permission.description:
The permission a person needs to approve an untrusted run's re-run with this repository's
connections and secrets.

MrReview.description: A review, with its comments — to its reviewer, its pending ones too.

body.description: Its summary, once submitted with one.

comments.description:
Its comments still pending, oldest first: once submitted they are the merge request's own,
and this is empty.

oneOf.description: What it concluded, once submitted.

MrReviewId.description: The identifier of a review: a reviewer's comments on a merge request, kept to themselves until submitted with a verdict.

MrSourceRun.description: A run of the fork's own pipelines at the merge request's proposed head, in the fork. It shows what the contributor's own pipelines said; this repository's merge check never reads it.

pipeline_name.description: The pipeline's name in the fork.

repository_full_path.description: The fork the run belongs to.

trust.description: Whether the fork trusted the run's code with its own connections and secrets.

MyTeam.description: A team you are on, with your place on it.

MyTeamPage.description: The teams you are on, across every organization.

group.description: The organization, under the name it was given.

oneOf.description: The organization the released name is kept for, if any.

released_name.description: The name it no longer holds, now held back for good.

NamespaceBalance.description:
An organization's balance: what it has paid in advance, what calls in flight hold, and what
can still be reserved.

available_micros.description: What can still be reserved: the balance, less what is reserved, plus any overdraft.

balance_micros.description: Top-ups less settled charges, refunds and chargebacks, in micro-dollars.

frozen.description: Whether a disputed payment has frozen the balance.

NamespaceEgressUsageView.description:
An organization's daily and monthly budgets for data downloaded from gitmoap, and how much of
each is used.

namespace_day.description: The current day's budget for the whole organization.

namespace_month.description: The current month's allowance for the whole organization — what the plan includes.

plan_tier.description: The plan the limit comes from.

NamespaceLimitOverridesView.description:
Read/echo view of a namespace's overrides — the limit-name → value map after
clamping. Served by the admin direct-override endpoint.

overrides.description:
Limit-name → override value (clamped to the ceiling). Absent keys use the
tier default.

NamespaceLimitsView.description:
Every limit in force for an organization, with live usage where it applies. Each `limit` is the
maximum that is actually enforced, so the view always agrees with what a request will hit.

group_counts.description: Group-scoped caps with live counts evaluated on `group_id` itself.

group_id.description: The group the request named; the group-scoped counts are evaluated on it.

root_group_id.description:
The root group the queried group belongs to; namespace usage is reported
for it.

scope_limits.description:
Limits that apply per repository, merge request, issue or operation, with what each applies
to. Usage is reported on each resource.

storage_used_pct.description:
Storage used as a percentage of the limit, rounded, at most 100. Absent when the plan has no
storage limit, which is not the same as 0%.

NamespaceUsageView.description: An organization's current usage of storage and pipelines, against its plan's limits.

pipeline_minutes_this_month.description:
Pipeline minutes used in the current calendar month: the running time of every pipeline
step, added together.

pipeline_runs_this_month.description: Runs started in the current calendar month.

root_group_id.description: The root group the queried group belongs to.

NestedComponentInstance.description:
A component used inside another component. The same as a component instance in a pipeline,
except that `stage_map` maps each slot to a slot of the containing component.

stage_map.description: Binds every slot the referenced component declares to a slot of the **containing** body.

NewChannelVisibility.description: What a person may create: a channel the group reads, or one its members read.

NewTeamMember.description: A person to put on a team as it is created.

Node.description: A step in a stage: one use of a provider capability, with its configuration.

allow_failure.description:
When `true`, this node's failure (a non-zero exit or a timeout, after any
retries) is non-blocking: it does not fail the enclosing stage or the run.
The node's transitive dependents — which can never receive its output —
are skipped, while independent branches and later stages keep running. A
run whose only failures were `allow_failure` nodes finishes
`succeeded_with_warnings`.

oneOf.description:
Holds this step until it is approved. A step deploying to an environment that requires
approval is held as well, whether or not this is set.

changes.description:
Path globs that decide whether this step runs: when none of them matches a path the push
changed, the step is skipped. When absent and `service` is set, the service's own path globs
apply.

config.description:
The step's provider-specific configuration, checked against the capability's
`config_schema` when the run starts.

oneOf.description:
The provider connection to use, by name (e.g. `aws-prod`). When absent, the step uses the
provider's only connection available to the repository, if there is exactly one.

The environment this step deploys to, by slug. It is looked up on the repository and then
on each group above it when the run starts.

Runs this step once for every combination of the named dimensions' values. At most 100
copies.

Keeps this step from running at the same time as any other step, in any of your
organization's pipelines, that names the same resource group — a Terraform state, a shared
staging database, a fragile external sandbox. The `cancel_previous` mode is not accepted here.

The catalog service this step acts on, by slug. Optional when the repository holds exactly
one service, which is then implied; required when it holds more.

An environment whose plain variables this step reads, by slug, without deploying there —
for a build that bakes the environment's settings in. The step receives the environment's
non-secret variables and nothing else: no approval, no lock, no secrets, and no deployment
is recorded. A step may name this or `environment`, not both.

Pins a specific provider version. When absent, the provider's default version for this
repository is used, as it stands when the run starts.

NodeAttemptRecord.description: One earlier attempt of a step that was retried.

NodeFailure.description:
Why a step failed. `kind` names the cause; `command_failed` also carries what the step's
provider said about it.

oneOf.description: Gitmoap could not prepare the step to run.
The step could not be started.
The outputs of the steps before it could not be handed to this one.
The step's configuration refers to a `$from` or `$context` value the run does not have.
The step's secrets could not be read.
The step's provider image could not be downloaded.

The step's provider image did not match the one recorded for its version, so it was not
run.
The step's command exited with a non-zero code.

code.description: The error code the step's provider gave, such as `TESTS_FAILED`.

exit_code.description: The command's exit code, when it is known.

message.description:
What the step's provider said went wrong, on one line of at most 512 bytes, with any
secret it contained redacted.

oneOf.description: The step was ended by a signal before it finished.

signal.description:
The signal's number: `9` is `SIGKILL`, which most often means the step ran out of
memory.

oneOf.description: The step used more memory than it was given.
The step finished, but its outputs could not be saved.
The step finished without writing an output it declares as required.
The step finished, but could not be completed.
The machine running the step was taken out of service while it ran.
The step was stopped before it finished.
The step stopped without saying why.

NodeLogIndexResponse.description: How large a step's log is and whether it is still being written, without returning any of it.

complete.description: Whether the step finished writing its log.

downloadable.description: Whether the whole log can be downloaded as one file.

dropped_lines.description: Lines that could not be stored. Reported so a gap in the log is never silent.

first_timestamp.description: When the first line was emitted, RFC 3339. Absent on an empty log.

last_timestamp.description: When the last line was emitted, RFC 3339. Absent on an empty log.

total_bytes.description: Uncompressed size of the log in bytes.

truncated.description: Whether output collection stopped at this step's log-size ceiling.

NodeLogSearchResponse.description: Where a search term appears in a step's log.

complete.description:
Whether the whole log was searched. `false` when the match limit or the
scan budget stopped it early.

total_lines.description: Lines in the whole log, so a client can show what share was searched.

NodeLogsResponse.description: One page of a step's logs. Every line carries its position in the whole log, so a client can jump anywhere in it without reading what comes before.

first_line.description: Position of the first line in this page.

next_line.description: Line to ask for next, or absent at the end of the log.

total_lines.description: Lines in the whole log — what a scrollbar is sized against.

truncated.description: Whether output collection stopped at this step's log-size ceiling.

NodeOidcFederation.description:
The cloud role a step assumes through OIDC federation, taken from its connection when the run
started. Holds no secrets.

audience.description:
A custom audience for the identity token, when the connection sets one. The standard
audience is `sts.amazonaws.com`.

oneOf.description: The AWS region for the step's calls, when the connection sets one.

role_arn.description: The IAM role the step assumes with `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`.

NodeOrigin.description: The component this step was expanded from, frozen as it was when the run was triggered.

inner_node_id.description:
This node's identifier *inside* the component body — what its author called it, before
expansion prefixed it with the instance.

instance_id.description: The component instance in the pipeline the author wrote.

version.description: The version the instance's reference resolved to.

NodePortSpec.description: One input or output port declaration.

cardinality.description:
How many connections this port accepts (input ports only). A `many` input waits for every
connection feeding it.

oneOf.description: For a `custom` port, the id of the schema it carries (e.g. `aws.ecs.task-definition/v1`).

NodeResourceGroup.description:
A resource group a step holds while it runs, so only one step naming it runs at a time. Unless
`mode` says otherwise, a step queues for the group, for as long as the pipeline's timeout
allows unless `max_wait_seconds` sets a shorter limit.

NodeSizeView.description: The size a step runs at, and what each minute of it counts against the monthly compute minutes.

cpu.description: vCPU, as a step's `cpu` is written: `"0.5"`, `"2"`.

minutes_per_minute.description:
How many compute minutes one minute of this step counts: `0.8` per vCPU plus `0.1` per GiB
of memory, and never less than `0.25`. The default step, one vCPU and 2 GiB, counts `1`.

NodeStatus.description: Where a step has got to.

NodeStatusCounts.description:
How many of a stage's steps are in each status. A status with no steps is left out, so a stage
of four successful steps reads `{"succeeded": 4}`.

NodeStatusEntry.description: One step's current status, in the compact form the status poll returns.

allow_failure.description:
Whether the step is allowed to fail. A failure of such a step does not fail the run, so
show it as a warning.

NodeView.description:
One step of a pipeline run: where it sits in the run, its status and timings, and its earlier
attempts.

allow_failure.description:
The author marked this step as allowed to fail: if it fails or times out, the stage and the
run carry on (the run ends `succeeded_with_warnings`) and only the steps that depend on it
are skipped. Show such a failure as a warning.

capability_id.description: The capability this step runs, as `{provider}:{name}` (e.g. `docker:build`).

error_summary.description:
Why the step failed, skipped, timed out or was cancelled, in a sentence or two. For a step
that failed after it ran, the same text as `failure` describes.

oneOf.description:
Why a step that ran failed, as a cause a client can act on. Absent for a step that
succeeded or never ran.

history.description: Earlier attempts of this step after retries, oldest first.

oneOf.description:
The repository's own component this step was expanded from, when the author wrote an
instance of one (`./<name>`) rather than the step itself.

logs_href.description: Relative URL of this step's logs.

name.description:
The step's display name, as the pipeline's author wrote it when the run started. Empty for
older runs recorded without one; show the capability instead.

oneOf.description:
The component this step was expanded from, when the author wrote a component instance
rather than the step itself. Absent for a step the pipeline declares directly, and for runs
that predate this field.

provider_id.description:
The provider that runs this step (e.g. `docker`), as chosen from the catalog when the run
started.

retry_after.description:
When the platform next checks whether a held step can start, RFC 3339 — the wait timer's
expiry, or the next check of the concurrency lock. Absent when nothing is scheduled,
including while waiting for an approval, which a person gives rather than a clock.

size.description:
The size this step runs at and what a minute of it counts against your organization's
monthly compute minutes.

oneOf.description:
Why a step that has not started is being held: it is waiting for an approval, for an
environment's wait timer, or for another run to release its concurrency lock. Absent for a
step that is simply waiting for the steps before it.

NodeWaitKind.description:
What a step that has not started is waiting for: `approval` (a person has to approve it),
`wait_timer` (an environment's wait timer has not run out) or `concurrency_lock` (another run
holds its concurrency lock).

NotificationCategory.description: What a notification is about, by kind — the categories a person sets preferences for.

NotificationHistoryItem.description: One notification sent to you, or held, or not sent — and on which channel.

category.description: What it is about, by kind.

channel.description: Where it was meant to reach you.

digest.description: Whether it was, or will be, sent in your email digest.

link.description: Where in the web app it leads.

next_attempt_at.description: When it is next due, while it is still owed.

sent_at.description: When it reached your inbox or the mail service.

oneOf.description: Why it was not sent, when it was not.

waiting_for_email.description:
An email still owed while this deployment sends no notification email: it waits for email
to start, and is not late.

NotificationIntentId.description: A notification: one thing a part of Gitmoap decided some people should know about

NotificationMode.description: How a category reaches you on a channel.

NotificationPreference.description: How one category reaches you on one channel.

mode.description: How it reaches you there — your choice, or the category's default.

required.description: Whether the category cannot be turned off.

NotificationPreferenceChange.description: A change to how one category reaches you on one channel.

channel.description: The channel to change it on.

mode.description:
How it should reach you there. `digest` is for email only, and a category that cannot be
turned off takes anything but `off`.

NotificationPreferences.description: Your notification preferences: every category on every channel, and when email may reach you.

email_enabled.description:
Whether this deployment sends notification email. While it does not, notifications reach
you in the app only, and email rows wait (`waiting_for_email` in the history).

preferences.description: One entry per category and channel, whether you have changed it or not.

digest_frequency.description: Whether digests are sent hourly or daily.

digest_hour.description: The local hour, 0 to 23, a daily digest is sent at.

oneOf.description:
Hours in which email waits, unless what it reports cannot be turned off. Absent when email is
never held back.

time_zone.description: The time zone your quiet hours and digest hour are in.

NotificationSubject.description: What a notification is about. `kind` says which, and decides the other fields.

oneOf.description: A gate waiting for, or decided by, its approvers.
An agent's session.
A message in an organization's channel.

channel_id.description: The channel the message is in, which decides who may read it.

oneOf.description: One run of a ritual.
An AI organization as a whole.
One revision of an AI organization — a proposal waiting for its board.
A repository — a fork, about how it follows the repository it was forked from.

A group — the one that held a fork which no longer exists, since nothing of the fork is left
to point at.
A merge request, by the repository it lives in and its number there.

merge_request_iid.description: The merge request's number in that repository.

repository_id.description:
The repository the merge request lives in — for a merge request proposed from a fork,
its target.

NotificationSuppression.description: Why a delivery was not sent.

audience.description: The mail that is no longer sent to you.

redirect_host.description: The host the authorization code is sent to.

resource.description: The service the access is for.

OAuthClientKind.description: Where a client's registration comes from.

OAuthClientView.description:
An app as it describes itself. Its name and logo are its own claim, so they are shown beside
the host it sends the person back to.

OAuthCode.description: The single-use code the provider sent the browser back with.

OAuthError.description: A refusal in the OAuth specification's own shape.

expires_at.description: When the connection lapses unless the app uses it.

redirect_host.description: The host the app's sign-in returns to.

resource_scope_id.description: The group or repository the access is limited to, when it is.

OAuthRequestedScope.description: One scope an app asked for.

bundle.description: The bundle that includes it, when one does.

description.description: What the scope allows, in a sentence.

named_only.description: Never included in a bundle: it is granted only when chosen on its own.

OAuthScopeAccess.description: Whether a scope reads or changes things.

OAuthState.description: The `state` the provider sent the browser back with.

OAuthTokenRequest.description:
The token endpoint's form body: an authorization code to exchange, or a refresh token to
rotate. Unknown parameters are ignored, as the OAuth specification requires.

resource.description: The protected resource the token is for.

scope.description: Space-separated scopes; on refresh, at most the grant's own.

OAuthTokenResponse.description: An issued access token and the refresh token that renews it.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token expires.

scope.description: The scopes the access token carries, space-separated.

OidcConfigRequest.description: OIDC config block on the connection request.

client_secret.description: The client secret. Write-only: it is stored encrypted and never returned.

issuer_url.description: The OIDC issuer URL. Its settings are discovered from `/.well-known/openid-configuration`.

scopes.description: The scopes to request. Defaults to `["openid", "email", "profile"]`.

OidcConfigView.description: A connection's OIDC settings. The client secret is never returned, only whether one is set.

OidcDiscovery.description:
OIDC Discovery metadata (`/.well-known/openid-configuration`). `issuer`
equals the served origin byte-for-byte (relying parties compare it to the
JWT `iss`); `jwks_uri` is `{issuer}/.well-known/jwks.json`.

OidcFederationTarget.description:
The cloud role an OIDC-federated connection assumes, identified by `cloud`. `aws` is the only
cloud supported.

audience.description: The audience of the identity token. Defaults to `sts.amazonaws.com`.

oneOf.description: The AWS region for the provider's calls.

role_arn.description: The IAM role the pipeline assumes.

OnboardingActivation.description:
Advisory activation hints for the getting-started checklist. Fields are
`null` until the personal namespace is provisioned (the readiness gate).

clone_hint.description: A suggested `git clone` command for a new repo in the namespace.

has_access_token.description:
Whether the caller holds any personal access token (a connected git
client).

oneOf.description:
The personal namespace group id — lets the frontend `PUT /groups/{id}`
and target repo creation without a path→id lookup that a mid-Welcome
namespace rename would desync.

personal_namespace_path.description: The personal namespace's current path to clone into.

OnboardingIntent.description:
The person's stated goal, captured by the first-run Welcome.

`Unknown` is the canonical "the Welcome has not been completed" signal — a
fresh record starts here, and the first `PATCH` to `Solo`/`Team` retires the
Welcome. There is deliberately no separate "onboarded" flag.

OnboardingSteps.description: The sparse step map — a timestamp when complete, `null` when pending.

OpenDirectConversationRequest.description: A direct conversation to open with an AI agent.

OrgConfig.description:
An organization's whole configuration: its shape and board, agents, squads, positions,
autonomy, budgets, models, tracker, who may wake an agent, how pipelines treat agent-written
code, its calendar, how its agents talk, its rituals and the handoffs of agents it retires.

calendar.description: The organization's time zone and cycles.

handoffs.description: Where the open work of the agents this revision retires goes.

model_provider.description:
Whose account the organization's models are called on. **Pinned.** Left out of the stored
body while it is gitmoap's own, so a body that names none keeps its digest.

positions.description: The positions under the organization's own names, and their defaults.

rituals.description:
The organization's rituals (`rituals.md`). Adding or removing one is **structural**; its
content is **pinned**; its budget is **ordered**.

OrgMessageId.description: A channel message's id. Time-ordered: a later message has a greater id.

OrgPeoplePage.description: Everyone with access in an organization, longest-standing first.

OrgPerson.description: A person or service account with access somewhere in the organization.

grant_count.description: How many grants name them directly, anywhere in the organization.

joined_at.description: When they were first given access here.

last_exercised_at.description: When any of their access here last let them do something, to the day.

oneOf.description: Their role at the top-level group, when a grant there names them directly.

teams.description: The organization's teams they are on.

OrgPersonKind.description: How someone belongs to an organization.

OrgStructure.description: `structure` — the shape and the board, the people above every agent. **Structural.**

board.description: Besides the root group's Owners, who are always on it.

OrganizationOwners.description: The organization's owners, who reach everything whatever the page lists.

listed.description:
Whether their grants appear among the entries. They do not when this group or repository
stops inheriting access, yet the owners reach it all the same.

OrphanAction.description: What happens to the *work item* when its anchor is orphaned.

OwnerRef.description:
Who owns a service: a group, a team, or a person or service account. A service may also have no
owner, which the `has_owner` scorecard check surfaces.

oneOf.description: A team of the organization — the people on it, whoever they are this afternoon.

organization.description: The full path of the organization's top-level group, such as `acme`.

PackageDetail.description: A package and its versions, newest first.

PackageRegistryFormat.description: The package ecosystem a registry speaks. A group has at most one registry per format.

PackageVersionView.description: One published version of a package.

size_bytes.description: The size of the version's files, in bytes.

yanked.description:
Whether the version has been yanked, as a Cargo crate version can be. Always `false` for npm
and PyPI.

PackageView.description: A package in one of a group's registries, as a package listing shows it.

latest_version.description: The newest version, when there is one.

name.description: The package's name, as it was published.

total_bytes.description: The size of every file of every version, in bytes.

ParamSpec.description: What a manual trigger may be asked for: one declared parameter.

default.description: Used when the caller supplies nothing.

description.description: Shown next to the field when a person starts the run.

name.description:
How the parameter is addressed — in the trigger request body, and as the tail of a
`{"$context": "params.<name>"}` reference.

options.description:
When non-empty, the only values accepted — a fixed choice rather than free text. Applies to
`string` parameters; values are compared exactly.

required.description:
Whether a run may start without it. A required parameter with a `default` is satisfied by
that default, so the two are not in conflict.

type.description: The type a supplied value must have: `string` (the default), `number` or `boolean`.

ParamType.description: The type of a declared parameter's value: `string`, `number` or `boolean`.

ParticipantRole.description: How someone came to be a participant. One person commonly holds several.

PatchOnboardingRequest.description:
The `PATCH /user/onboarding` body — the only user-writable fields. Absent
fields are unchanged.

PendingLegalAcceptance.description: A document you have yet to accept, at the version you are asked to.

change_summary.description:
What changed since the version before it, as its publisher summarised it. None for a first
version.

effective_date.description: The day it takes effect, in UTC.

gates.description: Whether, until you accept it, your changes are refused. Reading always stays open.

introduces_charge.description: Whether it introduces a charge, which is only ever accepted expressly and never blocks you.

takes_effect_in_future.description: Whether it has yet to take effect: it can be accepted now, before it binds.

version.description: The version to accept.

PendingLegalAcceptances.description: The documents you have yet to accept.

items.description: Each document to accept. Empty when you owe nothing.

PercentileSurface.description: Exact p50/p95 over a bounded window, with the evidence behind them.

p50_seconds.description:
The median, in seconds. Absent when the window held nothing to measure — which is different
from a median of zero.

truncated.description:
Whether the window held more than 20,000 measurements, in which case the percentiles are
computed over 20,000 of them and `n` is that limit rather than the full count.

PermissionAppliesAt.description: Where a grant carrying a permission has any effect.

lowest_builtin_role.description:
The lowest built-in role that holds this permission. Every higher built-in role holds it
as well.

public_readable.description:
Whether a Public or Internal group or repository lets people read this without being
given access.

requires.description: The permissions this one is meaningless without. A role that holds it holds these too.

PermissionTier.description: How dangerous granting a permission is, which decides whether a custom role may carry it.

PermissionVerdict.description: The answer for one named permission.

by_visibility.description: Whether the group's or repository's visibility alone lets them do it, without any grant.

PipelineChange.description:
How a pipeline, a step or a component instance differs between the two sides: `added`,
`removed`, `changed`, or — for a pipeline only — `renamed` by a `moved` block.

PipelineComponentResponse.description: A published pipeline component: the body of its newest version, and its versions.

parameters.description: The ECR repository to push the image to.
parameters.name: repository

parameters.description: The environment the deploy step targets.
parameters.name: environment

examples.description: Build a container image, push it to ECR and deploy it to a Lambda function.
examples.name: lambda-release

versions.changelog: Waits for the function update to finish before reporting success.

body.description: The body of its newest published version.

source_path.description:
Where the component is written in its repository: `.gitmoap/components/<name>.hcl`, or its
directory. Absent on a component a group owns.

versions.description: Published versions, newest first. Present on a single-component read.

PipelineDefinitionInput.description: A pipeline definition to create, or to replace an existing one with in full.

component_instances.description:
Components this pipeline uses. Each expands into ordinary steps and connections before the
pipeline is validated.

oneOf.description:
Save as a `draft` (problems reported, not runnable) or as `published` (must be valid,
runnable). Defaults to `published`.

PipelineDefinitionStatus.description:
Whether a pipeline definition can run. A `draft` is saved even when it is invalid — problems are
reported, not refused — and cannot be run; a `published` definition must be valid to be saved,
and can be run.

PipelineDiffEntry.description: One pipeline that differs between the two sides.

base_valid.description: Whether it validates on the base side; absent when the base does not declare it.

change.description: Whether it was added, removed, renamed or changed.

directory.description: The directory of the namespace that declares it.

head_valid.description: Whether it validates on the head side; absent when the head does not declare it.

instances.description: The component instances that differ, by id.

name.description: The pipeline's name on the head side — on the base side for one removed.

renamed_from.description: The name a `moved` block leads it from, for a renamed pipeline.

steps.description:
The steps that differ, by id. Empty when a side does not validate, since there is no
definition there to compare.

PipelineDiffResponse.description:
What changes between two commits' pipelines: each pipeline that differs, compared as what it
runs rather than as its text.

base.description: What the change is measured from.

pipelines.description: Every pipeline that differs, by name.

unchanged.description: How many pipelines both sides declare alike.

PipelineDiffSide.description: One side of a pipeline comparison: the ref it was named by, when it was, and the commit read.

commit_sha.description: The commit whose files were read.

ref.description: The full ref the side was named by; absent when a commit was named.

PipelineElementChange.description: A step or a component instance that differs between the two sides.

change.description: Whether it was added, removed or changed.

fields.description:
For a changed one, the fields that differ — the canonical fields such as `capability_id`,
`config` or `environment`, `stage` when it moved between stages, and `inputs` or `after`
when an edge into it was added or removed.

id.description: The step's or the instance's id.

PipelineFileConflict.description: A part of a pipeline both the change and the file changed, differently.

element.description: What the part is, as `step "<id>": <field>`, `stage "<id>": <field>` or `triggers`.

reason.description:
Why the part is the file's to change, when no change to the file is the cause: its value
is computed by an expression, it belongs to an instance a `for_each` makes, or the
directory's `defaults` supplies it. The change is made in the file instead.

theirs.description:
What the file now holds there, as the JSON it means — a number, a string, a list or an
object; absent when the file removed it.

yours.description: What the change wants there, in the same form; absent when the change removes it.

PipelineFileDiagnostic.description: One problem with a pipeline file, or one thing worth saying about it.

examples.message: `memroy` is not an attribute of a step — did you mean `memory`?

code.description:
A stable code: a `syntax_*`, `unsupported_*`, `schema_*` or `reference_*` code of the
language, or a pipeline validation rule's own name.

oneOf.description: A replacement that fixes it, when there is exactly one.

message.description: What is wrong, in a sentence that names it.

related.description: Other places that matter to it — the other half of a duplicate, the rest of a cycle.

severity.description: Whether it stops the file applying.

target.description: The element it is about, as `step:<id>`, `stage:<id>`, `edge:<id>` or `component:<id>`.

PipelineFileFix.description: A replacement that fixes a diagnostic.

oneOf.description: What to replace; absent means the diagnostic's own span.

PipelineFileFormat.description: Which of the two pipeline file forms a text is.

path.description: The file's path from the repository's root.

column.description: The column, counted from 1 in Unicode characters.

offset.description: The byte offset from the start of the file.

PipelineFileRegistration.description:
Whether a pipeline declared at a ref is one of the pipelines the repository's default branch
registers.

PipelineFileResponse.description:
One pipeline at a ref, read: the files of its namespace, the definition it says, and every
diagnostic.

examples.name: ci

blob_sha.description:
The git object id of the file its block is in — what a commit that edits it names as
`expected_blob_sha`.

commit_sha.description: The commit it was read at.

oneOf.description:
The pipeline the namespace declares, its names bound to what they name in your organization
now. Absent when the namespace does not read or bind.

diagnostics.description: Every problem the pipeline has and everything worth saying about it, file by file.

files.description:
Every file of its namespace, as committed — the steps it runs may be written in any of
them.

name.description:
The pipeline's name: its `pipeline` block's label, or a `.json` file's name without its
extension.

path.description: The file its `pipeline` block is in, from the repository's root.

oneOf.description: The registered pipeline this is, when the default branch declares a pipeline of this name.

ref.description: The ref it was read at; absent when a commit was asked for instead.

text.description: The file its block is in, as committed.

PipelineFileSummary.description: One pipeline declared at a ref, summarised.

blob_sha.description:
That file's git object id at this ref — what a commit that edits it names as
`expected_blob_sha`.

changed_from_default.description:
Whether any file of its namespace differs from the default branch's — always `false` on the
default branch itself.

directory.description: The directory its namespace is — every `.hcl` file in it reads as one.

name.description:
The pipeline's name: its `pipeline` block's label, or a `.json` file's name without its
extension.

path.description: The file its `pipeline` block is in, from the repository's root.

oneOf.description: The registered pipeline this is, when the default branch declares a pipeline of this name.

registration.description: Whether the default branch registers the pipeline.

valid.description: Whether the pipeline reads, binds and validates with no error.

warning_count.description: How many warnings it has. A warning never stops a pipeline from running.

PipelineFileText.description: One file of a namespace, as text.

blob_sha.description: The file's git object id at the commit it was read at; absent for a file not committed yet.

path.description:
The file's path from the repository's root, under `.gitmoap/pipelines/` — or, for a
component a check is sent, under `.gitmoap/components/`.

text.description: The file's contents, at most 256 KiB.

PipelinePolicy.description:
`pipelines` — how pipelines treat code an agent wrote. **Ordered**: `untrusted` is stricter
than `trusted`.

agent_code.description:
Whether a run of code an agent wrote, or a run an agent started, gets the repository's
connections, secrets, cloud roles and build cache.

PipelineResponse.description: A pipeline definition: its stages, steps, connections and triggers.

examples.description: Build the image, push it to ECR and deploy it to production.
examples.name: release

oneOf.description: The problems found in a draft. Present only for drafts.

PipelineRunStatusView.description:
A compact view of a run's status, built for polling. Send the response's ETag back in
`If-None-Match` to get `304 Not Modified` while nothing has changed.

PipelineRunSummary.description: A pipeline run as it appears in a list — enough to draw its shape and status without fetching the whole run.

oneOf.description:
The step that broke the run — its first hard failure by when it finished — with the first
line of why. Absent while nothing has failed, when a retry brought the step back green, and
on runs recorded before it existed. A tolerated failure (`allow_failure`) never is one.

The pipeline definition this run was started from. Absent when that definition has since
been deleted; `pipeline_name` still names what ran.

stages.description:
Per-stage counts of how many steps are in each status, in execution order — enough to draw
the run's shape in a list. Empty for older runs recorded before these counts existed.

PipelineRunView.description:
One pipeline run in full: what started it, its status, and every stage, step and connection in
its graph.

edges.description:
The connections between the run's steps, so a client can draw its graph. Each one feeds an
output port of `from_node` into an input port of `to_node`.

oneOf.description:
The pipeline definition this run was started from. Absent when that definition has since
been deleted; `pipeline_name` still names what ran.

stages.description:
The run's stages in execution order, each with how many of its steps have finished and
failed.

oneOf.description:
Why the run stopped before its steps finished on their own. Absent while it runs and when
it finished by itself.

PipelineSource.description: Where on the default branch a pipeline is declared.

commit_sha.description:
The default-branch commit whose change last put the pipeline's content into effect. Absent
for a pipeline its files took over before the commit was recorded.

directory.description:
The directory under `.gitmoap/pipelines/` whose files declare it. Absent for a pipeline
last applied before directories were recorded.

removed_at.description:
When the pipeline's declaration was removed from the default branch, RFC 3339. The
pipeline keeps its id and its runs and starts nothing until a file declares it again.
Absent while it is declared.

stem.description:
The pipeline's name in its files: its `pipeline` block's label, or a `.json` file's name
without its extension.

PipelineTrigger.description: One trigger condition a pipeline declares.

actions.description: Which merge-request events the trigger responds to. Empty for other kinds of trigger.

ordinal.description: The trigger's position in the pipeline's list of triggers, counting from zero.

pattern.description: The branch or tag pattern. Absent means every ref of its kind.

ref_name.description:
For a pipeline defined in a file, the ref the trigger was read from. Absent for a pipeline
defined through the API, whose triggers apply to every ref of their kind.

source_dir.description:
For a pipeline defined in a file, the directory of the namespace that declares it
(`.gitmoap/pipelines/…`). Absent for a pipeline defined through the API.

source_sha.description:
The commit a file-authored projection was read at, so a client can say *as declared at
`a1b2c3`* rather than implying the answer is universal.

stem.description:
For a pipeline defined in a file, the pipeline's name as its files declare it. Absent for a
pipeline defined through the API.

PipelineVariable.description: One pipeline variable. Every pipeline node in the declaring scope receives it as an environment variable; `secret` decides whether the value is returned by the API, and `protected` whether a run on an unprotected ref receives it at all. A secret's value is write-only — it is redacted from step logs and never comes back out of a read.

protected.description:
Whether only a run on a protected branch or tag receives the variable — one a branch or tag
rule protects, building a commit in that ref's history.

value.description: The variable's value. Absent for a secret, whose value can be written but never read back.

PipelineVariableListResponse.description: The pipeline variables a group or repository declares itself.

limit.description: How many variables the group or repository may declare.

max_value_bytes.description: The longest value a variable may hold, in bytes.

variables.description: The variables, by name. A secret's value is never returned.

PipelineVariableSource.description: The group or repository that declared a variable.

full_path.description:
The full path of the group or repository that declared the variable (e.g. `acme/platform`
or `acme/platform/api`).

PipelinesEnablingPreview.description: What turning this repository's pipelines on would start, before anything changes: every pipeline file on its default branch and what would start it, every schedule and the account it would run as, and every environment the files name that resolves for the repository. Nothing was changed.

commit_sha.description: The commit they were read at. Absent for a repository with no commit on it.

complete.description:
Whether the lists were read. `false` when this deployment cannot read them, and the answer
says only what the switch would become.

default_branch.description: The default branch the pipeline files were read from.

environments.description: Every environment the files name that resolves for the repository.

pipelines.description: Every pipeline file on the default branch.

schedules.description: Every schedule that would start firing.

PlanTier.description:
The subscription plan an organization is on, which sets its resource limits. From smallest to
largest: `free`, `pro`, `team`, `enterprise`.

PortCardinality.description:
How many connections an input port accepts: `one` (the default) or `many`, in which case the
step waits for every connected source. An output can always feed any number of inputs.

PortDescriptor.description: One input or output of a capability — what it carries, whether it is required, and what it is for.

cardinality.description: How many sources this input accepts. `one` by default; `many` takes several at once.

description.description: What this port is for, in the provider's own words. Absent on a few older providers.

port_type.description:
Semantic type of the data this port carries. Drives edge
type-compatibility in the pipeline builder and validation/routing in the
engine.

oneOf.description:
For a `custom` port, the id of the schema it carries (e.g. `aws.ecs.task-definition/v1`).
Two `custom` ports connect only when their schema ids agree, or when either leaves this
unset.

PortGroup.description: A rule about how many of a capability's inputs may be connected together — which of them are alternatives, and whether one is required.

description.description:
Why these ports constrain each other, in the provider's own words. Rendered beside the
group, and repeated in the validation error when the group is unsatisfied — which is the
point: the sentence explaining the rule reaches the person who broke it.

ports.description: The member input ports, in the order the author should read them.

PortGroupKind.description: How many of a group's ports may be connected.

PortRef.description: A port on one of the component's steps.

PortType.description: What kind of data a port carries. Two ports connect only when their types match.

Position.description: An agent's job, which decides what it may do and which model tier it uses by default.

PositionOverride.description:
A position as the organization calls it, and its own defaults. Its title is **pinned**; its
work-in-progress limit is **ordered** (lower is stricter).

position.description: The built-in position this renames or re-defaults. Its behaviour does not change.

oneOf.description: The organization's word for the position.

wip_limit.description: Sessions an agent of the position runs at once, unless the agent says otherwise.

PositionRouting.description: Which model tier — or exact model — a position's agents use.

oneOf.description: An exact model, which stays exact until the provider retires it.

PositionTitle.description: What the organization calls a position, one line of at most 80 characters.

PostChannelMessageRequest.description: A message to post: a root message, or a reply in a thread.

examples.body: @ada-ai the release branch is cut — can you start the changelog?

oneOf.description:
What the message is. A person's is `message`, the default; an AI agent must name one of its
kinds — `status`, `question`, `handoff`, `escalation`, `decision`, `ritual_output` or `fyi`.

refs.description: Addresses the message links to — `acme/api#412`, `acme/api!87` — at most 20.

oneOf.description:
Reply in the thread of this message. A reply to a reply joins the root's thread, since
threads are one level deep.

thread_root_seq.description: Reply in the thread of the root message with this number — the `42` of `acme/~general/42`.

PredictedPipeline.description: A pipeline the commit would start.

oneOf.description:
The pipeline, when it is one stored in the platform. A pipeline declared in a file under
`.gitmoap/pipelines/` has no id and is named by its file.

PrincipalKind.description:
A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.

ProposalRunPolicy.description: `approve_each_head`: run nothing until a Developer approves that exact commit. `run_untrusted`: run every such head at once, without secrets — spending the repository's minutes on every contribution.

ProposalState.description: Where the proposal stands. `current`: it holds the source branch's tip as it was last read. `pending`: the source branch moved and its new commits are still to be copied. `blocked`: the source branch's newest tip was refused — a credential, an oversized file, a prohibited name — and the proposal keeps its last accepted version; `blocked` on the proposal lists why. `awaiting_publication`: the newest tip would publish code to a wider audience than can read the source, and whoever pushed it has not consented; nothing of it was copied. `source_unavailable`: the source can no longer be proposed from; the last version stays. `source_deleted`: the source repository was deleted; the last version stays reviewable and mergeable. `purged`: the current version was purged. `expired`: the merge request closed or merged and every version's retention ran out.

ProposalVersionState.description: `present`: the version's commits are kept for review and for the changes-since-a-version diff. `purging`: a purge started and has not finished. `purged`: its commits were removed on purpose; the record stays. `expired`: its retention ran out after the merge request closed or merged, or a newer version pushed it past the merge request's version limit.
