update refused with a `409` if someone changed the scorecard since you read it.

ScorecardAggregate.description:
How many services a scorecard could score, and how many it could not. External services have
nothing to measure, so they are counted separately rather than mixed into the totals.

config.description:
The check's own parameters, such as `{"days": 90}` for `released_within`. An unknown
parameter is refused with a `400` rather than ignored.

creates_work_item.description:
Whether a failure opens a work item in the owning group's backlog. Off by default, and it
takes effect only while the scorecard's campaign is active.

key.description: The built-in check's key for a `derived` check; your own name for the check otherwise.

ScorecardLevel.description:
One rung of a scorecard's ladder. A service is at the highest level all of whose required checks
are `passing` or `not_applicable`.

ScorecardResultsResponse.description: A page of a scorecard's results, with a summary across every service it covers.

ScorecardSummary.description: The cheap shape a listing renders.

by_level.description: Services at each named level. Absent levels are absent keys, not zeroes.

checks.description: Summed over every scored service's checks.

unleveled.description: Services reaching no level at all — including every service on a scorecard with no levels.

SearchHit.description:
One search result: what it is, where it lives, and enough text to show it. Fetch the resource
itself for everything else.

examples.excerpt: A refund above 10,000 EUR waits on the fraud check and times out after 30 seconds.
examples.title: Refunds over 10,000 EUR time out

excerpt.description: A short excerpt of the matching body, when the kind has one.

fork_of.description:
For a repository that is a fork: the path of the repository it was forked from, when you
can see that repository.

id.description:
The resource's own identifier, as its domain names it (an issue `uid`, a
repository id, a group id, a release `tag_name`).

iid.description:
The per-scope sequential number, for the kinds that have one. A comment carries the number
of the work item or merge request it was written on.

oneOf.description:
For a comment: what it was written on, `issue` or `merge_request`. With `scope` and `iid`
it addresses the thread the comment belongs to.

path.description:
For a spec: the document's file in its repository. For a wiki page: the page's path, which
is what reads it.

rank.description: How well the result matches the query; results are ordered by it, highest first.

oneOf.description:
The group or repository the result belongs to — a service's group, a comment's work item's
or merge request's scope. Absent for a group and a repository, which are one themselves.

SearchHitKind.description: What kind of thing a search result is.

SecretRef.description: A credential a step needs, identified by name and by the connection it comes from. Never carries the credential itself.

connection_id.description: The provider connection the credential comes from.

key.description:
A JSON path within the connection's credentials (e.g. `$.password`). It does not select part
of them: the step receives the connection's credentials whole.

logical_name.description: The name the step's provider knows this credential by.

Service.description: A named unit of software the organisation builds, owns and ships.

examples.description: Card payments: authorization, capture and refunds

external.description:
Whether the service is built outside gitmoap — a vendor SaaS, a service on another forge, a
database provisioned elsewhere. The catalog records its name, owner and the dependencies on
it, and nothing else. An external service has no repository paths.

group_id.description:
The **declaring** group — where the entry lives for listing and quota purposes. Not
necessarily the owner.

orphaned_at.description:
When the catalog file declaring this service stopped declaring it. The service is kept, with
its history, rather than deleted.

oneOf.description: Who owns the service. Absent when nobody does.

version.description:
The service's revision, incremented on every change. Send it with an update to have the
update refused with a `409` if someone changed the service since you read it.

ServiceCheckResult.description:
One check's current answer for one service, with where that answer came from: the pipeline run
and commit whose evidence decided it, or the person who attested it.

flapping.description:
Whether the check has changed state ten times today, after which further changes are not
recorded until tomorrow. Read it as "this check is not trustworthy": a threshold set at the
noise floor, or a test that is not deterministic.

ServiceCheckTransition.description: One change in a check's state for a service: what it was, what it became, and when.

ServiceDebt.description: The work items pinned to code in this service's paths, file by file — its technical-debt map.

ServiceDependency.description:
One dependency between two services, with the service at the far end and where the dependency
came from.

confidence.description:
How certain the dependency is: `1.0` for anything the platform observed or a person stated,
lower only for a derived one.

oneOf.description:
The repository whose file established this dependency — a lockfile for an observed one, a
catalog file for a declared one.

ServiceDependencyGraph.description: The services one service depends on, followed outward a limited number of hops.

depth.description: How many hops were followed: the requested depth, at most 3.

hidden.description: Dependencies left out because you cannot see the service at the far end.

nodes.description: Every service reached, the root included, deduplicated.

truncated.description:
Whether the graph stopped at its limit of 200 services, so it shows only part of the real
graph.

ServiceDependencyList.description: A service's dependencies in one direction. The list is not paginated.

hidden.description: Dependencies left out because you cannot see the service at the far end.

truncated.description: Whether the list stopped at its limit of 500 and more exist.

ServiceField.description: A service field an update changed.

ServiceKind.description:
What sort of thing a service is. The kind decides which scorecard checks apply: a `library` has
no deployments, so a deployment check is not applicable to it rather than failing. For your own
classifications, use annotations.

ServiceLanguagesResponse.description: A service's language breakdown, summed over the paths it owns.

excluded.description: What was left out, and why.

items.description: Languages, by bytes descending then name ascending.

sources.description:
One entry per repository contributing to the totals that you can read, so two people can see
different totals for the same service. An empty list means the service has no code you can
see.

total_bytes.description: Total counted bytes across every contributing repository.

ServiceLifecycle.description: Where a service is in its life.

ServiceLink.description: Somewhere a human goes when this service misbehaves.

ServiceLinkType.description: What a service link points at. `other` covers anything the listed kinds do not.

ServiceListItem.description:
One entry in the service catalog listing: a service, and how far along the promotion track it
has got.

deployments.description:
At most one entry per tier, ordered `development`, `testing`, `staging`, `production`. Empty
for a `library`, an external service, or anything never deployed.

ServiceOverview.description:
Everything a service page shows, in one call: the service, its repositories and owner, its latest
release and pipeline run, open merge requests, technical debt, where it is deployed, its
scorecards and its dependency counts.

current_deployments.description:
What is currently deployed, one entry per environment the service is running in. Absent
when it has never been deployed.

dependency_counts.description:
How many dependencies the service has and how many services depend on it, with how many of
those you cannot see.

repositories.description: The repositories holding the service's code. Repositories you cannot see are left out.

scorecards.description:
Every scorecard that applies to this service, with the level it reaches and its check counts.
Absent when no scorecard applies.

overlapping.description: The other services that also claim the path, in resolution order.

oneOf.description:
The service that owns the path when several claim it, chosen by a fixed overlap order. Absent
when no service claims the path.

ServiceRepoPath.description: A set of paths in one repository that belong to a service, given as a glob.

is_exclude.description:
Whether this glob removes its matches from the service's paths instead of adding them. It
affects only its own service.

path_prefix.description: The longest literal prefix of `path_glob`, worked out by the platform. Read-only.

ServiceRepoPathInput.description:
A set of paths in one repository to bind to a service, given as a glob. The platform works out
the path prefix itself.

ServiceRepositoryRef.description: A repository holding some of a service's code, with the globs that select it.

ServiceScorecardSummary.description:
One scorecard's verdict on one service: the level it reaches and how many checks are in each
state.

level.description:
The highest level every required check satisfies, or `null` when the scorecard has no levels
or the service reaches none of them.

ServiceScorecardsResponse.description: Every scorecard that applies to a service, with its verdict on it.

ServiceSelector.description:
Which services a scorecard covers. A service must match every field that is set; with every field
empty, the scorecard covers every service beneath the group or repository that owns it.

annotations.description:
Annotations a service must carry, as key–value pairs. Every entry must match; a service with
extra annotations still matches.

ServiceSource.description:
How the catalog entry came to exist. Set by the platform, never accepted from a request. Any
source other than `inferred` means a person has vouched for the entry.

ServiceSummary.description: The short form of a service that listings, search results and path lookups show.

ServiceTierDeployment.description:
One stop on a service's promotion track: whether anything is serving this environment tier, and
how the latest deployment attempt went. The two can differ — `{ "status": "failed", "deployed":
true }` means the previous version is still serving and the attempt to replace it failed. A tier
may hold several environments (`prod-eu`, `prod-us`): `status` is the worst across them, and
`deployed` is true if any of them is serving.

SessionSubject.description: What a session was started on, as an address such as `acme/api#412`.

address.description: The address acted on — `acme/api#412`, `acme/api!87` — when the session has one.

started_by.description: The person or account whose action started the session, when one did.

SetFeaturedRequest.description: Features a provider in the marketplace, or stops featuring it.

featured_rank.description:
Where to feature the provider: lower numbers are placed higher. `null` or absent stops
featuring it.

parent_ref.description:
The new parent. It may live in another group or repository, which is how an epic in a group
adopts a story in a repository.

SetIssuesIterationRequest.description: The work items to put in an iteration, each named by its scope and number.

items.description:
The work items, from 1 to 100. Each must be in the iteration's group or beneath it; one
named twice is set once.

SetIssuesIterationResponse.description:
The answer to putting many work items in an iteration: one result per item, in the order the
request named them.

SetIterationRequest.description: The iteration to put a work item in.

iteration_id.description: The iteration — one of the work item's own group's, or of a group above it.

SetListingRequest.description:
Changes a provider's marketplace listing. A field left out is not changed; `null` clears
`readme`, `homepage_url` or `repository_url`.

categories.description: The categories to list the provider under, one to three. Replaces the current ones.

examples.description: Usage examples, up to 10. Replaces the current ones; `[]` removes them all.

keywords.description: Search keywords, up to 10. Replaces the current ones; `[]` removes them all.

oneOf.description: The listing's README, in Markdown. `null` removes it.

SetNamespaceOverridesRequest.description: Per-namespace limit overrides. Setting a value to null removes the override and restores the plan's own limit.

overrides.description: Limit-name → value (or `null` to clear). Keys must be namespace `LimitKey`s.

SetProviderPolicyRequest.description:
Sets a group's provider policy: which tiers of provider its pipelines may use. A field left out
is inherited from the groups above rather than set here.

SkipWhen.description: When a run is skipped without calling a model: costs nothing and tells nobody.

SnoozeAttentionRequest.description: Hide an attention item until a later time.

until.description: When the item comes back, RFC 3339. Between one minute and ninety days from now.

SourceImageRef.description:
Where one capability's image lives in your registry: its reference, and the content digest you
attest to, which is checked again when the image is fetched.

SpecBlock.description:
One heading in a spec document. A heading is identified by its `name` and linked to by its
`anchor`; its number, when it has one, is for display only.

parent_ordinal.description: The enclosing block's `ordinal`, not its id — the tree is addressed the way it is read.

SpecDeclaredEdge.description:
A declared link between documents: a `depends_on` entry in a document's frontmatter. Reported
beside the observed links rather than merged into them, so a `depends_on` naming a document that
is never referenced stands out.

resolved.description: False when the named document is not in this repository's index.

SpecDocContent.description:
A spec document's text, at the commit the index was built from (`sha`), so it lines up with the
headings and records the index reports. The frontmatter is removed; it is served as structured
metadata instead.

SpecDocDetail.description: A spec document, its outline and its findings. Its text is fetched separately.

SpecDocSummary.description: One indexed spec document: its metadata, its counts and the commit it was indexed at.

orphaned_at.description:
When the file stopped being present in the repository. The record is kept rather than
deleted, so an existing link still resolves and tells you it moved.

SpecEndpointDecl.description: An HTTP operation (`METHOD /path`) a spec heading declares.

SpecFinding.description: One problem the spec checker found in a document.

truncated.description:
True when the graph stopped at its limit of 500 documents, so it shows only part of the
real graph.

SpecGraphEdge.description: An **observed** edge: one or more resolved references from one document to another.

depth.description: Hops from the root, or `0` for every node when no root was named.

SpecIdCitation.description: Where one citation of an identifier lives.

SpecIdDetail.description: One declaration, its typed body, and every citation the page could carry.

body.description: `{why, how, enforced_by}` for a rule; shape follows the family.

citations_truncated.description:
True when the identifier is cited more than 200 times and `citations` lists only the first
200. List the references with `target_id` set to see them all.

SpecIdKind.description: Which identifier family a declaration belongs to.

SpecIdSummary.description:
An identifier a spec declares, with how often the rest of the specs cite it. A count of zero
shows a rule nobody refers to.

doc_id.description:
The document declaring the identifier. Absent when that document has been removed; the
identifier is kept and cannot be reused.

SpecIndexStatus.description:
A summary of a repository's spec index: how much it holds, what state it is in, and the commit
it describes.

last_seen_sha.description: The commit the index describes. Absent when nothing has ever been indexed.

stale.description: True when any document is marked stale, so a client can tell the index is behind the branch.

SpecOpenQuestion.description: An unresolved question found in a spec — an unchecked checkbox, collected across the repository into one backlog.

SpecPosture.description:
Whether a document claims to follow the spec format. A `declared` document carries `gsf: 1` in
its frontmatter and is checked in full; an `untyped` one made no claim and is never reported for
not following it.

SpecRecord.description:
One typed entry extracted from a table in a spec document, or one checkbox item. `core` holds
the fields the record's `kind` defines; `extra` holds every other column of the table, as
written.

SpecRef.description: One cross-reference, and what it resolved to.

SpecRefKind.description: The form a cross-reference took in the source.

SpecStatus.description:
A document's declared lifecycle state.

`none` is a real value rather than an absence: a document that declares `status: none` has said
the question does not apply to it, which is a different fact from one that declared nothing.

Specialisation.description: An engineer's specialisation, which shapes the work it is given.

SquadBacklog.description:
The work a squad takes: the open work items in its repositories carrying any of these labels,
or every open work item there when it names none.

labels.description: The labels that put a work item in the squad's backlog.

SquadConfig.description:
One squad: a lead, its members (the agents naming it), the repositories it owns, its backlog and
who reviews its agents' work. **Structural.**

lead.description: The agent that leads the squad, a member of it.

repositories.description:
The repositories the squad owns. Its agents are granted these and nothing else, and its
channel, memory and digests are readable by whoever can read every one of them.

review.description: Who reviews the merge requests the squad's agents open.

SquadReview.description:
Who reviews the merge requests the squad's agents open: the platform adds these reviewer agents
to each one and wakes them.

reviewers.description: Reviewer agents of the same squad.

SsoAttributeMapping.description: Which identity-provider claim or attribute supplies each gitmoap field.

email.description: The claim or attribute carrying the person's email address. Defaults to `email`.

groups.description:
The claim listing the person's groups at the identity provider, if any. Teams linked to
those groups follow it.

username.description: The claim a new account's username is derived from, if any.

SsoConnectionRequest.description:
An organization's SSO connection settings. Exactly one of `saml` and `oidc` is given, matching
`protocol`.

auto_provision.description:
Whether to create an account for a person from a verified domain the first time they sign in.
Defaults to `false`.

oneOf.description:
The role newcomers are given at the top-level group — a built-in role, or one of the
organization's own (default Reporter). Invites without a role of their own use it too.

enforced.description: Whether people from a verified domain must sign in through SSO. Defaults to `false`.

idp_sync_max_age_days.description:
Days, 1–365, a person's place on a team linked to an identity-provider group lasts without
them signing in again to confirm it (default 30).

SsoConnectionStatus.description:
Where an organization's SSO connection is in being set up. A connection left `provisioning` or
`failed` is retried by saving the connection again.

SsoConnectionTestResult.description: The result of testing an SSO connection: whether it works, and each check made.

SsoConnectionView.description: An organization's SSO connection, with secrets withheld.

cognito_idp_name.description: The name the identity provider is registered under for sign-in.

default_role.description: The role newcomers are given at the top-level group.

idp_sync_max_age_days.description:
Days a place on a team linked to an identity-provider group lasts without the person signing
in again.

oneOf.description:
The last connection test since these settings were saved — what enforcing single sign-on
waits on. Absent until a test runs, and again after every save.

SsoDomainChallenge.description: A newly claimed domain, with the DNS record to create to verify it.

SsoDomainStatus.description:
Whether a claimed email domain has been verified. A `pending` domain has a DNS challenge to
complete; only a `verified` domain links existing accounts or creates new ones at sign-in.

SsoDomainVerification.description: The DNS-TXT verification instructions returned when a domain is claimed.

record_name.description: The TXT record name to create (`_gitmoap-challenge.{domain}`).

SsoDomainView.description: A domain the organization has claimed for SSO.

SsoInviteView.description: An invitation waiting for its recipient's first SSO sign-in.

expired.description:
Whether that time has passed: the invite admits nobody, and inviting the address again
replaces it.

expires_at.description: When the invite stops letting the address in; absent for one that waits until used.

oneOf.description: Why the address was invited.

role.description: The role given at the top-level group on first sign-in.

SsoLastTest.description: The outcome of a connection's last test, who ran it and when.

oneOf.description: Who ran it; absent once their account is gone.

SsoObservedGroup.description: A group name the organization's identity provider has asserted at a sign-in.

first_seen_at.description: When a sign-in first asserted it.

last_seen_at.description: When a sign-in last asserted it.

name.description: The group's name, exactly as the identity provider sends it — what a team links to.

SsoProtocol.description: The IdP protocol an org's connection speaks.

SsoResolveResponse.description:
Whether an email domain signs in through SSO, and where to send the person if so. When `sso` is
`false` the domain has no active connection, and the standard sign-in applies.

SsoTestCheck.description: One check in a connection test.

StackDiffResponse.description:
The cumulative diff a stacked merge request's whole downstack chain would
produce once merged — the net change from the stack base up to the anchor's
source tip, exactly what `merge-stack` on the same anchor applies.

anchor_mr_id.description: The merge request the diff is anchored on (top of the rolled-up chain).

base_branch.description: The stack base — the bottom-most target branch the diff is taken against.

diff.description:
Three-dot cumulative diff `merge_base(base_branch, anchor_source) …
anchor_source`. `diff.base_sha` is that merge base, not the base tip.

member_mr_ids.description:
The downstack merge requests rolled into this diff, base-first
(the anchor is last).

StackHealth.description: Overall health of a reconstructed stack.

StackNode.description: One member of a reconstructed stack.

children.description: Upstack dependents (a branch may have several). Empty in the `downstack` path.

commits_behind.description: Advisory — how far behind its target this MR's source is.

restack_required.description: Precise — the MR's stored `restack_required` marker (squash downstack).

StackSummary.description: A merge request's immediate neighbours in its stack. The whole stack is fetched separately.

StackView.description:
The full stack a merge request belongs to — the ordered downstack path to the
base plus the upstack tree of dependents.

Stage.description: A stage of the pipeline, holding steps. Stages run in the order they are listed.

StageRollup.description: How many of a stage's steps are in each status.

barrier_passed.description: Whether every step in the stage has finished.

tolerated_failures.description:
How many of the stage's failed or timed-out steps were allowed to fail, so they degrade the
run rather than fail it. Left out when zero.

StageType.description:
The pipeline stage a capability belongs to. Maps verbatim to the
`stage_type` field of a capability in `gitmoap-provider.yaml`.

StageView.description: One stage of a pipeline run and how far its steps have got.

barrier_passed.description: Whether every step in the stage has finished, so later stages may start.

failed_count.description: Steps in the stage that failed or timed out, not counting steps allowed to fail.

stage_index.description: The stage's position in execution order, counting from zero.

terminal_count.description: Steps in the stage that have finished, whatever their outcome.

StaleFile.description: A file a commit would change that is no longer what the caller edited.

oneOf.description: The blob at the branch's head now. Absent when the file has been deleted.
The commit that last changed the file, when it was found in time.

StartAiModelConnectionRequest.description:
Start connecting the organization's own account with a model provider. Connecting is an
Owner's acceptance that the organization's content goes to that provider under the routing
chosen here.

consent.description:
The Owner's acceptance that the organization's content goes to this provider, under this
routing. Required.

routing_region.description: Where the provider routes the organization's calls.

zero_data_retention.description:
Whether only endpoints that keep nothing may serve the organization's calls. On unless
turned off.

StartAiSessionRequest.description: Start an agent on a subject: a person's manual trigger.

subject.description: The address the work is about — `acme/api#412` — when there is one.

StartedAiModelConnection.description: A connection being made: where to send the Owner's browser, and until when.

authorize_url.description: The provider's authorization page, carrying the PKCE challenge and the `state`.

expires_at.description: When the request expires: the provider's code must be posted back before then.

StatusCategory.description:
The fixed category behind a status. A status also has a *name*, which the team owns and may
rename freely; the category is the part the platform reasons about. A team can call a status
"Ready for QA" and the platform still knows it is `in_review` — so a board can place it in a
column, a merge can move it, and a progress rollup can count it as not done.

StatusDef.description:
One status in a group's or repository's status set. A status is archived, never deleted: issues
already in it keep it and go on rendering, sorting and rolling up correctly.

category.description:
The category this status belongs to. It cannot be changed after the status is created: to
move work to a different category, add a status and archive this one.

is_default.description:
The status new issues land in. Exactly one status in a set carries it, and
it must be open.

StorageAfter.description: The destination namespace's storage once the fork's copy is counted.

StructureLevel.description:
The organization's shape: `L1` is engineers in one squad, `L2` adds squads each led by a
product owner, `L3` adds a director across the squads.

SubjectKind.description: Which kind of subject the access page lists.

SubjectRef.description:
Who a grant is to: `{ "principal": "<id>" }` for a person or a service account, or
`{ "team": "<id>" }` for a team of the organization.

SubmissionCapabilityInput.description:
One capability in a submission. `image_ref` and `image_digest` point at your own registry; for a
verified provider, gitmoap copies the image into its own registry.

bindable.description:
Config keys that can take their value from an earlier step. Each becomes an optional
`value` input port of the same name when the version is published.

input_groups.description: Rules over which of the capability's optional inputs may be connected together.

SubmissionProviderInput.description: The author-supplied provider block of a submission.

SubmissionState.description: Where a provider submission stands, from review through to publication or refusal.

SubmissionSummary.description: A compact submission entry for list endpoints.

SubmitContactMessageRequest.description: A message to a person at Gitmoap: what it is about, where the reply goes, and what it says.

examples.message: I cannot find where to rotate a service account token.
examples.name: Ada

email.description: Where the reply goes. Nothing is sent to it until a person replies.

oneOf.description: The name to address the reply to, when you want to give one.

topic.description: What the message is about, which chooses the desk a person answers it from.

website.description: Leave empty. A form a person fills in never sets it.

SubmitMrReviewRequest.description: Submit a review: its verdict and, optionally, a summary.

examples.body: Two things before this merges; see the comments.

oneOf.description: A summary, posted on the merge request as the review's comment.

SubmitProviderRequest.description: Submits a new provider, or a new version of an existing one.

oneOf.description:
Optional release notes for this version, in Markdown, up to 64 KB. They cannot be changed
once the version is published.

Required when `target_tier` is `private`: the organization (a top-level group) the provider
is private to. You must be at least a Maintainer there.
Optional registry pull credential (Private only); rejected for other tiers.

SubscriptionStatus.description:
Stripe subscription status, mirrored. `entitled_tier` is the only place it
becomes a `PlanTier`.

SubscriptionView.description:
The customer-facing subscription view — no Stripe ids. A never-subscribed
namespace synthesises a `Free`/`active` view.

SunsetVersionRequest.description: Sunsets a provider version after a grace period.

SuspectCommit.description: One commit in a regression's suspect range.

oneOf.description:
The commit's author, message and date. Absent when the commit can no longer be read — a
force-push removed it, or the work item has moved to another repository since it regressed.

SyncForkRequest.description: The body of a request to sync a fork branch from its upstream.

oneOf.description: The fork branch to move. Defaults to the tracked branch.
Refuse if the fork branch is no longer at this commit.
How to bring it in. Defaults to `fast_forward`.
The upstream branch to bring in. Defaults to the tracked upstream branch.

SyncMode.description: `fast_forward`: move the fork branch only if it has no commits the upstream lacks. `merge`: write a merge commit of the upstream branch into the fork branch. `reset`: move the fork branch to the upstream's tip, discarding its own commits — only for someone the fork's branch rules allow to force-push.

TagPattern.description: The tags a tag rule protects: one tag name, or a glob over tag names such as `v*` or `release-*`.

TagRuleId.description: A tag rule's id: one protected tag pattern on a repository or a group.

TagRuleResponse.description:
A tag rule: creating, moving or deleting a tag that matches `tag_pattern` needs at least
`allowed_to_create` on the repository.

allowed_to_create.description: The lowest access level that may create, move or delete a matching tag.

enforcement.description:
`enforced` on a group's rule holds every scope beneath it to this rule or a stricter one for
the same pattern; `default` otherwise.

scope_id.description: The repository or group the rule is attached to.

scope_type.description: Whether the rule is attached to a repository or a group.

tag_pattern.description: A tag name, or a glob where `*` matches any run of characters, `/` included.

TakeOverAiSessionResponse.description: A session a person took over, and where its work is.

branch.description: The agent's branch: what it pushed is there; what it had not pushed is lost.

repository.description: The repository the work is in, as an address.

session.description: The session, as it stood when it was taken over. It ends at its next step.

idp_group.description:
The identity provider's group this team mirrors. Absent for a team whose roster is kept by
hand.

member_count.description: People on the team, counting any whose place has lapsed but not yet been removed.

TeamAccessPage.description: A page of the grants a team holds, on groups and repositories you can see.

hidden_scopes.description: Whether the team also holds access somewhere you cannot see. Those places are never named.

TeamAccessReach.description:
How far a team's access reaches, as the person asking may see it: what someone joining gains,
or someone leaving loses.

hidden_scopes.description: Whether the team also holds access somewhere you cannot see. Those places are never named.

scopes_visible_to_you.description: Groups and repositories among them that you can see.

TeamDeletionPreview.description: What deleting a team does: its grants are revoked and its people lose what the team gave them.

access.description: The grants revoked with the team.

members.description: People on the team, each of whom loses the team's access.

at.description: Where the grant was made. It reaches there and everything beneath that inherits access.

expires_at.description: When their place on the team ends. After it, the team's access no longer reaches them.

synced_at.description: When the identity provider last confirmed this place, for a mirrored roster.

TeamMemberChange.description: A person put on a team, or — with `dry_run` — what putting them there would do.

dry_run.description: Whether this was only a preview, and nothing was changed.

gained_access.description: The team's access, which the person now has through it.

TeamMemberPage.description: A page of a team's people.

TeamMemberRemoval.description: A person taken off a team, or — with `dry_run` — what taking them off would do.

dry_run.description: Whether this was only a preview, and nothing was changed.

lost_access.description: The team's access, which the person no longer has through it.

people_losing.description:
On a preview, what the person would actually lose at each place the team's grants are made
that you can see — nothing where they keep the same access directly or through another team,
so an empty list means coming off the team changes nothing they can do there.

TeamMemberRole.description: A member's place on a team. Maintainers manage the roster.

TeamPage.description: A page of an organization's teams.

TeamRosterSource.description: Who keeps a team's roster: people, through the API, or an identity provider.

TeamSummary.description:
A team, as a grant names one. Someone who is not a member of the organization learns only that
a team holds the grant: `hidden` is `true` and the name, slug and size are left out.

TeamUsage.description:
Where a team is named besides its grants — what someone joining it is also signing up for: the
approvals they will be asked for, the deployments they can approve, the protected branches they
can push to, the services they will own, and the code they will be a required reviewer of.

Each place is listed only when you can see it there; the rest are counted, never named.

codeowners.description:
CODEOWNERS lines naming the team, as each repository's default branch had them at its last
push or merge.

hidden.description: Whether the team is named somewhere you cannot see.

truncated.description: Whether a list stops short: each holds at most 100.

TeamUsageBranchRule.description: A protected-branch rule that lets the team push or merge below the rule's minimum role.

at.description: The group or repository the rule protects branches of.

merge.description: Whether the team may merge into them.

push.description: Whether the team may push to the branches the rule protects.

TeamUsageCodeownersLine.description:
A line of a repository's CODEOWNERS file that names the team, making everyone on it a required
approver for the paths the line covers.

at.description: The repository whose file it is.

file_path.description: `CODEOWNERS` or `.gitmoap/CODEOWNERS`, on the repository's default branch.

pattern.description: The paths the line covers, as written.

TeamUsageEnvironment.description: An environment whose deployments the team may approve.

at.description: The group or repository that owns the environment.

TeamUsageRule.description: An approval rule that names the team among its approvers.

at.description: The group or repository that defines the rule.
The group that declares the service.

content.description: The file's text, each field written as `{{name}}` where its value goes.

TemplateField.description: A value a template asks for, written into its content as `{{name}}`.

label.description: What to call it next to the input that fills it in.

name.description: The placeholder's name — `year` stands for `{{year}}`.

TemplateSummary.description: A template, without its content — one entry of a listing.

fields.description: The values the content asks for, in the order it first asks.

ThreadReplies.description: A thread: its root message and a page of its replies, oldest first.

items.body: The changelog ritual starts in this thread.

items.description: Its replies, oldest first.

next_token.description: Pass as `next_token` for later replies; absent on the last page.

TimeZoneName.description: An IANA time-zone name, such as `Europe/Amsterdam` or `UTC`.

TodoPolicy.description: What a bare `// TODO:` in a push becomes.

TokenPrincipalKind.description: The kind of principal an access token authenticates as.

TokenResourceBinding.description:
Restricts a token to a single group subtree or repository (GitHub
fine-grained-PAT style). Omit for a token usable across everything the
principal can already reach.

TopScopesResponse.description: The repositories and groups you have been most active in over a time window.

TransitionSource.description:
Why a work item's status changed: whether a person decided it, a commit or merge request said
so, or a pipeline's evidence proved it.

TransitionTable.description:
Which status categories a work item may move to from each category, as a map from a category to
the categories it may move to. A category not listed may move anywhere.

oid.description:
The entry's git object id at this commit. For a file, it is the `blob_sha` a blob read
returns — so a client holding an edited copy can tell from a listing alone that the file
changed underneath it.

TreeEntryCommit.description: One entry of a directory listing, with the commit that last changed it.

oneOf.description:
The newest commit that changed this file, or anything inside this directory. Absent when
the search reached its limit before finding one; `truncated` on the response says so.

name.description: The entry's name within the directory being listed.

path.description: The entry's full path from the repository root — the key to join against a tree listing.

TreeLastCommitsResponse.description:
The last commit to change each entry of one page of a directory listing. Ask with the same
`ref`, `path`, `limit` and `page` as the directory listing and the two line up entry for entry,
so a page can show its file list at once and fill in the commits when they arrive.

oneOf.description: The newest commit that changed anything in this directory.

truncated.description:
The search reached its limit before every entry had an answer. The entries it did not
reach carry no `commit`; they have one, it was simply too far back to find in time. A
search that ran out of time is answered with `Cache-Control: no-store` and no `ETag`, so
asking again searches again; one that reached its limit on commits read gives the same
answer every time.

TreePaths.description: Every file path at a commit — what "go to file" searches — or, with a glob, how many match.

commit_sha.description:
The commit the paths were read at — the ref resolved, so every page and every count reads
one snapshot.

count.description: With a glob: how many files match it.

paths.description:
The paths, repository-relative, in `git`'s order: every file's, or the first of those the
glob matches.

truncated.description:
Whether the repository holds more files than one read lists, so `paths` — and `count` —
cover only the first of them.

TriggerAllowList.description:
`triggers` — who may wake an agent beyond the organization's members. **Ordered**: a smaller
allow-list is stricter.

TriggerContext.description: What started this run — the event, the commit, the branch, and who or what triggered it. Available to every step.

before_sha.description:
The commit the ref pointed at before the push — what a `paths` filter compares against. On
a run started by hand, the commit its starter named to compare from, if any.

oneOf.description: Which commit a merge-request-triggered run built.

depth.description:
How many pushes made by pipeline runs led to this run, one after another; `0` when no
pipeline's push started it.

every_step.description: Every step runs, whatever its path filter says — asked for by whoever started the run.

extra.description:
Additional fields supplied by whatever started the run, passed along without being
interpreted.

oneOf.description:
Where the run's steps came from: a saved pipeline, or the request that started it. Set by
the platform; absent on runs that started before this was recorded.

params.description:
The values a person supplied when starting the run, keyed by the parameter names the
pipeline's manual trigger declares.

pipeline_stem.description:
The pipeline file the run's definition was read from, `.gitmoap/pipelines/<stem>.*` at the
commit it built. Absent for a run of a pipeline defined through the API.

oneOf.description:
For a run of a merge request from a fork: the merge request, the version of its proposed
commits the run built, and the pipeline file it ran. Absent for every other run.

protected_ref.description:
Whether the run is on a protected ref: a branch or tag a rule protects, building a commit
in that ref's history. Only such a run receives the connections and variables marked
protected. Set by the platform when the run starts.

ref_name.description:
The full ref (e.g. `refs/tags/v1.2.0`). Set for runs a tag started, which `branch` cannot
describe.

oneOf.description:
The organisation this run belongs to — the root group of the repository it was triggered
for.

Recorded when the run starts and never recalculated, so a repository moved to a different
organisation part-way through a run keeps the artifacts, logs and cache it has already
produced. Absent on runs that started before runs recorded this.

schedule_stem.description: Which scheduled trigger fired, when `kind` is `schedule`.

source_sha.description:
The source-branch commit this run tested: a merge request's source head for a
merge-request run, whichever commit it built, and the commit itself for a push or manual
run. Set by the platform; absent on a run whose graph the caller supplied, which never
counts toward a merge request's pipelines.

target_sha.description:
The target branch's tip this merge-request run was tested against. Once the target branch
moves on, the merge check reports a merge-result run as out of date.

triggered_by.description:
Who started the run, set by the platform from the authenticated caller; a value supplied in
a request is ignored.

trust.description:
Whether the code being built is trusted with the repository's connections and secrets. Set
by the platform when the run starts, whatever a request says.

oneOf.description:
Why the run has the trust it has: who wrote the code, a person's merge or approval, or the
organization's AI configuration. Absent on runs that started before this was recorded.

TriggerEvaluation.description: One recorded evaluation — the answer to "I pushed and nothing happened, why?".

oneOf.description: Whose access the evaluation was checked against.

before_sha.description:
The commit the ref pointed at before the update this evaluation was about — with
`commit_sha`, the range a retry evaluates again. Absent for a ref that was created, and for
evaluations recorded before the range was kept.

detail.description:
Whatever makes the outcome actionable rather than merely named — the declared patterns,
the quota gate that closed, the violation list.

TriggerEvent.description:
One condition that starts the pipeline, identified by `type`. Branch and tag patterns are
matched against the short name (`main`, not `refs/heads/main`): `*` matches within one path
segment and `**` across segments, so `release/*` matches `release/1` but not `release/1/2`.

allow_pipeline_triggered.description:
Opt in to being triggered by a push that a pipeline run itself made. Without this a
pipeline that pushes cannot cause itself; with it, the depth cap still bounds the
chain, because an opt-in with no bound is an unbounded loop with extra steps.

paths.description:
Absent = no path constraint. Matches when **any** changed path matches **any**
pattern; a `!`-prefixed entry removes an earlier match.

actions.description:
Absent = `opened`, `synchronized`, `reopened`. An unrecognised action is dropped
rather than failing the whole definition.

build.description: Which commit to build. Defaults to the merge result.

oneOf.description: Runs when a tag is pushed.

params.description:
The typed inputs a person starting the run supplies. Supplied values are checked
against these when the run starts, and a step's config reads one as
`{"$context": "params.<name>"}`; a reference to a parameter not declared here is refused
when the pipeline is saved.

TriggerInput.description:
What started the run, as the caller describes it. The repository and the person starting the
run are filled in by the platform.

kind.description: What kind of event started the run. Defaults to `manual`.

params.description:
Values for the parameters the pipeline's manual trigger declares, by name. They are checked
against the declared parameters before the run starts, and only these can be read from a
step's config — unlike `extra`, which is passed along as given.

TriggerKind.description: What caused a run to start.

TriggerOutcome.description:
Why a pipeline did or did not start for a ref update. `matched` means a run started. Otherwise:
`no_trigger_match` (no trigger matched the event, ref or paths), `not_registered_at_ref` (no
pipeline at that ref), `draft` (the pipeline is a draft), `authority_denied` (whoever pushed
lacks Developer access), `authority_unresolvable` (whoever caused the event could not be
identified), `authority_revoked` (the owner of a schedule lost Developer access),
`quota_exhausted`, `loop_guard` (a pipeline's own push, without opt-in or too many in a row),
`superseded` (replaced by a newer run), `provider_validation_failed`,
`connection_resolution_failed`, `definition_invalid`, `already_triggered` (the same event was
already handled), `merge_conflict` (the merge result could not be built), `pipelines_disabled`
(the repository's pipelines are switched off — a new fork's are until a Maintainer turns them
on), `held` (a merge request from a fork, at a commit nobody has vouched for, waits until a
Developer of the repository approves that commit) or `skipped` (the commit message asked for
no run).

TriggerPipelineByIdRequest.description: Starts a run of a saved pipeline definition.

every_step.description:
Run every step, whatever its path filter says. By default a step that deploys runs only if
something it watches changed since its environment's last deploy, and any other filtered
step runs when a step after it does.

pipeline_timeout_seconds.description: The run's overall time limit, in seconds. Absent or `0` uses the platform default.

oneOf.description:
Compare from this commit: a step that does not deploy runs only if something it watches
changed between this commit and the one being built. Absent, such a step runs when a step
after it does.

TriggerPipelineRunRequest.description:
Starts a pipeline run from a fully resolved pipeline graph supplied in the request, rather than
from a saved pipeline definition.

pipeline_id.description: The saved pipeline in this repository the run is filed under.

TriggerPipelineRunResponse.description: Confirms the pipeline run was started. Fetch the run by its id to follow its progress.

oneOf.description:
The saved pipeline the run is filed under; absent when it is filed under none, as a run of a
pipeline only a branch's file defines is.

TriggerTrust.description: Whether the code being built is trusted with the repository's connections and secrets. A run is `untrusted` when an AI agent started it or wrote code it builds that no person has merged, and the agent's organization keeps agent code untrusted; it runs without connections, secrets or the build cache until a person approves it.

TrustReason.description: Why the platform gave a run the trust it has.

oneOf.description: Trusted: no AI agent started the run or wrote the code it builds.
Trusted: an agent wrote the code, and a person brought it in with a merge commit.
Trusted: a person approved the commit this run builds.

Trusted: an agent started the run or wrote the code it builds, and the organization's AI
configuration trusts agent-written code in pipelines.

revision.description:
The AI organization's revision that was live when the run started. Absent when none had
been published.

oneOf.description: Untrusted: an AI agent started the run.
Untrusted: the commits the run builds include one an agent wrote that no person merged.
Untrusted: the run builds more commits than the platform reads to check who wrote them.

Trusted: a merge request from a fork whose every writer is a Developer of this repository,
at a version vouched for or approved by a Maintainer.

Untrusted: a merge request from a fork at a version nobody vouched for — someone who could
have written to its source branch is not a Developer of this repository — or a run of the
proposal's own pipeline files.

Untrusted: whoever moved the branch the run builds holds no Developer on this repository — a
maintainer's edit to a contributor's branch — or the branch moved by an automatic sync from
the repository it was forked from, which nobody decided.

UnchangedGrant.description: A subject the request named that already had what it asked for.

UnchangedReason.description: Why a subject named in a create request was left as it was.

external.description: Services marked external, which the platform cannot measure.

reason.description: Why nothing could be derived, in one phrase a page can render beside the number.

UnsubscribeAudience.description:
Which mail an unsubscribe link stops: one notification category's email, or the blog's
newsletter.

oneOf.description: Email about one notification category.
The blog's newsletter.

UpdateAccessGrantRequest.description: Change a grant's role, its expiry or its reason. Fields left out are unchanged.

expires_at.description: A new end date, or `null` for access that lasts until it is revoked.

oneOf.description: A new reason, or `null` to clear it.

UpdateAccessInheritanceRequest.description: Whether grants made on the groups above reach this group or repository.

expected_revision.description:
The revision the edit was made from; a page written since is refused `409`, so two editors
never overwrite each other silently. Omit it to write whatever the page holds.

oneOf.description: `manual` stops the platform moving the anchor; any other value hands it back to the platform.

UpdateApprovalPolicyRequest.description: Set a group's or repository's approval policy.

enforcement.description:
`enforced` holds every group and repository beneath to these switches or stricter. Only
someone who administers access here may set or clear it.

UpdateApprovalRuleRequest.description: Change an approval rule. Send only what changes.

applies_to_branches.description: `null` makes the rule apply to every branch.

UpdateBlueprintRequest.description:
Replace a blueprint as a whole. Work items already filed as it keep their criteria; apply the
blueprint to a work item again to add any new facets to it.

version.description:
The `version` you last read. The update is refused with a `409` if the blueprint changed
since.

oneOf.description: On a group only; see the create request.

UpdateChannelRequest.description: A change to a channel. Only what is present changes.

oneOf.description: A new name, unique in the group.
A new topic; an empty one clears it.

UpdateCodeSearchSettingsRequest.description: The body that turns an organization's code search on or off.

enabled.description: On, or off. Off deletes the organization's index; on indexes every repository again.

UpdateCriterionRequest.description: Edit one criterion. Every field is optional; absent means "leave alone".

oneOf.description:
`{"binding": {...}}` re-binds it and resets its evidence, `{"binding": null}` turns it into a
manual checkbox, and omitting the key leaves the binding untouched.

checked.description:
Tick or untick a manual criterion. Refused with a `409` for a bound one, whose state comes
from its evidence.

UpdateEnvironmentRequest.description:
Changes some of an environment's fields. A field left out is not changed; `null` clears
`display_name` or `url`.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency guard. When supplied and stale, the write is a `409`.

UpdateForkRequest.description: The body of a request to change how a fork follows its upstream.

auto_sync.description:
Fast-forward the tracked branch on every push to the upstream branch, as you. Needs read
access to the upstream; it pauses, with a reason, rather than merge or discard anything.

code_search.description:
Index the fork for code search. A fork is left out unless one of its Maintainers turns this
on, so a network of forks does not answer one search many times.

oneOf.description: The fork branch that follows the upstream.
The upstream branch it follows.

UpdateForkSettingsRequest.description:
The body of a request changing a scope's own fork settings. Absent leaves a field alone; `null`
returns it to what it inherits.

allow_maintainer_edits.description: Whether the authors of merge requests from forks may let the target's maintainers push to their branch.

oneOf.description: How many days the proposed versions of a merge request closed without merging are kept; `0` keeps them until purged.
Who may open a merge request from a fork into the repositories beneath this scope.

fork_merge_requests_enforced.description: A group's only: enforce `fork_merge_requests` as a ceiling beneath it.

oneOf.description: Who may fork, and where to.

forking_enforced.description: A group's only: enforce `forking` as a ceiling beneath it.

min_account_age_days.description: How old, in days, an account must be to open a merge request from a fork.

min_account_age_days_enforced.description: A group's only: enforce `min_account_age_days` as a floor beneath it.

oneOf.description: Where the forks beneath this scope may open merge requests to.

outbound_merge_requests_enforced.description: A group's only: enforce `outbound_merge_requests` as a ceiling beneath it.

override_group_settings.description: For a repository: whether its own row counts.

oneOf.description: When a merge request from a fork runs its target's pipelines.

proposal_runs_enforced.description: A group's only: enforce `proposal_runs` as a ceiling beneath it.

UpdateIssueRequest.description: Every field optional; an empty body is a `400`.

version.description:
Required. The `version` you last read; if the work item has changed since, the update is
refused with a `409` rather than silently overwriting someone else's change.

UpdateIssueSettingsRequest.description:
A partial update of a group's or repository's work item settings. Leave a field out to keep it;
set it to `null` to clear it, so the value is inherited again from the parent group.

UpdateIssueViewRequest.description: A change to a saved view; only the fields sent change.

filters.description: New filters, replacing the old ones whole.

name.description: A new name, 1–80 characters.

position.description: A new place in the list.

UpdateIterationCadenceRequest.description:
Changes to a cadence. Only the fields you send change, and at least one is required. Its schedule
is fixed once it exists; to change the schedule, pause it and create another.

active.description: Pause it with `false`, or resume it with `true`.

iterations_in_advance.description: How many upcoming iterations to keep created: 1 to 12.

oneOf.description: A new title, used for iterations it generates from now on.

UpdateIterationRequest.description:
Changes to an iteration. Only the fields you send change, and at least one is required. A
generated iteration's days come from its cadence and cannot be changed.

description.description: A new description, or `null` to remove it.

oneOf.description: A new last day. Refused for a generated iteration.
A new first day. Refused for a generated iteration.
A new title.

UpdateLabelRequest.description:
Changes a label's title, colour or description — or its key. A new key moves every work item
carrying the label to it in one transaction; the old key then answers `409 LABEL_RENAMED`,
naming the new one, for thirty days.

oneOf.description: A new key. One the scope already defines is refused `409`.

title.description: Its display name, 1–64 characters; `null` shows its key again.

allow_maintainer_edits.description:
For a merge request from another repository, and its author's alone to change: let this
repository's mergers push to the source branch, or stop letting them.

closed.description:
Closing a milestone is an edit, not a separate verb: it changes one field and
nothing else happens.

allow_merge_without_pipeline.description:
While `require_pipeline_success` is on: whether a merge request that no pipeline applies to
may merge. Off — the default — blocks it. `null` inherits.

require_pipeline_success.description:
Block the merge until every pipeline that applies to the merge request's head has
succeeded. `null` inherits.

UpdateNotificationPreferencesRequest.description: Change your notification preferences. Fields left out are unchanged.

oneOf.description: Hourly or daily digests.

preferences.description: Categories to change, each on one channel. At most one entry per category and channel.

oneOf.description: New quiet hours, or `null` for email that is never held back.
A new time zone.

UpdateProviderConnectionRequest.description:
Changes a provider connection. Supplying `credentials` rotates them: new and changed fields are
stored and fields left out are removed. Supplying `config_overrides` replaces the current ones.
`protected`, `environment_ids` and `environment_bound` change which runs and steps may use it;
each field left out keeps its current value.

environment_bound.description:
`false` removes the binding, so any step may use the connection again. `true` keeps a
connection bound and, on an unbound one, needs `environment_ids`.

environment_ids.description: Binds the connection to these environments, replacing the ones it is bound to. At most 20.

oneOf.description:
A new role, audience or region for an `oidc_federation` connection. A connection's
`auth_mode` cannot be changed.

protected.description: Whether only a run on a protected branch or tag may use the connection.

UpdateProviderSettingsRequest.description:
Body for editing an existing install's version policy — the allow-policy
and the track-latest toggle. Distinct from `upgrade_provider` (which moves
the pinned `default_version`, gated by changelog-ack): this edits *which*
versions are declarable and whether the install auto-advances. Every field
is optional; an absent field leaves that setting unchanged.

oneOf.description:
Replace the allow-policy (e.g. restrict to a `List`/`Range` to disable
old versions). Absent ⇒ unchanged.

UpdatePublisherRequest.description: `PATCH /publishers/{id}` request body — any subset of the mutable fields.

oneOf.description:
On a group only: `enforced` holds every group and repository beneath to these rules or
stricter ones. Only someone who administers access on the group may set or clear it.

UpdateReleaseRequest.description: Changes some of a release's fields. A field left out is not changed.

version.description:
The release's `version` as you last read it. The update is refused if the release has
changed since.

catalog_enabled.description:
Whether the repository's catalog file is read into the service catalog. Off for a new fork,
whose file names the services of the repository it was forked from.

narrow_forks.description:
With a `visibility` that narrows who can read the repository: also narrow its forks in its
organization that you may change and that would otherwise stay more visible than it.

pipelines_enabled.description:
Whether pushes, merge requests, tags and schedules start pipeline runs. Off for a new fork
until a Maintainer turns it on; `GET /repositories/{repo_id}/pipelines-preview` lists what
would start first.

purge_closed_proposals.description:
With a `visibility` that widens who can read the repository: first purge every kept
version of the merge requests from forks that were closed without merging, so the wider
audience never reads what nobody accepted. `GET /repositories/{repo_id}/visibility-preview`
lists them.

UpdateRoleRequest.description:
Change a custom role. Absent fields are left as they are; `added` and `removed`, when sent,
replace the lists they name. A changed role changes access everywhere it is granted.

UpdateScorecardRequest.description:
A partial update. `checks` and `levels`, when given, replace the whole list rather than being
merged into it.

campaign_active.description:
Switches the campaign on or off. Unlike every other field here, changing it requires the
Owner role, because switching it on can file work items across every covered service.

version.description:
The `version` you last read. When given and the scorecard has changed since, the update is
refused with a `409`.

UpdateServiceRequest.description:
A partial update. Each owner field is three-state: absent leaves it alone, `null` clears it, and
a value sets it.

version.description:
The `version` you last read. When given and the service has changed since, the update is
refused with a `409`.

UpdateTagRuleRequest.description:
Change a tag rule. The pattern is the rule's identity and does not change; a different pattern
is a different rule.

oneOf.description:
The lowest access level that may create, move or delete a matching tag. Unchanged when left
out.
On a group only: `enforced` or `default`. Unchanged when left out.

UpdateTeamRequest.description: Rename a team, or change its description. Absent fields are left as they are.

UpdateWebhookRequest.description: Changes some of a webhook's fields. A field left out is not changed.

UpdateWikiPageRequest.description: Replace a page's content or title.

expected_head_sha.description:
The head the edit was composed against.

**Required, and there is no mode that omits it.** An unconditional overwrite has a window in
which two saves observe the same head and one is lost with nothing reporting it.

UpdateWikiRequest.description: Turn a wiki on or off, or change where it reads from.

UpgradeDisposition.description:
Where a pipeline using the component stands against the target version: `on_target` (its
reference already selects it), `needs_repin` (its reference has to be changed to reach it) or
`unresolvable` (its reference selects no version at all, because every candidate has been
retired).

changelog_acknowledged.description:
Must be `true` to advance to a new version when the org's effective
`require_changelog_ack` policy is set; ignored otherwise.

UsageEntry.description:
One charge on the ledger: what it was for, its amount and fee, and the price and token counts
it was computed from.

funding.description:
Who paid the usage: the balance, or the organization's own provider account — in which case
the balance paid only the fee.

price_ref.description: What the amount was calculated from: the model price used and the token counts.

subject.description: What was charged for — for a model call, organization, agent, session and turn.

UsageFunding.description:
Who paid a charge's usage (M7). Every budget counts usage and fee alike whatever the funding;
only what the balance holds and pays differs.

UsageLimitEntry.description: A limit with its live usage — used for the namespace and named-group buckets.

UsageLine.description: What a ledger entry charges for. One line so far: AI model usage.

UserProfile.description: A person's public profile: what anyone may read about an account, signed in or not.

avatar.description: The URL of the person's avatar image, when they have one.

closed.description:
Whether the account was closed. A closed account whose record stays — because something it
wrote stays where other people work — has a generated username, `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, which no open account may take; the same shape names it wherever it appears as an
actor.

ValidatePipelineRunRequest.description:
Checks the steps of a resolved pipeline graph against the provider catalog, as starting a run
would, without starting one.

ValidatePipelineRunResponse.description:
The result of checking a pipeline graph without running it. `valid` is `true` when
`violations` is empty; `resolved` names the provider image each step would run; `warnings` are
advisories that do not block a run, such as a deprecated provider version.

ValidationSummary.description:
The result of validating a pipeline definition: reported on a draft, and returned with a `400`
when saving a published definition fails. Each problem carries a stable `code`.

warnings.description:
Things worth knowing that do not make the definition invalid, such as a deprecated
component version. A violation stops a published definition from being saved; a warning
never does. Left out when there are none.

ValidationTarget.description: The part of the pipeline a validation problem points at.

id.description:
Id of the stage, step, connection or component instance at fault; empty for a problem with
the pipeline as a whole.

ValidationTargetKind.description: Which kind of element a validation violation targets.

ValidationViolation.description: One reason a definition is invalid.

ValidationWarning.description: One thing worth saying about a definition that is nonetheless valid.

code.description: Stable machine code — the warning rule's own name, exactly as a violation's is.

VelocityIteration.description: One closed iteration in a cadence's velocity.

carry_over_points.description: The points it left unfinished: still open in it, or rolled over out of it.

committed_points.description:
The points it took on: every work item in it that was not cancelled, and those rolled out
of it.

sequence.description: Its position in the cadence. Absent once its cadence no longer numbers it.

VerificationChallenge.description:
An open self-service namespace-ownership challenge on a publisher. The `token`
is a non-secret nonce the publisher places publicly (a DNS TXT record or a
GitHub repo file) for the platform to read back.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339; after this the challenge is no longer verifiable.

target.description: The domain or GitHub organisation being verified. It must match the publisher's namespace.

VerificationMethod.description:
How a publisher's `verified` flag was earned. `Manual` is the platform-admin
grant (D3); `Dns` / `Github` are the self-service namespace-ownership proofs.

VerificationState.description:
Whether CI has proved the work item's acceptance criteria. `unverified` until a pipeline run
proves them, `verified` once one has, and `regressed` when a later run shows that evidence
no longer holds.

VerifyProviderConnectionRequest.description:
Which repository and ref a connection's verification speaks for — the identity token is the one
a pipeline run there would carry, so the role's trust policy is checked against exactly that.

ref.description:
The ref the run would be for, `refs/heads/…` or `refs/tags/…`; the repository's default
branch when absent.

oneOf.description:
The repository whose runs would use the connection. A repository's own connection needs
none; a group's names one of the group's repositories.

VersionLifecycle.description:
Lifecycle state of a published `ProviderVersionManifest`. `Active` is the
default; `Deprecated` still runs but the trigger-time validator surfaces a
warning; `Sunset` runs only inside its grace window, after which a trigger
referencing it fails validation.

VersionPolicy.description:
The set of versions a node may declare for a provider at a scope.

`AnyPublished` (the default when unset) permits every catalogued version —
the trust boundary is the catalog. `List`/`Range` let an org curate. The
version a node *runs* is always an exact `ProviderVersion`; a `Range` only
governs which exact versions are declarable, so reproducibility holds (no
floating run-time versions).

VersionSource.description:
Where a step's provider version came from: `node` (the step pins it), `group_default` (the
default version set for the repository or a group above it) or `track_latest` (the latest
published version when the run started).

ViolationCode.description:
Why steps failed the provider checks made when a run starts. Each code is stable: match on the
code, never on the message.

VisibilityChangePreview.description: What changing this repository's visibility would make readable, or leave readable, before anything changes. Nothing was changed.

bound_forks.description:
When the change widens the audience: the forks bound to this repository. They stay private
and bound, and nothing of theirs becomes readable.

branches_becoming_readable.description:
When the change widens the audience: the branches that become readable to it, at most a
thousand together with the tags.

forks_staying_more_visible.description:
When the change narrows the audience: forks of this repository in its organization that
stay more visible than it will be.

other_organization_forks.description:
When the change narrows the audience: how many forks in other organizations stay more
visible than it will be. Their names are their owners'.

refs_not_listed.description: How many more branches and tags become readable than are listed.

retained_proposals.description:
When the change widens the audience: the merge requests from forks whose kept versions
become readable, those closed without merging first.

tags_becoming_readable.description: When the change widens the audience: the tags that become readable to it.

WarningCode.description:
An advisory about a step's provider version that does not stop the run:
`provider_version_deprecated` (the version still runs but is discouraged) or
`provider_version_sunset_pending` (the version is sunset and its grace period is running out).

Widget.description:
A capability a type opts into. It governs which fields the API accepts and which
sub-resources exist — which is what lets one entity serve eight types without
eight sets of validation.

A request that sets a field whose widget the type does not declare is refused with a `400`,
never silently ignored.

Wiki.description: A scope's wiki, as its settings.

clone_url.description:
Where this wiki can be cloned from. Absent when the wiki has no clone URL of its own, as for
a wiki that reads its pages from a repository.

default_page.description: The page served at the wiki's root.

enabled.description:
Whether the wiki is on. **A disabled wiki is `false` here, never a `404`**: whether a wiki
exists is not a secret, and only its contents are.

oneOf.description: The commit the index was last built from. Absent until the first sync.

page_count.description: How many pages the wiki has.

oneOf.description: The directory a `in_repo` wiki reads from. Absent for a `dedicated` one.

upload_url.description: Where to `PUT` the bytes. Short-lived, and returned only when the attachment is created.

WikiBacklink.description: A page that references this one, from `spec_refs`.

WikiFormat.description: The markup a page is written in, decided by its file extension.

WikiHeading.description: One heading in a page's table of contents.

anchor.description: The GitHub-compatible slug, which is what a link into the page uses.

parent_ordinal.description: The enclosing heading's ordinal, so a client can rebuild the tree without a second read.

WikiPage.description: One page's identity and address. The tree is a list of these.

doc_id.description: Stable identity. **Unchanged by a rename**, which is what lets every backlink survive one.

content.description: The markup, read from git at the wiki's head.

oneOf.description:
The commit the content was read at — the `ETag` validator.

The *commit* and not the blob, because a wiki save's precondition is the wiki's head
(`expected_head_sha`), and the validator a reader holds is the one a later save presents.
Weaker than a per-page validator (any edit anywhere in the wiki moves it) and honest, which
is the trade worth making for a cache tag.

Set when a redirect resolved this request, so the client can update its address bar and say
*this page moved* rather than silently showing something else.

toc.description:
From `spec_blocks`. Empty until the projection has caught up, which is a different thing
from the page having no headings and is why the page itself is never sourced from there.

WikiPageDetail.description:
A page, its content, and everything the index knows about it — the one read that composes git
and PostgreSQL.

WikiRevision.description: One commit in a page's history.

WikiSource.description: Where a wiki's pages come from.

WorkItemType.description:
The kind of work item. The type decides where an item may live (a group or a repository), which
types it may have as children, and which fields it accepts.

WorkingHours.description:
When an agent works, in the organization's time zone: a ritual runs with the participants who
are at work when it starts, and a facilitator outside its hours fails the run.

end.description: When its day ends; earlier than `start` means the day runs past midnight.

bearer_auth.description: Cognito ID token, or a gitmoap access token (personal `gmp_…` / service-account `gms_…`).

get.description:
The API URL, the git endpoint, the sign-in settings and where client downloads live — what the
`gitmoap` CLI and the git remote helper read so they carry only the service's host. Anyone may
read it, without signing in; clients cache it for a day, and a shared cache may hold it for
five minutes.

501.description: This deployment does not publish a client configuration

get.summary: The settings the command-line tools read to reach Gitmoap.

get.description:
The public keys (RFC 7517) that verify the signature on an identity token gitmoap issued to a
pipeline run, matched by the token's key id. Anyone may read it, without signing in, and it may
be cached for five minutes.

501.description: The OIDC issuer is not configured on this deployment

get.summary: JSON Web Key Set publishing the public half of the OIDC signing key(s).

get.description:
The authorization server metadata document (RFC 8414) an app reads to find where to send people
and where to exchange codes: the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256), refresh tokens,
public clients identified by a client ID metadata document, and every scope and bundle that can
be asked for. Anyone may read it, without signing in.

501.description: The authorization server is not configured on this deployment

get.summary: Metadata for this deployment's OAuth authorization server

get.description:
The protected resource metadata document (RFC 9728) for this deployment's MCP service: its
address, the authorization server that issues access to it, that access tokens travel in the
`Authorization` header, and the scopes it understands. Anyone may read it, without signing in.

200.description: Protected resource metadata for the MCP service

501.description: The authorization server is not configured on this deployment

get.summary: Which authorization server protects the MCP service, and what it can grant

get.description:
The OpenID Connect discovery document for the identity tokens gitmoap issues to pipeline runs,
so a cloud provider can register gitmoap as an identity provider and trust those tokens: the
issuer, where its signing keys are published, RS256 signatures and the claims a token carries.
Anyone may read it, without signing in, and it may be cached for five minutes.

501.description: The OIDC issuer is not configured on this deployment

get.summary: OIDC Discovery document for the gitmoap issuer.

delete.description:
Anyone can give up their own direct grant. Revoking someone else's needs the right to manage
access at the grant's group or repository, and the caller must hold the role being taken away.
The organization's last Owner cannot be removed, and a service account's own level is changed
on the service account, not here. With `dry_run=true` the answer says who would lose what, and
nothing changes.

**Required scope:** `access:manage`

parameters.description: Say who would lose what, and change nothing
parameters.name: dry_run

200.description: A preview: who would lose what. Nothing was changed

400.description: Bad request — a path parameter is not a well-formed value of its type

401.description: Authentication required

403.description: The caller cannot revoke this grant

409.description: The organization would be left without an Owner, or this is a service account's own level

delete.summary: Revoke a grant, or give up your own.

patch.description:
Send at least one of the three; an expiry must be in the future and at most a year away.
Callers who can manage access at the grant's group or repository may call it, and must hold
both the role it has and any role it is given. A grant whose access the caller cannot see is
not found. A service account's own level is changed on the service account, not here. With
`dry_run=true` the answer says what a change of role would do, and nothing changes.

**Required scope:** `access:manage`

parameters.description: Say what would change, and change nothing
parameters.name: dry_run

200.description: The grant as it now stands, or a preview

400.description: Invalid request

401.description: Authentication required

403.description: The caller cannot change this grant

409.description: This is a service account's own level — change it on the service account

422.description: A service account cannot hold this role here

patch.summary: Change a grant's role, expiry or reason.

delete.description:
Only the owners of the group or repository the limit was set on may remove it; a limit on a
group or repository whose access the caller cannot see is not found. With `dry_run=true` the
answer says who would stop being narrowed, and nothing changes.

**Required scope:** `access:administer`

parameters.description: Say who would stop being narrowed, and change nothing

400.description: Invalid limit id or dry_run value

401.description: Authentication required

403.description: Only the owners of the scope can remove its limits

409.description: The request conflicts with the resource's current state; `reason` says how
